text: For which uncountable cardinals κ does every vacillating poset P of size κ, with no infinite antichain, admit a chain meeting every class of some antichain partition of P? Vacillating means no saturated chain, or its reverse, is a lexicographic sum of countably many infinite chains having no infinite increasing sequence. A chain is saturated if no outside element can be inserted between two of its elements while preserving a chain.

author: Tobias Boege

author: Tobias Boege

author: Tobias Boege; Janneke H. Bolt; Milan Studený

source_title: Algebraic sparse factor analysis

author: Mathias Drton; Alexandros Grosdos; İrem Portakal; Nils Sturma
source_title: Algebraic sparse factor analysis
text: Put A_i=ch(h_i). Define I_i as the kernel of σ_uv↦t_ut_v for u,v∈A_i and σ_uv↦0 otherwise. Does some term order ≺ satisfy in_≺(I_1*I_2)=in_≺(I_1)*in_≺(I_2)? The join * is the vanishing ideal of the Zariski closure of sums from the two varieties; in_≺ denotes the leading-monomial ideal.

author: Tobias Boege
source_title: On the Intersection and Composition properties of conditional independence

text: Characterize the seven-dimensional entropy vectors of discrete triples (A,X,Y) with finite entropies satisfying I(A;X)=I(A;Y)=0, without requiring any of A,X,Y to be a function of the other two.

source_title: On the Relationship Between Probabilistic Circuits and Determinantal Point Processes

author: Denis Deratani Mauá; Cassio P. de Campos; Alessio Benavoli; Alessandro Antonucci
source_title: Probabilistic Inference in Credal Networks: New Complexity Results

author: Denis Deratani Mauá; Cassio P. de Campos; Alessio Benavoli; Alessandro Antonucci
source_title: Probabilistic Inference in Credal Networks: New Complexity Results
text: What is the exact complexity under strong independence for imprecise HMMs when the query can precede observations? Is polynomial-time smoothing possible?

title: Lifting a self-adhesive CI pattern to a self-adhesive polymatroid
author: Tobias Boege
source_title: Selfadhesivity in Gaussian conditional independence structures

author: Kuikui Liu

author: Kuikui Liu
source_title: Spectral Independence: A New Tool to Analyze Markov Chains
text: For every graph of maximum degree Δ and every q≥Δ+2, does single-vertex heat-bath Glauber dynamics on proper q-colorings mix in polynomial time? In the boundary regime q≥Δ+1, does an FPRAS for the number of proper colorings exist?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Random-cluster Glauber mixing for nonintegral cluster weights
author: Kuikui Liu
source_title: Spectral Independence: A New Tool to Analyze Markov Chains
text: For every fixed 1<q<2 and 0<p<1, does edge heat-bath Glauber dynamics mix in polynomial time on every finite undirected multigraph for μ(F)∝q^{k(F)}p^{|F|}(1−p)^{|E∖F|}, where k(F) counts components of (V,F)?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: An FPRAS for perfect-matching normalizers on general graphs
author: Kuikui Liu
source_title: Spectral Independence: A New Tool to Analyze Markov Chains
text: Does counting perfect matchings in arbitrary finite undirected graphs on an even number of vertices admit an FPRAS?

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Computing globally sufficient decision information under nondegeneracy
author: Yuhan Ye; Saurabh Amin; Asuman Özdağlar
source_title: Learning Decision-Sufficient Representations for Linear Optimization
text: When each vertex has exactly m positive coordinates, what is the complexity of computing d* and a minimum global sufficient dataset? Do the general NP-/coNP-hardness results survive this nondegeneracy promise?

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Adaptive query complexity of pointwise decision sufficiency
author: Yuhan Ye; Saurabh Amin; Asuman Özdağlar
source_title: Learning Decision-Sufficient Representations for Linear Optimization
text: Allow successive exact queries q_tᵀc to depend on earlier answers. What is the minimum worst-case query count until the consistent cost fiber lies in one action’s optimality region? When is it below d*? This is deployment-time branching, not offline construction of one fixed dataset.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Sharp intermediate budgets for weighted decision-data compression
author: Steve Hanneke; Shay Moran; Alexander Shlimovich; Amir Yehudayoff
source_title: Open Problem: Data Selection for Regression Tasks
location: Questions 2 and 4; current refinement: arXiv:2608.30254v2, §6–7 and Conjecture 6.5; arXiv:2608.28007, Conjecture 7.2.
text: For finite $D\subset\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m$, let $L_D(W)=|D|^{-1}\sum_{(x,y)\in D}\|Wx-y\|_2^2$ and $L_D^*=\min_W L_D(W)>0$. Let $A^*$ return the minimum-Frobenius-norm weighted least-squares minimizer. Define $F_w(d,m,n)=\sup_D\inf_{S\subset D,\,|S|\le n,\,w\in\Delta(S)}L_D(A^*(\sum_{z\in S}w_z\ell_z))/L_D^*$. Determine the remaining intermediate profile, especially $d<n<(m+1)d-1$ for $m\ge2$, excluding resolved endpoint and low-dimensional cells. The smallest reported vector conjectures are $F_w(2,2,3)=13/8$ and $F_w(2,2,4)=5/4$; these form one profile question.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Gap-free square-root regret for unknown binary causal graphs
author: Shi Feng; Neng Xiong; Wei Chen
source_title: Combinatorial Causal Bandits without Graph Skeleton
text: In an unknown fully observed DAG with n binary nonreward variables and binary reward Y, let X₁≡1 and P(X=1|pa(X))=θ_Xᵀpa(X)+ε_X, with unknown nonnegative θ_X and centered sub-Gaussian noise restricted to keep every probability in [0,1]. Each round intervenes from a fixed combinatorial menu containing the null and all atomic interventions, and observes all variables. Can expected regret against the best intervention be poly(n)√T polylog(T), without a positive lower bound on nonzero coefficients? Oracle access is allowed to joint maximization of expected intervened reward over actions and parameters in current confidence ellipsoids; implementing that oracle is not charged.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: The frontier between identifying causes and earning reward
author: Mohammad Shahverdikondori; Jalal Etesami; Negar Kiyavash
source_title: Graph Learning is Suboptimal in Causal Bandits
location: §7 Discussion and Future Directions; Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2.
text: In the finite, causally sufficient unknown-graph bandit model of Shahverdikondori–Etesami–Kiyavash, actions set at most m of n ℓ-valued variables and reveal the post-intervention variables and reward. Let R_T(π,E′) be worst-case cumulative regret and δ_T(π,d,E′)=sup_{V∈E′}Pr_V{d(H_T)≠Pa_V(Y)}. Characterize the achievable pairs (R_T,δ_T), and the conditions on identifiable subclasses E′ under which parent identification and minimax regret can be optimized together. The source’s demonstrated conflict on a hard subclass is known; the requested object is its unresolved quantitative frontier, not the claim that a conflict exists.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Classifying regret with continuous partial-observation actions
author: Johannes Kirschner; Tor Lattimore; Andreas Krause
source_title: Linear Partial Monitoring for Sequential Decision Making: Algorithms, Regret Bounds and Applications
text: Consider linear partial monitoring with known compact action set A, bounded reward features φ_a∈R^d, continuous bounded observation maps M_a, a known bounded convex parameter set Θ, and unknown θ∈Θ. Playing a yields y=M_aθ+ε with conditionally mean-zero sub-Gaussian noise, while its unobserved mean reward is φ_a^Tθ. Characterize the minimax order of inf_π sup_θ EΣ_{t≤T}(max_a φ_a^Tθ−φ_{a_t}^Tθ) for continuous A in terms of observability and action geometry. The four-regime finite-action classification is established and is not the question.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: A budget conversion that preserves every good-enough decision guarantee
author: Kapilan Balagopalan; Yinan Li; Yao Zhao; Tuan Nguyen; Anton Daitche; Houssam Nassif; Kwang-Sung Jun
source_title: Fixed Budget is No Harder Than Fixed Confidence in Best-Arm Identification up to Logarithmic Factors
location: §7 Conclusion, second direction; §2–3 for strong/weak fixed-confidence definitions.
text: Given a tolerance-indexed fixed-confidence family A(ε,δ) for a specified structured stochastic-bandit class, with Pr{μ*−μ_ĩ>ε}≤δ and an explicit envelope Pr_ν{τ>N(ν,ε,δ)}≤δ on every instance ν, can it be converted into one fixed-budget procedure independent of ε that simultaneously retains these ε-good-arm guarantees, with only logarithmic budget overhead relative to N? Determine sufficient stopping-tail conditions and the sharp conversion. Ties and multiple acceptable answers are allowed; the proved unique-exact-best-arm conversion is excluded.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Can margin ambiguity be completed without an unbounded VC cost?
author: Noga Alon; Steve Hanneke; Ron Holzman; Shay Moran
source_title: A Theory of PAC Learnability of Partial Concept Classes
location: §III-A, Question 21; current status in Chornomaz–Moran–Waknine 2025 §4.1 and Frick et al. 2026 §7.
text: For a Hilbert space V, let H_{R,γ} be the partial binary concepts h:V→{0,1,?} whose every finite supported labeled sample lies in a ball of radius R and has the two labeled convex hulls separated by at least 2γ. Does there exist, uniformly over dim V, a total binary class H̄ extending every h∈H_{R,γ} and having VC dimension bounded only by R and γ? Ask only the VC part: the parallel bounded-Littlestone-disambiguation question has a negative solution. Nontrivial margin parameters are intended.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Iterated-logarithm stopping boundaries for nonparametric best-arm GLRs
author: Marc Jourdan
source_title: Solving Pure Exploration Problems with the Top Two Approach
text:
For K independently sampled arms with laws on known [0,B], let $\widehat
u_{t,a}$ and $N_{t,a}$ be empirical laws and adaptive counts; m denotes a law’s mean. Define $Z_t(i)=\inf_{\kappa\in\mathcal P([0,B])^K:\,\exists j
e i,\,m(\kappa_j)\ge m(\kappa_i)}\sum_aN_{t,a}D_{m KL}(\widehat
u_{t,a}\|\kappa_a)$. Stop when $\max_iZ_t(i)>c(t,\delta)$, recommending a maximizer. Under every adaptive sampling rule, can wrong-stopping probability be ≤δ with $c(t,\delta)=O(\log\log t)$ for fixed δ and $\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}c(t,\delta)/\log(1/\delta)=1$ for fixed t? This is the empirical-law GLR, not a generic confidence interval.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Structured forecast queries with correlated substitute information
author: Rafael Frongillo; Mary Monroe; Eric Neyman; Bo Waggoner
source_title: Robust forecast aggregation via additional queries
text: Let n Bayesian experts observe possibly overlapping correlated signals, with joint law D unknown to the aggregator and E[Y²]<∞. Write L_D(A)=E_D(A−Y)² and A*=E_D[Y|all signals], requiring Var_D(Y)−L_D(A*)>0. If S↦Var_D(E[Y|signals in S]) is submodular, determine the optimal worst-case normalized error (L_D(A)−L_D(A*))/(Var_D(Y)−L_D(A*)) under bounds on the three query complexities. Queries cannot adapt to realized replies.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Is decoder-only side information enough for the conditional-dependence exponent?
author: Han Wu; Shun Watanabe
source_title: Distributed Hypothesis Testing Against Dependence
location: §III-C, Theorems 3–4, equations (36)–(45), Corollary 1; introduction explicitly states remaining tightness question.
text: Under H0, (X,Y,Z) has finite-alphabet law P_XZ P_{Y|Z}; under H1 it has law Q_XYZ. A rate-R encoder observes X^n, while the tester observes the message and (Y^n,Z^n). Is the optimal type-II Stein exponent E(R) equal to the exponent Ẽ(R) when the encoder also receives Z^n? The latter is max_{P_{U|XZ}:I_P(U;X|Z)≤R} min_{P̃:P̃_UXZ=P_UXZ, P̃_UYZ=P_UYZ} D(P̃_UXYZ || P_{U|XZ}Q_XYZ), with |U|≤|X||Z|+1. General equality is open; Z=g(X) is already solved. Type-I error tends to zero, and all laws/code constraints are as in the source.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: A common garbling decoder for opposite-correlation binary models
author: Adway Girish; Robinson D. H. Cung; Emre Telatar
source_title: On the suboptimality of linear codes for binary distributed hypothesis testing
location: Conjecture 1; §2.1 Blackwell order, Theorems 1–2; §5 numerical evidence.
text: Let (X^n,Y^n) consist of n i.i.d. DSBS(p_h) pairs under hypothesis h∈{0,1}, with p_0≠p_1 and (p_0−1/2)(p_1−1/2)≤0. For every full-row-rank binary k×n matrix G, does observing the first k pairs (X^k,Y^k) Blackwell-dominate observing (GX^n,GY^n), all arithmetic modulo two? Equivalently, is there one stochastic channel from the truncated experiment to the linearly compressed experiment that reproduces its distribution under both hypotheses? The independence endpoints and p_1=1−p_0 are already proved; the unequal-magnitude opposite-sign case remains.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Feedback-graph regret when changing observations has a cost
author: Raman Arora; Teodor V. Marinov; Mehryar Mohri
source_title: Bandits with Feedback Graphs and Switching Costs
location: §5–6 for incomplete graph-dependent lower-bound program; current status: Cesari–Colomboni 2026 arXiv:2606.03851, abstract and §1–2.
text: For a fixed known finite directed feedback graph G, an oblivious adversary fixes losses ℓ_t∈[0,1]^K. Choosing i_t reveals ℓ_t(j) for edges i_t→j and incurs ℓ_t(i_t)+1{i_t≠i_{t−1}}. Characterize the minimax expected regret against the best fixed action as a function of G and T, including which observable graphs have √T versus T^(2/3) order (up to logarithms), and whether further regimes occur. Preserve whether self-loops exist. The two-action revealing/blind apple-tasting graph has Θ(√T) regret and must not be listed as an unresolved hard example.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Pathwise stopping bounds for conjugate exponential-family computations
author: Nicholas James Hay
source_title: Principles of Metalevel Control
location: §7.3 item 3, printed pp. 93–94; Theorem 4.8, p. 43; Example 4.4, pp. 41–42.
text: For one uncertain action sampled at cost d>0 against a known outside option u, characterize which exponential-family observation laws and conjugate priors admit a pathwise O(1/d) bound on the optimal number of computations, uniform over histories. Can a threshold on conjugate posterior weight establish it? The source asks for the necessary additional conditions.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Exact complexity of adaptive action evaluation
author: Vincent Conitzer; Tuomas Sandholm
source_title: Definition and Complexity of Some Basic Metareasoning Problems
location: Definition 4 and §3.3, pp. 3–4; final paragraph before §4.
text: Is ACTION-EVALUATION PSPACE-complete for explicitly tabulated independent evaluation trees? Edge probabilities and leaf utilities are rational; internal steps have nonnegative integer costs. Given budget N, decide whether an adaptive expected-utility-optimal policy can begin by advancing tree 1, with pathwise cost at most N and terminal reward the largest conditional expected leaf utility.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: A proof-search procedure competitive with every proof system
author: Jan Krajíček; Pavel Pudlák
source_title: Propositional proof systems, the consistency of first order theories and the complexity of computations
location: Krajíček–Pudlák1989 §2, especially Theorem 2.1; proof-search formulation in Krajíček2021 Definitions 1.1,2.1 and Theorem 2.4.
text: Does a pair (A,P) exist such that, for every pair (B,Q), constants c,C depending only on (B,Q) satisfy time_A(τ)≤C(time_B(τ)+1)^c for every tautology τ? Equivalently, does a p-optimal propositional proof system exist?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Does lack of an optimal proof calculus admit a computable improvement operator?
author: Erfan Khaniki
source_title: Jump Operators, Interactive Proofs and Proof Complexity Generators
location: Problem 10, printed p. 591; definitions of jump operators and Conjectures 3.1,5.1; Egidy2026 Q1.
text: In the unrelativized Cook–Reckhow model for TAUT, does nonexistence of a length-optimal proof system imply existence of a total recursive jump operator J? Here P simulates Q when a polynomially length-bounded translation maps every Q-proof to a P-proof of the same tautology, and J must map each code of a proof system P to a proof system J(P) that P does not simulate. No behavior is required on codes that are not proof systems.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Exact deterministic memory exponent for binary hypothesis testing
author: Tomer Berg; Ofer Shayevitz; Or Ordentlich
source_title: Binary Hypothesis Testing with Deterministic Finite-Memory Decision Rules
text: Fix $0<q<p<1$ and equal priors for iid Bernoulli$(p)$ versus Bernoulli$(q)$ observations. A deterministic time-invariant $S$-state tester has $M_0=s$, $M_t=f(M_{t-1},X_t)$ and decision $d(M_t)$. Let $e_S$ minimize $\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^n\Pr\{d(M_t)\ne H\}$ over such testers and initial states. Determine the sharp exponential decay with $S$, including whether the liminf and limsup of $-S^{-1}\log e_S$ coincide, throughout the interior parameter regime.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Joint sample and memory complexity of Bernoulli bias estimation
author: Tomer Berg; Or Ordentlich; Ofer Shayevitz
source_title: Statistical Inference with Limited Memory: A Survey
location: §10 final statistical-inference paragraph (printed pp. 42–43); §§2.3,3 define finite-sample risk and machine classes.
text: For iid Bern(θ), θ∈[0,1], determine inf_{f,g,s0} sup_θ Eθ[(g(Mn)−θ)²] jointly in n,S, where M0=s0∈[S], Mt=f(Mt−1,Xt), and f,g are fixed deterministic maps. The S states must include any clock. The source also asks the randomized-transition version; the established infinite-time-average Θ(1/S) result is not a finite-sample answer.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Finite-state minimax risk in Gaussian linear regression
author: Tomer Berg; Or Ordentlich; Ofer Shayevitz
source_title: Statistical Inference with Limited Memory: A Survey
text: For a given bounded parameter set Θ⊂R^d, Xi iid∼N(0,I_d), and independent Vi iid∼N(0,σ²), let Yi=θᵀXi+Vi with θ∈Θ. Determine the minimax risk inf_{K,g,s0} sup_{θ∈Θ} Eθ||g(Mn)−θ||² as a function of n,S,d,σ² and Θ, where M0=s0∈[S], K(·|Mt−1,Xt,Yt) is one fixed measurable randomized transition kernel on [S], and g:[S]→R^d is fixed. The kernel and readout may be designed for n but cannot access a free time counter.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Sharp state complexity of streaming entropy estimation
author: Tomer Berg; Or Ordentlich; Ofer Shayevitz
source_title: Memory Complexity of Estimating Entropy and Mutual Information
location: §VII Conclusions and Open Problems, pp. 22–23; §I definition(3), Theorems 1–2.
text: In the finite-state entropy-estimation model, for fixed constants 10^{-5}<ε<1/(4 ln2) and 0<δ<1/2, what is the sharp dependence of S*(n,ε,δ) on alphabet size n? In particular, is a superlinear polylogarithmic factor unavoidable, or can the O(n(log n)^4) upper bound be reduced to O(n) states? The existing lower bound is Ω(n).

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Best universal computation budget schedule using one random bit
author: Spyros Angelopoulos; Bertrand Simon
source_title: Learning-Augmented Online Bidding in Stochastic Settings
location: §6 Conclusion, final question; definition(1), §1; §4.1 for non-prediction use.
text: For online bidding without advice, a target u≥1 is fixed before the algorithm’s randomness. The algorithm submits increasing positive budgets x0,x1,… until the first xi≥u and pays Σ_{j≤i}xj. What is inf_A sup_{u≥1} E[cost_A(u)]/u when A may use only one unbiased random bit in total, equivalently choosing equally between two deterministic bidding sequences?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: A fully polynomial additive approximation for calibration distance
author: Mingda Qiao
source_title: Computational and Statistical Hardness of Calibration Distance
text: Given rational D,f and ε>0, can CD_D(f) be approximated additively within ε in time polynomial in input bit length and 1/ε?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Sharp two-sided sample complexity of calibration distance
author: Mingda Qiao
source_title: Computational and Statistical Hardness of Calibration Distance
location: Theorems 3–4; §4, “Finer-grained results for estimation and testing”.
text: With iid D samples and f-query access, what is the minimax sample count for additive-ε estimation of CD_D(f) with success ≥0.99? Close Ω(√N/ε) versus O(N/ε²).

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The tolerant-testing landscape for calibration distance
author: Mingda Qiao
source_title: Computational and Statistical Hardness of Calibration Distance
text: With iid D samples and f-query access, determine the constant-success sample complexity of distinguishing CD_D(f)≤ε₁ from CD_D(f)≥ε₂, 0<ε₁<ε₂; especially between ε₁,ε₂=Θ(ε) and ε₁=ε, ε₂≫√ε.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Minimax sequential distance from calibration
author: Mingda Qiao; Letian Zheng
source_title: On the Distance from Calibration in Sequential Prediction
text: In binary sequential prediction, determine inf_A sup_B E[CD_T(Y,P)], where CD_T=min_{q∈[0,1]^T: Σ_{t:q_t=v}(Y_t−v)=0 for every v} Σ_t|P_t−q_t|. At each t, A predicts before observing Y_t, and a non-prescient adaptive adversary may use the history but not A’s current sampled prediction. Close the gap Ω(T^{1/3}) versus O(√T).

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The optimal binary online ECE exponent
author: Yuval Dagan; Constantinos Daskalakis; Maxwell Fishelson; Noah Golowich; Robert Kleinberg; Princewill Okoroafor
source_title: Breaking the T^{2/3} Barrier for Sequential Calibration
location: Introduction, fundamental rate question; arXiv v4, 16 September 2026.
text: Determine the minimax order of E[Σ_{p∈[0,1]} |Σ_{t:P_t=p}(Y_t−p)|] for T rounds of randomized binary forecasting against non-prescient adaptive outcomes. The best bounds retained in the September 2026 revision are Ω(T^{0.54389}) and O(T^{2/3−c}) for a universal c>0. Is there a matching exponent or a sharper asymptotic characterization?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: One forecaster optimal for every proper loss
author: Rafael Frongillo; Haipeng Luo; Nishant A. Mehta; Jon Schneider
source_title: Toward Simultaneously Optimal Regret in U-Calibration
text: For fixed K and asymptotic T, does one online forecasting algorithm, not told the downstream proper loss ℓ, achieve for every ℓ its individual minimax regret rate, up to constants or logarithmic factors in T, allowing constants to depend on K and ℓ? The 2026 result achieves √T-type regret for all bounded proper losses and log T for smooth ones, but leaves the full simultaneous-optimality question open.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Sharp outcome-dimension dependence with smooth-loss adaptivity
author: Rafael Frongillo; Haipeng Luo; Nishant A. Mehta; Jon Schneider
source_title: Toward Simultaneously Optimal Regret in U-Calibration
text: Can a single proper forecaster attain R_ℓ=~O(√(KT)) for every bounded proper loss while retaining logarithmic-in-T regret for every bounded β-smooth proper loss? The current simultaneous algorithm gives ~O(K^{5/4}√T) in the general class and O(β log T+β√K log K) for the smooth class; remove the extra dimension dependence without losing adaptivity.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Sharp abstention–mistake tradeoff under oblivious insertions
author: Jialin Yu; Moïse Blanchard
source_title: Distribution-Free Sequential Prediction with Abstentions
text: For every finite-VC class F, determine the optimal worst-case tradeoff between expected mistakes E[M] and expected clean-input abstentions E[A] when corruption times and inserted instances are fixed in advance. The known guarantee M=O(T^{4a}), E[A]=~O(d²T^{1−a}), 0≤a≤1/4, is separated from the lower-bound tradeoff E[M]=Ω(T^a) or E[A]=Ω(T^{1−a}). Close the gap for general d=VC(F).

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Distribution-free abstention against adaptive corruptions for every VC class
author: Jialin Yu; Moïse Blanchard
source_title: Distribution-Free Sequential Prediction with Abstentions
location: §6, boxed open question; Definition 6 for the currently required reduction dimension.
text: Does every finite-VC class admit E[M],E[A]≤poly(d)T^{1−Ω(1)}, d=VC(F), when insertion times and inputs can depend on the entire past, and μ is unknown? The current additional finite-reduction-dimension assumption is not allowed.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Is Lipschitzness necessary for fast online recalibration?
author: Lunjia Hu; Kevin Tian; Chutong Yang
source_title: Optimal Recalibration of an Online Predictor
text: In the hinted binary online game, nature selects (q_t,y_t) adaptively from past history, reveals q_t, and then the forecaster outputs p_t before y_t is revealed. Characterize the proper losses ℓ for which one can ensure E[K₁(p,y)]≤ε and E[T^{-1}Σ_t(ℓ(p_t,y_t)−ℓ(q_t,y_t))]≤ε² in Θ(ε^{-3}) rounds. Is Lipschitzness necessary, and in particular what happens for unbounded log loss when comparator loss is finite (avoiding infinity subtraction)?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Optimal calibration rates at intermediate nonstationarity
author: Junyan Liu; Haipeng Luo; Lillian J. Ratliff
source_title: Adaptive Calibration in Non-Stationary Environments
location: §2 definitions; §6 second future direction; v2, 22 May 2026.
text: For sequential Bernoulli outcomes with unknown mean sequence q_1:T, determine the minimax expected calibration error as a function of T, C=min_qΣ_t|q_t−q|, and K=1+Σ_{t<T}1{q_t≠q_{t+1}}. In particular, are the adaptive upper bounds ~O(min{√T+(TC)^{1/3},√(KT)}) for cumulative l1 calibration and ~O(min{(1+C)^{1/3},K}) for cumulative squared calibration optimal in intermediate regimes?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Sharp high-dimensional calibration round complexity
author: Binghui Peng
source_title: High dimensional online calibration in polynomial time
location: §1.1 immediately after Theorems 1.1–1.2; current lower-bound comparison: Fishelson et al. Theorem 4.3.
text: For outcomes Y_t∈{e_1,…,e_d} and randomized forecasts P_t∈Δ_d, determine the minimax number T(d,ε) of rounds needed to ensure E[Σ_{p∈Δ_d}||Σ_{t:P_t=p}(Y_t−p)||₁]≤εT against non-prescient adversaries. Known strategies require d^{~O(1/ε²)} rounds. Determine the sharp joint dependence on dimension and accuracy; polynomial-in-d feasibility at fixed ε is already established.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Efficient realized KL-calibration with high probability
author: Haipeng Luo; Spandan Senapati; Vatsal Sharan
source_title: Simultaneous Swap Regret Minimization via KL-Calibration
text: Can an explicit computationally efficient forecaster guarantee ~O(T^{1/3}) realized KL-calibration, equivalently log-loss swap regret, with probability at least 1−δ against non-prescient adaptive binary outcomes? Here KLCal=Σ_p n_p KL(Ber(ȳ_p)||Ber(p)), and swap regret compares realized p_t with all hindsight replacements σ(p_t). Existing explicit bounds are for pseudo KL-calibration; the comparable realized KL guarantee is nonconstructive.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Optimal prediction-set-complexity dependence of conditional coverage error
author: Jiadong Liang; Zhimei Ren; Yuxin Chen
source_title: Optimal training-conditional regret for online conformal prediction
location: §4.3, Proposition 4.3 and “Implications beyond the online setting” (v2 numbering).
text: For i.i.d. training data of size n from any distribution D on X×R admitting a density, and independent randomization U, an algorithm outputs Ĉ(x), a union of at most K intervals. Determine inf_π sup_D E|P_D{Y∈Ĉ(X) | training data,U}−(1−α)| for fixed α∈(0,1/2], sharply in K and n. The known lower bound is ~Ω(min{K^{-1/2},n^{-1/2}}).

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The minimax accuracy of an adaptively reused leaderboard
author: Moritz Hardt
source_title: Climbing a shaky ladder: Better adaptive risk estimation
text: A mechanism holds n i.i.d. observations from unknown D. An analyst adaptively submits k models f_t using previous releases R_1,…,R_{t−1}; loss is in [0,1]. Can it ensure max_{t≤k}|R_t−min_{i≤t}E_D ℓ(f_i,Z)|=~O(n^{-1/2}) with high probability and only polylogarithmic dependence on k? Determine the optimal rate between the known ~O(n^{-2/5}) upper bound and Ω(√(log k/n)) lower bound.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Exact pivotal e-values for infinite composite hypotheses
author: Zhenyuan Zhang; Aaditya Ramdas; Ruodu Wang
source_title: On the existence of powerful p-values and e-values for composite hypotheses
text: Let P and Q be possibly infinite classes of probability laws dominated by a common R, jointly atomless: under a dominating measure there is a continuous randomizer independent of all density ratios. Is there a nonnegative statistic E with the same null distribution for every P∈P, E_P E=1, and inf_{Q∈Q}E_Q log E>0 if and only if 0∉cl_TV(Span(P)+Conv(Q))?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: When horizonwise reverse projections form an e-process
author: Aaditya Ramdas; Peter Grünwald; Vladimir Vovk; Glenn Shafer
source_title: Game-Theoretic Statistics and Safe Anytime-Valid Inference
text: Let Q and composite null P be laws on a filtered observation space, with finite-horizon densities. At each t, assume inf_W D(Q_t||P_{W,t})<∞ over probability mixtures W of null laws. Let P_t* be the generalized reverse information projection of §3.3.2, possibly a subprobability measure, and choose one adapted version E_t=q_t/p_t* on the specified filtration. Characterize when sup_{P∈P}E_P[E_τ]≤1 for every stopping time τ, so that (E_t) is an e-process rather than merely a sequence of fixed-time e-variables.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Online versus adaptive private statistical-query release
author: Mark Bun; Thomas Steinke; Jonathan Ullman
source_title: Make Up Your Mind: The Price of Online Queries in Differential Privacy
text: For a fixed dataset x∈X^n and a fixed family Q of predicates φ:X→{0,1}, a query asks n^{-1}Σ_iφ(x_i). Are the sample complexities under (ε,δ)-differential privacy equivalent in their achievable query/accuracy tradeoffs, when queries arrive online but are fixed in advance versus when each query can depend on earlier answers? Or does some family Q separate these models for fixed nontrivial accuracy and success probability?

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Small-multiplier BH control under negative Gaussian dependence
author: Ziyu Chi; Aaditya Ramdas; Ruodu Wang
source_title: Multiple testing under negative dependence
location: §7 p. 21, first open problem; equation (26) p. 9; Gaussian dependence §3.3.
text: Let K p-values have a Gaussian copula with all off-diagonal latent correlations nonpositive; each of the K₀ true-null p-values is super-uniform. Apply BH at level 0<α<1: R=max({r:P_(r)≤αr/K}∪{0}), and let V count rejected true nulls. Is E[V/(R∨1)]≤(K₀/K)s(α) for every such joint law, where s(α)=min{α+2α²+(9/2)α³+(eα)⁴/[√(8π)(1−eα)₊],1}, with 1/0=∞?

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Simes validity for arbitrary correlated centered Gaussian two-sided tests
author: Ziyu Chi; Aaditya Ramdas; Ruodu Wang
source_title: Multiple testing under negative dependence
location: Remark 11 p. 11, referring to Finner–Roters–Strassburger, On the Simes test under dependence, §7.
text: For every K≥1, correlation matrix Σ and Y∼N_K(0,Σ), put P_i=2Φ(−|Y_i|) and S=min_{1≤r≤K} KP_(r)/r. Does Pr(S≤α)≤α hold for every α∈(0,1)? All coordinates are null; Σ may contain correlations of either sign.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Worst-case BH inflation beyond one-common-factor Gaussian dependence
author: Edgar Dobriban
source_title: The Benjamini–Hochberg Procedure Can Fail to Control the FDR for Correlated Two-Sided Gaussian Tests
location: Dobriban §8; Lei arXiv:2607.14812v3, Theorem 2.1, Theorem 4.2 and §5.
text: For X∼N_m(μ,Σ), Σ positive semidefinite with unit diagonal, with Φ the standard-normal CDF, use p_i=2Φ(−|X_i|), nulls μ_i=0, and BH level q. Let R=max({r:p_(r)≤qr/m}∪{0}) and V count rejected true nulls. Determine the sharp asymptotic order as q↓0 of B(q)=sup_{m,μ,Σ} E[V/(R∨1)]. In particular, does the Θ(q√log(1/q)) order reported by Lihua Lei within the one-common-factor class extend to arbitrary Gaussian correlation matrices, or can unrestricted covariance yield larger-order inflation?

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Instance-dependent samples for a noisy matrix-game equilibrium
author: Arnab Maiti
source_title: Open Problem: Optimal Instance-Dependent Sample Complexity for finding Nash Equilibrium in Two Player Zero-Sum Matrix games
location: §2, named Open Problem, pp. 6231–6232; §3 partial progress.
text: An unknown finite two-player zero-sum game has payoff matrix A∈R^{n×m}. The learner may adaptively sample any entry and observes A_ij plus zero-mean 1-subgaussian noise. Characterize, up to logarithmic factors, the optimal instance-dependent sample complexity of outputting an ε-Nash pair with probability ≥1−δ, ideally in the form Θ(H₁(A,ε)log(1/δ)+H₂(A,ε)). Each player must gain at most ε by any unilateral deviation. Arbitrary rectangular games and mixed or nonunique equilibria remain in scope; the solved strict-pure-equilibrium and n×2 special cases do not settle this question.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Constant total regret of optimistic fictitious play
author: John Lazarsfeld; Georgios Piliouras; Ryann Sim; Stratis Skoulakis
source_title: Optimism Without Regularization: Constant Regret in Zero-Sum Games
text: For every finite zero-sum matrix A, does simultaneous optimistic fictitious play have total external regret bounded by a constant depending on A and initialization but not T? With arbitrary initial mixed x₀,y₀, the updates select pure maximizers x_{t+1}∈argmax_x xᵀA(Σ_{k=0}^t y_k+y_t) and y_{t+1}∈argmin_y (Σ_{k=0}^t x_k+x_t)ᵀAy. The target is max_x Σ_t xᵀAy_t−min_y Σ_t x_tᵀAy=O_A(1), including tie-breaking choices. This would give O_A(1/T) duality-gap convergence of average play; the paper proves only the 2×2 unique-interior-equilibrium case.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Approximate satisficing paths in general finite games
author: Bora Yongacoglu; Gürdal Arslan; Lacra Pavel; Serdar Yüksel
source_title: Paths to Equilibrium in Games
location: §4, Open questions and future directions; Definitions 1–5.
text: For every finite n-player general-sum game, n≥3, ε>0 and initial mixed profile, is there a finite path to ε-Nash equilibrium where every player already an ε-best responder retains its entire mixed strategy at the next step? Unsatisfied players may change freely. The ε=0 result is established.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Satisficing paths in multiplayer discounted Markov games
author: Bora Yongacoglu; Gürdal Arslan; Lacra Pavel; Serdar Yüksel
source_title: Paths to Equilibrium in Games
location: §4 second open question; Appendix C, Definitions 6–8 and final paragraph.
text: Does every finite-state/action discounted general-sum Markov game with n≥3 players and fixed γ∈(0,1) admit, from every stationary randomized profile, a finite path to stationary Markov-perfect Nash equilibrium, freezing each player whose policy is already a best response from every state? Other players may change freely.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Single-exponential optimization under signal leakage
author: Nika Haghtalab; Mingda Qiao; Kunhe Yang
source_title: Leakage-Robust Bayesian Persuasion
text: With two signals per receiver, can OPT be computed in 2^{O(n)} time, polynomial in numerical encoding and explicit leakage-law size?

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Signal-alphabet size versus leakage-robust utility
author: Nika Haghtalab; Mingda Qiao; Kunhe Yang
source_title: Leakage-Robust Bayesian Persuasion
location: §5, Direct vs indirect schemes; Appendix E.
text: What utility is attainable with q signals per receiver? Do two signals always give a constant-factor approximation, and does some finite f(n) suffice for exact optimality?

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Monotonicity for structured random signal leakage
author: Nika Haghtalab; Mingda Qiao; Kunhe Yang
source_title: Leakage-Robust Bayesian Persuasion
location: §2.2 leakage models; §5, Monotonicity of sender utility.
text: For direct signals, is OPT nonincreasing in k for k-star, k-clique and k-broadcast, and is OPT(broadcast)≤OPT(clique)≤OPT(star)? Respectively: k uniform senders reveal to one other uniform receiver; k uniform receivers share mutually; k uniform senders reveal to everyone.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: PTAS boundary for robust Stackelberg commitment
author: Jiarui Gan; Minbiao Han; Jibang Wu; Haifeng Xu
source_title: Robust Stackelberg Equilibria
text: Given a rational finite leader–follower game with payoffs in [0,1] and fixed δ>0, can the leader’s robust Stackelberg value be approximated additively to every fixed ε>0 in polynomial input time? For leader mixture x, define BR_δ(x)={j:u_f(x,j)>max_k u_f(x,k)−δ}; maximize min_{j∈BR_δ(x)}u_l(x,j). Preserve the strict inequality. Alternatively, prove constant-additive-error hardness that closes the gap between the known no-FPTAS result and QPTAS.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Sharp price of replacing ex-ante by ex-post information constraints
author: Yakov Babichenko; Inbal Talgam-Cohen; Konstantin Zabarnyi
source_title: Bayesian Persuasion under Ex Ante and Ex Post Constraints
location: Assumption 5.2, Theorem 5.3, Proposition 5.5 and Appendix E.
text: In finite-state Bayesian persuasion, fix prior p₀ and require E[p]=p₀. Let nonnegative upper-semicontinuous sender utility satisfy λu(p)+(1−λ)u(q)≤M u(λp+(1−λ)q) for every posterior p,q and λ∈[0,1]. For m continuous convex constraints, compare OPT_ante under E[f_j(p)]≤c_j with OPT_post under f_j(p)≤c_j after every signal. Determine the least universal C(m,M) with OPT_ante≤C(m,M)OPT_post, equivalently the worst OPT_ante/OPT_post ratio when OPT_post>0. For m≥2,M>1, the M^m upper bound and m+1 lower bound at M=2 do not match. The inequality formulation also covers zero optima.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Depth-independent exact gadgets for robust subgame responses
author: David Milec; Ondřej Kubíček; Viliam Lisý
source_title: Continual Depth-limited Responses for Computing Counter-strategies in Sequential Games
location: §5, Definition 5.1 and paragraph immediately after; Theorems 5.2–5.3.
text: In finite two-player zero-sum perfect-recall extensive-form games, can continual depth-limited restricted Nash response use a resolving gadget whose size is independent of the number of previously resolved subgames, while satisfying Definition 5.1 of Milec–Kubíček–Lisý? The gadget must preserve, for every resolving-player information set, the value contributed by the unrestricted-opponent branch G′ when the opponent best responds in the full G′. The current full gadget retains past solved regions and grows linearly with resolving depth; ordinary safety gadgets fail this exactness condition.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Sharp complete-policy regret for tallying feedback loops
author: Dhruv Malik; Yuanzhi Li; Aarti Singh
source_title: Complete Policy Regret Bounds for Tallying Bandits
text: In the shared tallying-bandit model, determine the minimax expected complete policy regret jointly in T,m,K. No monotonicity, repeated-exposure optimality or weighted-tally assumption is imposed. The target is the best full action sequence under its own induced feedback, rather than the best fixed action.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Sharp regret under approximate repeated-exposure optimality
author: Dhruv Malik; Conor Igoe; Yuanzhi Li; Aarti Singh
source_title: Weighted Tallying Bandits: Overcoming Intractability via Repeated Exposure Optimality
location: Definition of α-REO, main regret theorem, §4 discussion; Malik thesis §§4.3.1 and 4.6, pp. 49 and 56.
text: For weighted tallying bandits, let losses be h_x(w_xᵀy) with unknown w_x∈(0,1]^m, h_x:R→[0,1], and y recording occurrences of x among the last m choices. Assume α-REO: some x* satisfies h_{x*}(||w_{x*}||₁)≤h_x(w_xᵀy)+α for every x and y∈{1}×{0,1}^{m−1}. With known m, determine the minimax complete-policy-regret dependence on α across all joint regimes of T,m,K. The established bound is ~O(√(KT)+mK)+αT; necessity of αT is established only in some regimes, not for every α>0.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Optimal anonymous conventions for repeated resource allocation
author: Luděk Cigler; Boi Faltings
source_title: Symmetric Subgame Perfect Equilibria in Resource Allocation
location: AAAI 2012, §3 end and §4, p. 1332; thesis Definitions 16, 19, 21–23 and §§4.2.3, 5.2, printed pp. 77 and 86.
text: In Cigler–Faltings’ infinitely repeated resource-allocation game G_{N,C}, N agents each yield or choose one of C homogeneous resources; yielding pays 0, sole use pays 1, and collision pays −γ<0. For fixed 0<δ<1, characterize the highest expected discounted social payoff of symmetric subgame-perfect strategy profiles, especially convention/implementation profiles that first break symmetry and then assign continuation roles. Symmetry means equivariance under renaming agents, not identical realized actions. Preserve the source’s public occupancy feedback and, for augmented conventions, its public coordination signal, uniform on {1,…,K} independently each round and visible before acting, for a specified K (K=1 gives no additional signal).

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Complexity of optimal defense under one-target leakage
author: Haifeng Xu
source_title: Information as a Double-Edged Sword in Strategic Interactions
location: Chapter 8, §8.2.1, Remark after Lemma 16, printed pp. 114–115; LP (8.4).
text: In the zero-sum PRIL security game, a defender mixes over subsets of at most k of n targets. Attacking target j pays the defender r_j if protected and c_j otherwise, with r_j>c_j. With known probability p_i, exactly target i’s realized protection status leaks before the attacker chooses a target; with p₀=1−Σ_i p_i nothing leaks. For rational data, is computing the optimal defender commitment polynomial-time solvable, or NP-hard? The NP-hardness of optimizing an arbitrary linear functional over the pairwise-marginal polytope, or of the column-generation oracle, does not itself prove hardness of this restricted game objective.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Optimal corruption dependence with unilateral preference-data coverage
author: Andi Nika; Debmalya Mandal; Parameswaran Kamalaruban; Adish Singla; Goran Radanović
source_title: Corruption-robust Offline Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
text: In finite-horizon general-sum linear Markov games with Bradley–Terry trajectory-preference labels and the shared coverage assumption, what is the minimax Nash-gap dependence on strong contamination replacing an ε fraction of offline comparison tuples? Keep horizon, feature dimension and coverage constants explicit. Is the O(√ε) corruption term necessary, or can it approach the linear-ε lower bound known under uniform coverage? Separate finite-sample error.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Optimal uncoupled last-iterate rate in irreducible Markov games
author: Yang Cai; Haipeng Luo; Chen-Yu Wei; Weiqiang Zheng
source_title: Uncoupled and Convergent Learning in Two-Player Zero-Sum Markov Games with Bandit Feedback
location: §3 interaction and convergence definitions; Assumption 1; Theorem 2; §7 Discussion.
text: What is the optimal finite-time last-iterate duality-gap rate for uncoupled rational learning in finite two-player zero-sum γ-discounted Markov games, γ∈[1/2,1), with unknown rewards/transitions, when every stationary policy pair reaches every state from every other in expected time at most L? Each player sees the state and its sampled bounded payoff, but not the opponent’s action or policy; only one continuing trajectory is available. Measure max_s[max_y V_{x_T,y}(s)−min_x V_{x,y_T}(s)], with state/action counts, L and (1−γ) dependence explicit. The known 2023 rate is ~O(T^{−1/(9+η)}) for every η>0.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Polynomial-time solution of simple stochastic reachability games
author: Anne Condon
source_title: The Complexity of Stochastic Games
location: Condon (1992), complexity question; Condon (1993), introduction; Rüst (2007), §1.1 and final SSG chapter.
text: Is there a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given a finite stopping simple stochastic game and start state s, decides whether max_σ min_τ Pr_s^{σ,τ}(reach Win)≥1/2? Vertices belong to Max, Min or chance; chance chooses between two successors uniformly, and Win/Lose are absorbing. Stopping means absorption occurs almost surely under every strategy pair. Time is measured in the encoded graph size. Equivalently, compute exact values and optimal positional strategies. Do not confuse approximate value iteration or fixed-parameter algorithms with this worst-case polynomial guarantee.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Polynomial bit-complexity for deterministic mean-payoff games
author: Uri Zwick; Mike Paterson
source_title: The Complexity of Mean Payoff Games on Graphs
location: Zwick–Paterson (1996), introduction and complexity results; Friedmann thesis abstract and §3.3.
text: Given a finite total directed graph partitioned between Max and Min, binary-encoded integer edge weights w, initial vertex s and rational threshold q, can one decide in deterministic polynomial time whether Max has a strategy ensuring liminf_{T→∞}(1/T)Σ_{t<T}w(e_t)≥q against every Min strategy? Equivalently, compute the value and optimal positional strategies. The unresolved target is polynomial in bit length, not pseudo-polynomial in the numerical weight bound. This deterministic mean-payoff problem is not known equivalent to simple stochastic reachability, although it reduces to it.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Deciding exact infinite discounted trade-off targets
author: Udi Boker; Thomas A. Henzinger; Jan Otop
source_title: The Target Discounted-Sum Problem
location: Definition 1, §§1–3 and §8; updated and corrected version of LICS 2015, DOI 10.1109/LICS.2015.74.
text: Given rational $0<\lambda<1$ and $t$, is it decidable whether some unrestricted infinite binary sequence satisfies $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}b_i\lambda^i=t$? The general unresolved case already includes rational $\lambda<1/2$ that are not reciprocal integers. Existence of a finite or eventually periodic solution is decidable; those restrictions are not the target.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Rationality of discounted-utility tail probabilities
author: Nathalie Bertrand; Pranav Ghorpade; Senthil Rajasekaran; Sasha Rubin; Moshe Y. Vardi
source_title: The Stochastic Target Discounted-Sum Problem
location: §5 Conclusion, threshold-probability paragraph; Theorem 13 for the solved arbitrary-precision approximation result.
text: Let C be a finite Markov chain with a specified initial state, rational transition probabilities and integer transition labels w_i from a finite alphabet. For rational λ∈(0,1) and t, must Pr_C(∑_{i=0}^∞ λ^i w_i>t) be rational? If always rational, can that value be computed exactly? Approximation to any prescribed precision is already established.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Completeness of identification under context-dependent study selection
author: Jaron J. R. Lee; AmirEmad Ghassami; Ilya Shpitser
source_title: A General Identification Algorithm For Data Fusion Problems Under Systematic Selection
location: §6, Algorithms 1–2 and Theorems 4–5; Lee thesis Chapter 4, printed pp. 56–58, especially p. 58 (PDF p. 73).
text: In the context-selected structural causal models of Lee–Ghassami–Shpitser, is SS-ID (Algorithms 1–2) complete for identifying p(Y(a,S=∅)) from the observed joint law p(V), including the selector S, and its labelled selection ADMMG? The model allows latent confounding and arbitrary selection into experimental regimes. Equivalently, does its remaining unclassified FAIL case always admit two compatible CS-SCMs agreeing on p(V) but disagreeing on the target? Preserve the context-specific structural restrictions and the source’s support/positivity conditions; ordinary selection-bias ID does not establish this claim.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: A common causal estimand without a common do-calculus proof
author: Clément Yvernes; Emilie Devijver; Marianne Clausel; Eric Gaussier
source_title: Identifiability in Causal Abstractions: A Hierarchy of Criteria
text: Is there a collection C of causal diagrams on the same observed variables and a query Q=P(y|do(x),z), with X,Y,Z pairwise disjoint, such that one observational functional identifies Q in every G∈C and every SCM compatible with G, yet no single do-calculus derivation of an identifying expression is valid in all G∈C? This is the source’s IG-but-not-ICD conjecture. The functional must be common to the class; mere separate identifiability with different graph-dependent formulas is insufficient.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Generic distinguishability of every noncomplete cyclic equal-noise graph
author: Mathias Drton; Benjamin Hollering; Jun Wu
source_title: Identifiability of Homoscedastic Linear Structural Equation Models using Algebraic Matroids
text: For distinct noncomplete G,H, must dim(M_G∩M_H)<max{dim M_G,dim M_H}? This max-dimension notion permits inclusion of lower-dimensional models.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Parentally closed certificates for distinct feedback components
author: Mathias Drton; Benjamin Hollering; Jun Wu
source_title: Identifiability of Homoscedastic Linear Structural Equation Models using Algebraic Matroids
text: For noncomplete G1,G2 with equal labelled out-degrees but different strongly-connected-component partitions, must some k∈{1,2},i and L⊆ne_Gk(i) satisfy pa_Gk(L)∩ne_Gk(i)⊆L and |ch_Gk(i)∩L|>|ch_G(3−k)(i)∩L|?

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: An edge-reversal obstruction to Jacobian-matroid causal tests
author: Mathias Drton; Benjamin Hollering; Jun Wu
source_title: Identifiability of Homoscedastic Linear Structural Equation Models using Algebraic Matroids
text: For complete G1,G2 differing by one edge reversal, do their Jacobian matroids coincide? Ground-set elements are precision entries K_ij, i≤j; independence is column independence in the transposed parametrization Jacobian over the rational-function parameter field.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Boundary-free OCT rigidity for every positive linear scaling
author: Simon Buchholz; Michel Besserve; Bernhard Schölkopf
source_title: Function Classes for Identifiable Nonlinear Independent Component Analysis
location: Theorem 5 and paragraph immediately following, printed p. 9 in full arXiv PDF; Definitions 4–5.
text: Let ν be uniform on C_d=(0,1)^d, R∈O(d), and D=diag(μ1,…,μd) with every μi>0. If Φ_t is a smooth family of diffeomorphisms onto their images, analytic in t, each with mutually orthogonal Jacobian columns, Φ_0(x)=RDx and (Φ_t)#ν=(RD)#ν for all t, must Φ_t=RD on C_d for all t? Theorem 5 proves this for almost every positive scaling vector; the open extension asks for every vector. No boundary agreement condition is imposed.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Sharpness of closed-form multivalued causal-response bounds

In the known-prior case, can any nonlinear rule strictly outperform the best fixed linear extremization m+c(k)(k^−1Σ_iY_i−m)? Here v(Z)=E[(Y−m)²]−E[(Y−Z)²], with v(Y_[k])>0. What is the minimax sample size n*(d,η,b,σ,u) for estimating β within Euclidean error u with probability 0.99, in regimes above the intrinsic nonidentification floor? The source characterizes the unlimited-sample floor up to constants but explicitly leaves optimal finite-sample complexity unresolved; that established floor is excluded from the question.

title: Finite-time regret of likelihood-projection sampling over latent orders
author: Emil Carlsson; Newton Mwai; Fredrik D. Johansson
source_title: Latent Order Bandits
location: Current v2 (18 August 2026), §3.2, Algorithm 2 and printed pp. 6–7.
text: There are k arms with independent Gaussian rewards N(μ_a,σ²), known σ, and a known finite collection of m order-constrained mean sets H_s; the unknown μ belongs to their union. Put M_a={v:v_a≥v_b for all b} and Σ_a=∪_{s:a maximal in s} H_s. At each round, lobTS assigns arm a probability proportional to exp(−d_a(t)/(2σ²)), where d_a(t)=inf_{v∈M_a∩Σ_a}∑_b N_b(t)(v_b−μ̂_b(t))² (empty set gives zero probability). It starts with no observations; unobserved coordinates have zero weight. What finite-time frequentist bound holds for R_T=E∑_{t≤T}(max_b μ_b−μ_{A_t}), as a function of T, the gaps and order structure? In particular, is R_T=o(T) for every well-specified instance with a unique best arm? This asks about the specified heuristic, not existence of some low-regret algorithm.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Remove the dimension loss in variation-adaptive two-point dynamic regret
author: Hang Yu; Yu-Hu Yan; Peng Zhao
source_title: Improved Dimension Dependence for Bandit Convex Optimization with Gradient Variation
location: §5.1, equation (5.1), Theorem 6; Appendix E.1 Theorem 9; latest arXiv v2, 8 September 2026.
text: Let X⊂R^d be compact convex with rB₂⊂X⊂RB₂. An oblivious sequence of convex G-Lipschitz, L-smooth losses f_t is observed only through two exact function values per round. The loss charged is their average. For an oblivious comparator sequence u_t, define P_T=∑_{t=2}^T||u_t−u_{t−1}||₂ and V_T=∑_{t=2}^T sup_{x∈X}||∇f_t(x)−∇f_{t−1}(x)||₂². Can the extra factor d in the source’s expected dynamic-regret guarantee Õ(√[d³(1+P_T+V_T)(1+P_T)]) be removed, while retaining its P_T,V_T dependence and not knowing P_T? The target is the √d rather than d^{3/2} leading dimension dependence; determine if it is attainable or intrinsically impossible, preserving initialization/lower-order terms where needed.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Does time-dependent Pandora search admit a PTAS?
author: Georgios Amanatidis; Ben Berger; Tomer Ezra; Michal Feldman; Federico Fusco; Rebecca Reiffenhäuser; Artem Tsikiridis
source_title: Pandora’s Box Problem With Time Constraints
location: §2 model and §2.1 oracle model; §5 conclusions, printed p. 17.
text: In Pandora’s Box Over Time there are n boxes, integer processing delays p_i≥0, and an explicit horizon H≥n+∑_i p_i. Inspecting unused box i at time t costs c_i(t)≥0, draws V_it from a known nonnegative distribution D_it, and prevents another inspection before t+1+p_i. All box-time draws are independent. Stopping is allowed only after every initiated inspection has completed (t_i+p_i≤T). At stopping time T≤H, collect max_{inspected i} v̄_i(V_it,T−t−p_i), minus all inspection costs; 0≤v̄_i(v,τ)≤v̄_i(v,0)=v. Waiting and adaptive inspection/stopping are allowed. Does this optimization problem admit a polynomial-time approximation scheme, or can one rule out a PTAS under a standard complexity assumption? Preserve the source’s value-oracle access for expected maxima of reservation-truncated independent rewards, or state an explicit finite-support encoding. Approximation is multiplicative relative to optimal expected net utility, with stopping without inspection available.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Efficient optimal stopping under a finite mixture of product distributions
author: Andrés Cristi
source_title: Hardness of Correlated Prophet Inequality, contribution to Approximation Algorithms for Stochastic Optimization (Dagstuhl Seminar 25132)
text: There are m known scenarios, each specifying n distributions on a common set of k reward values. A scenario is sampled uniformly once; conditional on it, the n rewards are sampled independently. Rewards arrive in their fixed order. A policy observes the prefix and must irrevocably stop on one observed current reward, maximizing expected payoff. Can an optimal online stopping policy be computed in time polynomial in m,n,k (and the bit length for rational inputs)? If exact optimization is intractable, what approximation to the optimal online payoff is possible? The computational output must permit the policy’s stop/continue decision at an observed history without expanding an exponential history tree.

author: José Correa; Maximilian Fichtl; Reda Jlibene; Rida Laraki; Vasilis Livanos; Kevin Schewior; Victor Verdugo
source_title: Threshold Dynamics and Correlated Prophet Inequalities
location: §1.1, especially printed pp. 2–4; common-base model and stated 1/2 question.
text: Let Z,X_1,…,X_n be mutually independent nonnegative random variables with known bounded-support laws. Only Y_i=Z+X_i is revealed, sequentially in fixed order; neither Z nor any X_i is directly observed. Does every such instance admit a possibly randomized stopping rule τ∈{1,…,n}, adapted to the revealed Y-prefixes, satisfying E[Y_τ]≥(1/2)E[max_iY_i]? The rule may use the whole observation history and must accept a current value irrevocably, taking the last value if necessary. It is not restricted to one fixed threshold.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms

author: Evan J. R. Brody; Haya Diwan; Lisa Hellerstein; Thomas Lidbetter
source_title: On Extensions of the Unanimous Vote Problem
location: §4 definition and Theorem 7; §6 open questions, printed p. 11.
text: There are n independent dice with known rational outcome probabilities on d colors, each usable once. Choose a permutation before observing outcomes; reveal dice in that order until every color has appeared or all n dice have been revealed. Minimize the expected number of reveals. What is the exact computational complexity of finding an optimal permutation: is there a polynomial-time algorithm in the explicit n×d probability input and its bit length, or is the optimization NP-hard? The prescribed rule keeps revealing if collecting every color has become impossible, until all dice are exhausted.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Remove the dimension penalty from one-batch trajectory-preference exploration
author: Andreas Schlaginhaufen; Reda Ouhamma; Maryam Kamgarpour
source_title: Efficient Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning: Randomized Exploration Meets Experimental Design
location: §2; Assumptions 2.1 and 3.3; Algorithm 2; Theorem 3.5 and footnote 3 immediately following it.
text: Consider the source's discounted MDP with known continuous features φ(s,a)∈R^d, ||φ(s,a)||≤L, unknown linear reward rθ*(s,a)=〈θ*,φ(s,a)〉, ||θ*||≤B, and trajectory features Φ(τ)=∑h≥0 γ^hφ(sh,ah). Independent comparison labels satisfy P(τ≻τ′)=σ(〈θ*,Φ(τ)−Φ(τ′)〉). A learner can execute policies and call a polynomial-time (ε,δ)-PAC reward-optimization oracle for any proposed reward vector. Can computationally tractable preference-free exploration, collecting T trajectory pairs before a single final batch of labels, remove the extra √d from the high-probability final policy loss bound Õ(√(κd³/T)), achieving Õ(√(κd²/T)) under the same access assumptions? Here κ=max|z|≤2BL/(1−γ) 1/σ′(z), and loss is V*θ*−Vπ̂θ*.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Find a weighted minimum cut from ordinal cut comparisons efficiently
author: Vincent Cohen-Addad; Tommaso d’Orsi; Anupam Gupta; Guru Guruganesh; Euiwoong Lee; Renato Paes Leme; Debmalya Panigrahi; Madhusudhan Reddy Pittu; Jon Schneider; David P. Woodruff
source_title: Combinatorial Optimization using Comparison Oracles
location: §5 closing paragraph; AppendixD.3, especially D.3.1–D.3.2; §1.1 for computation-versus-query distinction.
text: An unknown undirected graph on a known vertex set V, |V|=n has nonnegative edge weights. Write c(S)=∑{u,v}:u∈S,v∉S wuv for each nonempty proper S⊂V. The only weight access is an exact oracle returning sign(c(S)−c(T)) for two such cuts. In the source’s oracle model (two n-bit cut indicators per query, a unit-cost oracle call), is there an algorithm using polynomially many queries and polynomial additional computation that returns an exact global minimum cut for arbitrary nonnegative weights? The source leaves the weighted extension open even for integer weights in [0,B]; distinguish polynomial dependence on the bit length log B from the known (nB)^{O(r² log B)} special-case bound for r distinct weighted degrees. No comparisons of differences of cut values or arbitrary edge subsets are available.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Close the comparison cost gap for decision-sufficient knapsack utilities
author: Ritabrata Barat; Siddharth Barman; Nirjhar Das; Sukruta Midigeshi
source_title: Packing Linear Programs and Fractional Knapsack using Comparison Oracles
location: §1 Our Results, printed p. 2; Definition 1, p. 4; Theorem 1; Theorem 25, p. 29.
text: Let n≥3, δ<1/(6n²), and unknown distinct values vi∈(0,1]∩δZ define x*v(p)∈argmax{vᵀx:x∈[0,1]^n,pᵀx≤B}, with an unknown fixed greedy tie-breaking order. Prices p range only over [0,1]^n. The known capacity satisfies B≤(n−1)(min vi/max vi−δ²/n²). An oracle returns sign(wᵀx*v(p)−wᵀx*v(q)) for any two prices, with fixed unknown w∈R^n_{>0}. Determine the sharp worst-case comparison complexity of recovering v up to positive scale with success probability at least 2/3 over all admissible instances. In particular, is the additive B² overhead in O(n log(1/δ)+B²) necessary, or can recovery uniformly match the Ω(n log(1/δ)) lower bound? The unresolved gap matters when B² dominates n log(1/δ).

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Achieve square-root accuracy from sigmoid comparisons of bundles
author: Kaien Sho; Shinji Ito
source_title: Submodular Function Minimization with Dueling Oracle
location: §3 model, printed p. 6; Theorems 4–5, printed pp. 9–10; §7 Conclusion and Open Questions, p. 10.
text: Let f:2^[n]→[0,1] be an unknown submodular cost. At round t choose arbitrary subsets St,S′t and receive a fresh independent Yt∈{−1,+1} with P(Yt=+1|St,S′t)=σ(b[f(St)−f(S′t)]), where the slope b>0 is fixed and known. After T calls output Ŝ and measure expected simple regret E[f(Ŝ)−minS f(S)]. Can a computationally efficient algorithm attain T^(−1/2) decay, with polynomial dependence on n for each fixed b, rather than the source’s O_b(n^(7/5)T^(−2/5)) bound? Establish the sharp rate. The source conjectures the square-root T exponent; its general lower bound is Ω_b(n/√T), while Ω_b(n^(3/2)/√T) is proved only when every queried pair differs in O(1) elements.

author: Yuval Filmus; Massimo Lauria; Mladen Mikša; Jakob Nordström; Marc Vinyals
source_title: Towards an Understanding of Polynomial Calculus: New Separations and Lower Bounds
text: Fix a field K and a constant input-clause width k. For unsatisfiable k-CNFs F, is Deg_PCR,K(F)≤O(Sp_PCR,K(F)), with a constant depending at most on K and k? Here PCR uses Boolean and complementarity axioms, multiplication by a variable and K-linear combinations; Deg minimizes largest monomial degree and Sp minimizes peak total monomial occurrences in retained polynomials, counted with repetition. The current general relation loses a square root; no XOR substitution of F is allowed.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Can bounded-depth proofs of search hardness be analyzed efficiently?
author: Noel Arteche; Albert Atserias; Susanna F. de Rezende; Erfan Khaniki
source_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
text: For every fixed-depth Frege Q, is PAP_Q restricted to s≥n^c in P for some constant c>0?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Can witnesses be extracted from proof-search lower bounds in parallel?
author: Noel Arteche; Albert Atserias; Susanna F. de Rezende; Erfan Khaniki
source_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
location: §1.4 p. 12; Definition 3.5 p. 25; Theorem 4.6 and Corollary 4.7 pp. 32–33.
text: For φ with polynomially many clauses and s≥n³, can FNC extract a satisfying assignment, or report none, given a resolution refutation of Ref_s(φ)?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Can resolution be weakly automated by a stronger certificate system?
author: Noel Arteche; Albert Atserias; Susanna F. de Rezende; Erfan Khaniki
source_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
location: §1.4 p. 12, On the weak automatability of Resolution; Theorem 1.9.
text: Does an automatable Cook–Reckhow system polynomial-time simulate resolution? Automatability requires deterministic proof finding polynomial in input length plus shortest proof size.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Does generic one-wayness already obstruct threshold-logic proof search?
author: Noel Arteche; Gaia Carenini; Matthew Gray
source_title: Quantum Automating TC^0-Frege Is LWE-Hard
location: Introduction, Open problems: Towards generic hardness assumptions, p. 4 (October 2025 full version); journal §1.3.
text: Does existence of one-way functions imply that TC^0-Frege is not weakly automatable by deterministic classical algorithms? TC^0-Frege uses constant-depth threshold formulas; weak automatability permits any Cook–Reckhow system with polynomial-time proof translation from TC^0-Frege and a proof-finding algorithm polynomial in its shortest proof length. The hypothesis is generic existence of a standard polynomial-time one-way function, not security of a particular factoring, Diffie–Hellman or lattice construction.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Channel coding with a fixed-state receiver
author: Tomer Berg; Or Ordentlich; Ofer Shayevitz
source_title: Statistical Inference with Limited Memory: A Survey
text: For a given finite-alphabet DMC W(y|x), S states and 0<ε<1, characterize C_ε(W,S)=sup_{n≥1} R*(n,W,S,ε). Here R* maximizes (log₂ M)/n over deterministic encoders [M]→X^n, a time-invariant update g:Y×[S]→[S], initial state U0=1 and final decoder d:[S]→[M], with a uniform message and average error≤ε. Can processing more symbols than can be stored verbatim improve the optimum, and by how much?

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Sharp sample–memory tradeoff for streaming uniformity testing
author: Clément L. Canonne; Joy Qiping Yang
source_title: Simpler Distribution Testing with Little Memory
location: §4 p. 10, first open direction; Theorems 1.1–1.2 and Table 1.
text: Determine the sharp uniformity-testing sample–memory tradeoff n_U*(k,ε,m), especially for low memory and nonconstant ε.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Sharp sample–memory tradeoff for two-stream closeness testing
author: Clément L. Canonne; Joy Qiping Yang
source_title: Simpler Distribution Testing with Little Memory
text: Determine the sharp closeness-testing tradeoff n_C*(k,ε,m), with both distributions unknown.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Does fresh algorithmic randomness help memory-limited uniformity tests?
author: Clément L. Canonne; Joy Qiping Yang
source_title: Simpler Distribution Testing with Little Memory
text: Can internal randomness strictly improve uniformity-testing sample complexity at fixed m and error 1/3, compared with deterministic updates and decisions on the random data?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Optimal log-loss prediction with finitely many states
author: Eado Meron; Meir Feder
source_title: Finite-Memory Universal Prediction of Individual Sequences
location: §II equations(2)–(3), p. 1508; §V.C pp. 1518–1520, particularly the final conjecture before §VI.
text: Let A range over randomized time-invariant K-state predictors, with fixed initial state, Bernoulli forecast p_t=g(M_t), and update M_{t+1}~P(·|M_t,x_t). Define r_K=inf_A limsup_{n→∞} max_{x^n∈{0,1}^n} [n^-1 E_A Σ_{t=1}^n (−x_t log₂ p_t−(1−x_t)log₂(1−p_t))−h₂(n^-1Σ_t x_t)]. Is r_K=Θ(1/K), or is a logarithmic factor necessary? The known gap is Ω(1/K) versus O(log K/K).

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Exact fixed-degree sum-of-squares refutation for finite-domain constraints
author: Alex Bortolotti; Monaldo Mastrolilli; Luis Felipe Vargas
source_title: On the Degree Automatability of Sum-of-Squares Proofs
text: For every fixed finite rational domain D, finite constraint language Γ and degree d, is the degree-d SoS-CSP decision problem polynomial-time solvable? Given a CSP(Γ) instance in the source’s local polynomial encoding, with equations p_i=0 and domain equations ∏_{a∈D}(x_j−a)=0, decide whether real polynomials s_l,h_i satisfy −1=Σ_l s_l²+Σ_i h_i p_i with all displayed products of degree≤d. Keep the canonical input encoding and exact feasibility. No degree-d refutation does not mean that the CSP is satisfiable.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Do sparse CNF refutations require unexpectedly large coefficient encodings?
author: Tuomas Hakoniemi
source_title: Monomial-size vs. Bit-complexity in Sums-of-Squares and Polynomial Calculus
location: §8 Conclusions and open questions, p. 15; definitions §§2.2–2.3 pp. 3–4.
text: For unsatisfiable CNFs F with the standard polynomial clause equations and Boolean/complementarity axioms, are minimum monomial size M_P(F) and minimum rational bit complexity B_P(F) polynomially related for P=SOS and P=PCR/Q? In particular, is B_P(F)≤poly(|F|+M_P(F))? Monomial size counts explicit monomials with multiplicity, permitting real coefficients for SOS; bit complexity uses reduced rational fractions in binary and includes PCR inference scalars. Different refutations may attain the two minima. Treat the two systems as one comparison family.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Balanced splitting for cross-fit Gaussian confidence sets
author: Robin Dunn; Aaditya Ramdas; Sivaraman Balakrishnan; Larry Wasserman
source_title: Gaussian universal likelihood ratio testing
location: §3.1; Supplement §S3; dissertation §2.3.1 p. 12 and Appendix B.3.
text: For even n, d≥1 and α∈(0,1), let Y₁,…,Yₙ be i.i.d. N_d(θ*,I_d). For a split with n₀+n₁=n and n₀,n₁≥1, let L_j(θ) be the likelihood on part j and Ȳ_j its sample mean. Put C_CF={θ:[L₀(Ȳ₁)/L₀(θ)+L₁(Ȳ₀)/L₁(θ)]/2<1/α}. Does n₀=n₁ minimize E[diam(C_CF)²] over the split sizes, with Euclidean diameter?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Can convex surrogates beat polyhedral embedding dimension?
author: Jessica Finocchiaro; Rafael Frongillo; Bo Waggoner
source_title: Embedding Dimension of Polyhedral Losses
text: For a finite nonredundant loss ℓ:R×Y→R₊, let emb(ℓ) be the smallest d admitting a polyhedral L:R^d×Y→R₊ and injective φ:R→R^d with L(φ(r),y)=ℓ(r,y) and r Bayes-optimal for p iff φ(r) is L-optimal for p. Let cc(ℓ) be the smallest dimension of a convex surrogate calibrated to ℓ on all of Δ_Y. Must emb(ℓ)=cc(ℓ)? Equality for dimension 1 is proved; the question concerns higher dimensions.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Convex CVaR elicitation dimension
author: Jessica Finocchiaro; Rafael Frongillo; Bo Waggoner
source_title: Unifying Lower Bounds on Prediction Dimension of Consistent Convex Surrogates
text: Fix α∈(0,1). On the class P of continuous densities with support R, strictly increasing CDF and finite first moment, define CVaR_α(p)=inf_z E_p[α^{-1}(z−Y)1{Y≤z}−z]. Is elic_cvx(CVaR_α)≥3: can no two-dimensional convex, lower-semicontinuous, integrable loss with attained Bayes minima elicit a property from which CVaR_α is recovered by a link?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Dimension bounds without attained minima
author: Jessica Finocchiaro; Rafael Frongillo; Bo Waggoner
source_title: Unifying Lower Bounds on Prediction Dimension of Consistent Convex Surrogates
text: Let γ be a property elicited by a finite target loss on finite Y, let P⊆Δ_Y be convex and p∈relint(P). A d-flat is {q∈P:E_q V(Y)=0} for some V:Y→R^d. If no d-flat through p is contained in γ^{-1}(r) for an optimal report r∈γ(p), must every convex surrogate calibrated to γ have dimension at least d+1 even when its expected loss need not attain its infimum? Keep finite expected losses and finite Bayes risk; only attainment is removed.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Lipschitz elicitation complexity beyond one dimension
author: Jessica Finocchiaro; Victor Ganson; Drona Khurana
source_title: Smoothed Elicitation Complexity for Approximate Γ-calibration of Discrete Classification Tasks
text: For an elicitable finite-valued property γ:Δ_Y⇒R with finite Y, characterize the minimum d admitting a single-valued Lipschitz elicitable property Γ:Δ_Y→[0,1]^d and a link ψ such that ψ(Γ(p))∈γ(p) for every p. What geometric conditions characterize the cases d≥2, extending the source’s one-dimensional strong-orderability characterization?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The multi-observation elicitation frontier of probability norms
author: Sebastian Casalaina-Martin; Rafael Frongillo; Tom Morgan; Bo Waggoner
source_title: Multi-Observation Elicitation
text: For a finite alphabet Y of size N≥3 and integer k≥3, determine the Pareto-minimal pairs (d,m) for which ||p||_k is smoothly (d,m)-elicitable on Δ_Y: a d-dimensional m-identifiable C∞ property Γ̂ uniquely minimizes E_{p^m}L(r,Y₁,…,Y_m), and a C∞ link on a neighborhood of its image recovers ||p||_k. Determine the intermediate regimes 1<m<k; the endpoints (N−1,1) and (1,k) are known under these smoothness conventions.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Do adaptive-order betting mixtures dominate all monotone independent e-mergers?
author: Vladimir Vovk; Ruodu Wang
source_title: Merging sequential e-values via martingales
text: Is every coordinatewise nondecreasing ie-merging function pointwise dominated by a generalized martingale merging function, for every finite number K of inputs? The known counterexample to GMMF domination without monotonicity is excluded.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Are all precise independent e-mergers adaptive-order betting mixtures?
author: Vladimir Vovk; Ruodu Wang
source_title: Merging sequential e-values via martingales
text: Suppose an ie-merger F is precise: E F(E₁,…,E_K)=1 for every independent vector of nonnegative mean-one inputs. Must F itself be a generalized martingale merging function, without assuming coordinatewise monotonicity?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The minimax cumulative squared calibration rate
author: Lunjia Hu; Haipeng Luo; Spandan Senapati; Vatsal Sharan
source_title: Efficient Swap Multicalibration of Elicitable Properties
text: In T rounds of binary forecasting against non-prescient adaptive outcomes, determine inf_A sup_B E[Σ_{p:n_p>0} n_p(ȳ_p−p)²], where n_p counts forecasts equal to p and ȳ_p is their empirical outcome mean. Is the known ~O(T^{1/3}) upper bound optimal, or what is the sharp rate? This is realized-bin squared calibration, with no fixed coarsening of the forecast values.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Statistical and computational auditing of distance to multiaccuracy
author: Nathan Derhake; Siddartha Devic; Dutch Hansen; Kuan Liu; Vatsal Sharan
source_title: Auditability and the Landscape of Distance to Multicalibration
text: Let X be finite, D a distribution on X×{0,1} whose X-marginal has full support, f:X→[0,1] given, and C={S₁,…,S_k} specified by membership queries. Set dMA_C,D(f)=inf_g E_{D_X}|f(X)−g(X)| subject to E_D[(g(X)−Y)1{X∈S_j}]=0 for every j and 0≤g≤1. From i.i.d. labeled D samples, determine the sample and computational complexity of additive-ε estimation with constant success probability, including whether domain-size-independent polynomial dependence on k and 1/ε is achievable.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: High-probability comparator-square-loss regret for a sampled expert
author: Liyu Chen; Haipeng Luo; Chen-Yu Wei
source_title: Impossible Tuning Made Possible: A New Expert Algorithm and Its Applications
text: If the learner must actually sample I_t∼w_t and incurs ℓ_{t,I_t}, can one obtain, simultaneously for every expert i, realized regret Σ_t(ℓ_{t,I_t}−ℓ_{t,i})=~O(1+√Σ_tℓ_{t,i}²) with probability at least 1−δ, with logarithmic dependence on d,T,1/δ? Or must some loss sequence force a larger-order deviation than the mixed-action comparator-square bound?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: One expert forecaster adaptive to both comparator and excess-loss variance
author: Liyu Chen; Haipeng Luo; Chen-Yu Wei
source_title: Impossible Tuning Made Possible: A New Expert Algorithm and Its Applications
text: Is there a single online full-information algorithm such that, for every i, Σ_t⟨w_t−e_i,ℓ_t⟩=~O(1+√{(log d) min[Σ_tℓ_{t,i}², Σ_t(ℓ_{t,i}−⟨w_t,ℓ_t⟩)²]}) on every bounded signed loss sequence? The same weights must realize both guarantees; selecting separately tuned algorithms after observing the sequence is not allowed.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The rounding gap between sequential calibration distance and its relaxation
author: Mingda Qiao; Letian Zheng
source_title: On the Distance from Calibration in Sequential Prediction
text: For y∈{0,1}^T and p∈[0,1]^T, let CD=min_{q calibrated for y}Σ_t|p_t−q_t|. Define LCD as inf_{(D_t)}Σ_t E_{q∼D_t}|p_t−q|, where the finite-support distributions D_t satisfy Σ_t(y_t−v)D_t({v})=0 at every support value v. Determine the sharp worst-case gap CD−LCD as T grows: is the proved O(√T) gap tight? More generally, can the sparse bound CD≤C·LCD+O(m), m=|{p_t}|, attain leading coefficient C=1?

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Jointly optimal conformity scores and sequential bets
author: Vladimir Vovk
source_title: An optimality property of the Bayes–Kelly algorithm
location: §3, equations (4)–(5); Theorem 3.2, equation (8); §4 Conclusion, printed p. 9.
text: Let Z be a measurable space, Q a specified law on Z^∞, and N≥1. Choose a measurable conformity measure A:Z^(*)×Z→R, where Z^(*) is the space of finite multisets. At time n, set a_i=A({Z_1,…,Z_n},Z_i) and p_n=(#{i≤n:a_i<a_n}+τ_n#{i≤n:a_i=a_n})/n, with independent τ_n∼Unif[0,1]. Let B range over nonnegative martingales starting at 1 for an i.i.d. uniform p-value sequence. How should (A,B) be jointly chosen to maximize E_{Q⊗U}[log B_N(p_1,…,p_N)]? Equivalently, characterize the optimizing A and value sup_A D(Q_A^N∥U^N), where Q_A^N is the induced p-value law. The fixed-A betting optimum is already known.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Natural-filtration catch-up for an infinite null family
author: Vladimir Vovk
source_title: The power of forgetting in statistical hypothesis testing
