location: Author revision 2 September 2024: §6.2, Proposition 6.2 and equation(13), printed pp. 13–14; §8 fourth research bullet, p. 19. COPA 2023 version uses Proposition 10.
text: Let (P_θ)_{θ∈N} be countably many pairwise mutually singular laws on the observation sequence, F_n=σ(Z_1,…,Z_n), and G_n⊆F_n a common filtration. For each θ, let S^θ be a nonnegative P_θ-martingale in G, starting at 1. For every ε∈(0,1), must there exist nonnegative P_θ-martingales T^θ in the full filtration F, also starting at 1, such that liminf_{n→∞} inf_θ T_n^θ ≥ (1−ε) limsup_{n→∞} inf_θ S_n^θ, P_θ0-almost surely for every θ0? Or can a countably infinite null family prevent this asymptotic catch-up? The theorem proves the assertion for finite Θ.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Linear-horizon imitation from an optimal expert
author: Nived Rajaraman
source_title: Bridging Demonstrations and Decisions: Theory and Algorithms for Provable Imitation Learning
text: In a finite H-stage MDP, the initial distribution and possibly time-dependent transitions are known, rewards r_t(s,a)∈[0,1] are hidden, and N independent demonstrations come from a deterministic policy optimal for those rewards. Does Rajaraman’s Algorithm 5 attain expected imitation gap ~O(H/N), for fixed finite state/action sizes and uniformly in H,N? It chooses a demonstration-consistent deterministic policy minimizing worst-case regret over rewards for which some such consistent policy is optimal (equations 4.7–4.8). The question is the statistical guarantee of this specified minimax rule on arbitrary finite MDPs, not merely existence of an optimal expert or the solved three-state terminal-reward case.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Decidability of exact energy-parity values
author: Mohan Dantam; Richard Mayr
source_title: Approximating the Value of Energy-Parity Objectives in Simple Stochastic Games
location: §1 exact threshold question and §2 definitions; Dantam thesis §6.1 p. 120.
text: Given a finite turn-based perfect-information stochastic game with rational chance probabilities, integer edge rewards, state priorities, initial state s, integer credit c>0 and rational q∈(0,1), is it decidable whether sup_σ inf_τ Pr_s^{σ,τ}[c+Σ_{i<n}r(e_i)>0 for every n, and the least priority seen infinitely often is even]≥q? Strategies may use unbounded memory. Almost-sure winning and arbitrary additive approximation are already decidable; they do not decide equality at an exact threshold.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Finite memory for stochastic energy–mean-payoff control
author: Mohan Sai Teja Dantam
source_title: Strategy Complexity and Computational Complexity in Simple Stochastic Games with Multiple Objectives
location: §6.2, printed p. 122; §2.1 objective definitions and chapter 4.
text: In every finite turn-based two-player stochastic game with rational transitions and integer d-dimensional edge rewards, suppose Max has a strategy ensuring, against all Min strategies, with probability one that a given initial credit plus every prefix sum in coordinate 1 stays positive and liminf average reward is strictly positive in each coordinate 2,…,d. Must Max have a finite-memory almost-surely winning strategy? The corresponding MDP theorem is known; replacing strict positivity by nonnegativity is not the question.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Must compact mean-payoff–parity strategies randomize memory?
author: Mohan Dantam; Richard Mayr
source_title: Mean-Payoff-Parity and Lifting Strategies from MDPs to 2-Player Stochastic Games
location: §6, final open question; Theorem 5 and §2 finite-memory strategy definitions; thesis §6.3 p. 123.
text: For finite turn-based stochastic games with integer rewards and a parity coloring, can every almost-surely achievable conjunction of strictly positive liminf mean payoff and min-even parity be won using randomized actions but deterministic memory updates with polynomially many memory modes? In particular, does the known k-mode bound, k the number of distinct even priorities, survive that restriction? Current k-mode strategies randomize both actions and memory updates; arbitrary finite memory is not the unknown.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Optimal regret when recommendations reshape preferences
author: William Brown
source_title: Learning in the Presence of Adaptive Behavior
text: What is the optimal horizon exponent for bandit regret against EIRD when the preference functions are unknown? Fix n>k>1 and unknown L-Lipschitz (in ℓ₁) f_i:Δ(n)→[λ,1], λ≥k/n. A k-item menu K_t induces Pr(i_t=i)∝f_i(v_t) on K_t, v_t is the empirical distribution of previous choices after an arbitrary known initial v₁∈Δ(n), and only i_t and r_t(i_t) are observed. The sequence r₁,…,r_T∈[0,1]^n is fixed in advance, before menu/choice randomization. Let EIRD=∩_v conv{p(K,v):|K|=k}. Can max_{x∈EIRD}Σ_t r_t·x−EΣ_t r_t(i_t) have a rate strictly below ~O(T^{3/4})? Brown conjectures that ~O(√T) is impossible without knowing the preferences.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: When can one mediator implement a learning equilibrium?
author: Eshwar Ram Arunachaleswaran; Natalie Collina; Yishay Mansour; Mehryar Mohri; Jon Schneider; Balasubramanian Sivan
source_title: Swap Regret and Correlated Equilibria Beyond Normal-Form Games
location: §6, paragraph after Theorem 27 and Theorem 28; §3 profile-swap definition.
text: Characterize two-player games with convex polytope action sets X,Y and bilinear utilities for which every profile correlated equilibrium is the projection of a correlated equilibrium of the vertex normal-form game. A correlated profile is φ∈conv{x⊗y}. It is a profile CE when, separately for each player, φ admits a convex decomposition into product profiles where that player is best responding; the decompositions may differ. A vertex-game CE instead supplies one joint distribution on V(X)×V(Y), obedient conditional on each recommended vertex, whose tensor expectation is φ. Equality is proved if either action set is a simplex; general polytopes can separate.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Uniform equilibrium in finite multiplayer stochastic games
author: Game Theory Society Israeli Chapter, Open Problems, Problem 1. Abraham Neyman (problem-list contributor); Eilon Solan (primary partial-progress source). Undated live author problem list, accessed 2026-10-05; linked primary partial-progress paper 2017..
source_title: Game Theory Society Israeli Chapter, Open Problems, Problem 1. Abraham Neyman (problem-list contributor); Eilon Solan (primary partial-progress source). Undated live author problem list, accessed 2026-10-05; linked primary partial-progress paper 2017..
location: Problem 1; Solan, The Modified Stochastic Games, introduction and uniform-equilibrium definition.
text: Does every stochastic game with finitely many players, states and actions, perfect monitoring and bounded stage payoffs admit a uniform equilibrium payoff? Precisely, for every initial state seek a vector v such that for each ε>0 there are a strategy profile σ and N with |E_σ[n^{-1}Σ_{t=1}^n g_t^i]−v_i|≤ε for every player i and n≥N, while every unilateral history-dependent deviation gives expected n-stage average payoff at most v_i+ε. One profile must work for all sufficiently long horizons. The unresolved general multiplayer case is not the proved two-player or discounted stationary case.

subject: Games of Incomplete Information & Bayesian Games
title: Efficient optimal cheap-talk filters beyond binary actions
author: Itai Arieli; Ivan Geffner; Moshe Tennenholtz
source_title: Optimal Information Design in Sender-Receiver Cheap Talk Interactions
text: For one sender and at least three receiver actions, can a sender-optimal or receiver-optimal filter be computed in polynomial time from rational game data?

subject: Games of Incomplete Information & Bayesian Games
title: Efficient sender-optimal filters with multiple senders
author: Itai Arieli; Ivan Geffner; Moshe Tennenholtz
source_title: Optimal Information Design in Sender-Receiver Cheap Talk Interactions
text: For binary receiver actions and multiple senders, can a filter maximizing a specified sender’s best-equilibrium payoff be computed in polynomial time?

subject: Games of Incomplete Information & Bayesian Games
title: Polynomial-time persuasion with a privately informed binary receiver
author: I. Arda Vurankaya; Ufuk Topcu
source_title: Learning to Persuade Privately Informed Receivers
location: Remark following Lemma 6, offline-computation paragraph; program (3).
text: With μ, utilities and ψ rational and known, is an exact optimal φ computable in polynomial input-size time?

subject: Games of Incomplete Information & Bayesian Games
title: Sharp regret for learning an unknown private information channel
author: I. Arda Vurankaya; Ufuk Topcu
source_title: Learning to Persuade Privately Informed Receivers
text: With ψ unknown and |R| known, determine minimax T-dependence of regret TV*−EΣ_tV(φ_t,ψ), V*=max_φV(φ,ψ): is ~O(T^{3/4}) improvable? Assume d_min=min_θ|u^R(a₀,θ)−u^R(a₁,θ)|>0, distinct H_r={p:Σ_θp_θψ(r|θ)[u^R(a₀,θ)−u^R(a₁,θ)]=0} after merging proportional likelihoods, and known γ>0 with ∀ action-pattern cell C ∃μ_C∈C ∀r: |n_rᵀμ_C|≥γ; n_r is H_r’s unit normal.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Is √N the price of exact non-myopic truthfulness?
author: Junpei Komiyama; Nishant A. Mehta; Ali Mortazavi
source_title: No-Regret Incentive-Compatible Online Learning under Exact Truthfulness with Non-Myopic Experts
text: With all reports observed, must every Online IC-BI mechanism incur worst-case expected belief regret Ω(√(NT))? The upper bound is O(√(NT) log T).

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Is T^(2/3) unavoidable for truthful bandit forecasting?
author: Junpei Komiyama; Nishant A. Mehta; Ali Mortazavi
source_title: No-Regret Incentive-Compatible Online Learning under Exact Truthfulness with Non-Myopic Experts
location: §1 bandit conjecture; §4.2 after Theorem 4; §2 Definition 6; §6 extra-observation discussion.
text: With only the selected expert’s report observed, is ~O(T^{2/3}N^{1/3}) minimax for Bandit Online IC-BI? Is the T^{2/3} exponent necessary for fixed N? A second report per round changes the model.

subject: Mechanism Design, Implementation & Auctions
title: Exact truthfulness versus regret with noisy strategic features
author: Thomas Kleine Buening; Aadirupa Saha; Christos Dimitrakakis; Haifeng Xu
source_title: Strategic Linear Contextual Bandits
location: §3.3 final paragraph; Appendix A final conjecture; §3 protocol and regularity assumptions.
text: Can a no-payment algorithm achieve o(T) worst-case regret while truthful reporting is an exact Nash equilibrium in the strategic linear contextual-bandit model with unknown θ* and noisy rewards? K persistent arms privately see true unit-bounded contexts x*_{t,i}, report contexts strategically, and maximize expected total selections. The learner observes only reports and the selected reward ⟨θ*,x*_{t,i_t}⟩+η_t, with zero-mean sub-Gaussian noise. Nature may choose contexts adversarially; reward differences are bounded and the nonzero optimality gap is constant. The conjecture rules out exact truthfulness plus no regret, not approximate Nash truthfulness.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Sharp representation size for surrogate-MDP planning
author: Sultan J. Majeed; Marcus Hutter
source_title: Reducing Planning Complexity of General Reinforcement Learning with Non-Markovian Abstractions
text: For every history-dependent environment with A≥2 actions, rewards in [0,1], discount γ∈[0.99,1), and 0<ε<1, determine the smallest worst-case number of abstract states after the paper’s fixed-length binary action sequentialization that guarantees (1−γ) sup_h(V*(h)−V^π(h))≤ε for every uplifted optimal policy of every surrogate MDP. Is the proved O(ε⁻¹(1−γ)⁻²⌈log₂A⌉³) upper bound tight? Surrogates average rewards and abstract transitions over histories in each fiber using arbitrary state-action-dependent dispersion laws.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Deciding exact probability equivalence of recursive language sensors
author: Colin de la Higuera; James Scicluna; Mark-Jan Nederhof
source_title: On the Computation of Distances for Probabilistic Context-Free Grammars
text: Is there an algorithm deciding, for two finite consistent probabilistic context-free grammars G₁,G₂ over the same finite alphabet with effectively encoded rational rule probabilities, whether P_G₁(w)=P_G₂(w) for every finite word w? Word probability sums all leftmost-derivation probabilities. Keep unrestricted ambiguity; equality of support languages and equality of individual derivation weights are different problems.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Deciding the unresolved side of a model-distance threshold
author: Stefan Kiefer
source_title: On Computing the Total Variation Distance of Hidden Markov Models
text: For a rational finite labelled Markov chain that terminates almost surely, rational initial laws P,Q, and rational τ∈(0,1), is d_TV(P,Q)≥τ decidable? Here d_TV=sup_E|P(E)−Q(E)| over finite-word events. Equivalently ask d_TV<τ; d_TV>τ is already undecidable. The same ≥ question remains open for infinite-word chains.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Polynomial-space approximation for infinite observation-trace distance
author: Stefan Kiefer
source_title: On Computing the Total Variation Distance of Hidden Markov Models
text: Can d_TV(P,Q) for rational finite labelled Markov chains generating infinite words be approximated within binary-encoded ε>0 using polynomial workspace in input bit length? P,Q are rational initial laws; events are measurable subsets of infinite traces. Arbitrary-precision computability is known, but the PSPACE bound holds only for finite-word chains.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Learning low-rank sequence laws without a fidelity assumption
author: Sham M. Kakade; Akshay Krishnamurthy; Gaurav Mahajan; Cyril Zhang
source_title: Learning Hidden Markov Models Using Conditional Samples
text: Let P be a distribution on O^T such that every prefix–future matrix [P(f|h)]_{f∈O^{≤T−t},h∈O^t} has rank≤r. A query selects a prefix h and receives an independent suffix from P(·|h), including a fixed consistent oracle convention for zero-probability prefixes. Can P be learned to total-variation error ε with confidence 1−δ in time and oracle calls polynomial in r,T,|O|,1/ε,log(1/δ), outputting an efficiently evaluable representation, without any lower bound on the paper’s spectral fidelity parameter?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Completeness of countable probabilistic I/O rewriting
author: Nathan Bowler; Sergey Goncharov; Paul Blain Levy
source_title: Probabilistic Strategies: Definability and the Tensor Completeness Problem
text: For an arbitrary I/O signature S, allowing operations with infinite response arities, consider well-founded programs built from requests Req k?(M_i) and countable probabilistic choice Σ_n p_nM_n, with p_n≥0 and Σ_np_n=1. Does equality of their probabilistic trace strategies imply equality in the least congruence generated by the ω-convex laws and commutation of each request with probabilistic choice? This is the tensor-completeness problem when both choice and the I/O signature are infinitary. Do not add a cancellation rule, under which completeness is already proved.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Sharp dimension cost of learning an ideal point from noiseless preferences
author: Marc Jourdan; Gizem Yüce; Nicolas Flammarion
source_title: Learning Parametric Distributions from Samples and Preferences
location: §5, “Dimensionality gap”; Theorems 4.8 and 5.3; Appendix F, Gaussian specialization.
text: Observe n independent triples (X_i,Y_i,Z_i), with X_i,Y_i independently N(θ,I_d), θ∈Θ=[−1,1]^d, and Z_i=sign(log p_θ(X_i)−log p_θ(Y_i)). Determine the sharp dimension dependence of inf_{θ̂} sup_θ E_θ||θ̂−θ||_2 in the high-sample regime. For isotropic Gaussians the source leaves a √d gap, up to logarithms, between Ω(d/n) and Õ(d^{3/2}/n) in the regime n≫d², with logarithmic terms retained in the upper bound. The labels are deterministic; this is not the stochastic Bradley–Terry feedback model.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Generic identification of more than two latent preference types
author: Xiaomin Zhang; Xucheng Zhang; Po-Ling Loh; Yingyu Liang
source_title: On the Identifiability of Mixtures of Ranking Models
location: §§2 and 4 (BTL model); §5 Conclusion and discussion, extension beyond two components.
text: For k≥3 and n items, let π_h>0, ∑_{h=1}^k π_h=1, and a_hi>0 with a_h1=1. Observe all pairwise probabilities P_ij=∑_{h=1}^k π_h a_hi/(a_hi+a_hj), i<j, but no component labels or linked multi-comparison records. Characterize the pairs (n,k) for which this parameter map is generically injective up to simultaneous permutation of the k components: outside a Lebesgue-null parameter set, are its fibers precisely those label permutations? The nontrivial question is beyond the known two-component result and beyond parameter-count-impossible regimes.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Optimal computation overhead for uncertain two-objective tradeoffs
author: Constantinos Daskalakis; Ilias Diakonikolas; Mihalis Yannakakis
source_title: How Good is the Chord Algorithm?
location: §2.1 (oracle and OPT), Theorem 2.2 and §3.1.2 (bounds), §5 (explicit open question).
text: Let an unknown feasible objective set I⊆[2^{−m},2^m]^2 be accessible only through exact Comb(λ), which returns a point minimizing y+λx (λ≥0, including λ=∞). An ε-convex Pareto set S⊆I satisfies: every p∈I has q∈conv(S) with q≤(1+ε)p coordinatewise. Let OPT_ε(I) be its minimum cardinality. What is the optimal worst-case ratio sup_I E[N_A(I,ε)]/OPT_ε(I) over adaptive oracle algorithms that always output such a set? Close the gap between Ω(log m+log log(1/ε)) for every algorithm and O((m+log(1/ε))/(log m+log log(1/ε))) achieved by Chord.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Construct optimal multi-symbol sequence-model compression
author: Clara Lacroce; Prakash Panangaden; Guillaume Rabusseau
source_title: Towards an AAK Theory Approach to Approximate Minimization in the Multi-Letter Case
text: For a minimal n-state real weighted finite automaton computing an absolutely summable series f:Σ*→R, |Σ|≥2, and k<n, give a constructive solution of the source’s optimal k-state approximation problem in the Hankel operator norm: minimize ||H_f−H_g||op over series g realizable with at most k states, where H_f(u,v)=f(uv). The unresolved step is constructive noncommutative AAK approximation, not ordinary unconstrained matrix truncation.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Decide bounded likelihood ratios with polynomially many interpretations
author: Dmitry Chistikov; Stefan Kiefer; Andrzej S. Murawski; David Purser
source_title: The Big-O Problem
text: Is big-O decidable when both automata are polynomially ambiguous: at most p(|w|) accepting paths per word for some polynomial p, without a fixed degree bound?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Unconditional bounded-ratio testing on structured sequence supports
author: Dmitry Chistikov; Stefan Kiefer; Andrzej S. Murawski; David Purser
source_title: The Big-O Problem
text: Is big-O unconditionally decidable when both support languages lie in w₁*···w_m* for finite words w_i, with arbitrary ambiguity? Known decidability assumes Schanuel’s conjecture; unary complexity is coNP-complete.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Sharp cost of exact register compression for weighted sensors
author: Yahia Idriss Benalioua; Nathan Lhote; Pierre-Alain Reynier
source_title: Minimizing Cost Register Automata over a Field
text: What is the tight complexity of register minimization for rational linear cost-register automata? Given a rational WFA computing f and k, decide whether some finite-control deterministic CRA computes exactly f on every word using at most k rational registers, simultaneous linear register updates, and state-dependent linear output. The number of control states is unrestricted.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Tight complexity of deterministic minimum-cost interpretation
author: Shaull Almagor; Guy Arbel; Sarai Sheinvald
source_title: A Complexity Bound for Determinisation of Min-Plus Weighted Automata
text: Determine the tight complexity of deciding whether a finite min-plus WFA with integer edge weights has an equivalent deterministic WFA on all finite words. A word’s value is the minimum total edge cost among its runs; no run gives +∞. Use the source’s single-initial-state, all-states-accepting convention; equivalent standard variants are inter-reducible.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Compute linear closures of recursively constrained sensor updates
author: Yahia-Idriss Benalioua; Nathan Lhote; Pierre-Alain Reynier
source_title: Is the linear Zariski closure of a context-free language of matrices computable?
location: Talk abstract; Questions slides, PDF pp. 33–38.
text: Given a context-free grammar for L⊆Σ* and rational d×d matrices M_a for a∈Σ, is the linear Zariski closure of {M_{a₁}···M_{a_t}:a₁···a_t∈L} effectively computable? The required output is a finite union of rational vector subspaces, represented by bases, equal to the smallest such finite union containing these matrices. Matrices need not be invertible.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Compute a transcript within the quasipolynomial sample budget
author: Arnav Burudgunte; Paul Valiant; Hongao Wang
source_title: Quasipolynomial Trace Reconstruction
location: §1, Run time vs. sample complexity; Definition 2; Theorem 43.
text: For fixed p∈(0,1), can worst-case exact deletion-trace reconstruction achieve quasipolynomial sample size and runtime, succeeding with probability≥2/3 for every n-bit source? Full reconstruction is required, not pairwise distinguishing.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Polylogarithmic observations for typical exact transcript recovery
author: Ittai Rubinstein
source_title: Average-Case to (Shifted) Worst-Case Reduction for the Trace Reconstruction Problem
text: For every fixed deletion probability δ∈(0,1), can a uniformly random unknown X∈{0,1}^n be reconstructed exactly from (log n)^{Oδ(1)} independent deletion traces, with success probability 1−o_n(1) over X and the channel? No polynomial-time condition is added.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Accuracy-scalable reconstruction under insertions and deletions
author: Diptarka Chakraborty; Debarati Das; Robert Krauthgamer
source_title: Approximate Trace Reconstruction via Median String (In Average-Case)
text: In the source’s insertion–deletion channel R_p, at each step copy the current input bit with probability 1−p, delete it with probability p/2, or insert a uniform random bit with probability p/2 without advancing. For fixed sufficiently small p>0 and uniform S∈{0,1}^n, can its near-linear-time reconstruction theorem be extended to edit error O(εpn), for arbitrary ε>0, using poly(1/ε) traces and success probability at least 1−1/n? Runtime is near-linear in n for fixed p,ε.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Reconstruct probability sequences on a fixed finite grid
author: Joey Rivkin; Gregory Valiant; Paul Valiant
source_title: A Generalized Trace Reconstruction Problem: Recovering a String of Probabilities
text: In generalized trace reconstruction, a hidden vector p∈[0,1]^n first emits independent Bernoulli(p_i) bits, then each bit is deleted with fixed probability δ∈(0,1). If all p_i lie in {0,1/k,…,1}, what is the minimax number of traces for recovering p to ℓ∞ error below 1/(2k), with probability at least 2/3? In particular, can superpolynomial-in-n lower bounds persist for a fixed k≥2?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Faster recovery of a sparse distribution of latent messages
author: Shyam Narayanan
source_title: Improved Algorithms for Population Recovery from the Deletion Channel
text: For fixed retention p∈(0,1) and fixed TV accuracy ε∈(0,1/2), can a distribution D supported on at most ℓ unknown n-bit strings be learned to TV error ε, with success at least 2/3, using both exp(~O(n^(1/5) poly(ℓ))) traces and time? A trace first samples x∼D and then independently deletes bits of x; component labels and repeat observations of a chosen component are unavailable.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Sharp decision fidelity from one deleted observation
author: Xi Chen; Anindya De; Chin Ho Lee; Rocco A. Servedio; Sandip Sinha
source_title: Approximate Trace Reconstruction from a Single Trace
text: Let A receive n and one δ-deletion trace of x, and output an n-bit estimate. Determine the sharp asymptotic values of L_worst(δ,n)/n and L_avg(δ,n)/n, where L_worst(δ,n)=sup_A inf_x E[LCS(A(trace,n),x)] and L_avg(δ,n)=sup_A E_{X uniform}[LCS(A(trace,n),X)] for fixed δ, already at δ=0.1 or 0.9. Here LCS denotes longest-common-subsequence length, and A is deterministic, as in the source definitions.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Are coordinate summaries optimal through seven bits?
author: Hessam Mahdavifar; Ahmad Beirami
source_title: The Most Informative Bit and Beyond: A Proof of the Courtade–Kumar Conjecture and Multibit Extensions
text: Let X be uniform on F₂^n and Y=X⊕Z with independent Bernoulli(p) noise bits, 0≤p≤1/2. For every 2≤k≤7, n≥k and deterministic f:F₂^n→F₂^k, must I(f(X);Y)≤k(1−h₂(p))? No balance or surjectivity assumption is imposed on f; h₂ is binary entropy in bits.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Sharp Hellinger information from a noisy Boolean sensor
author: Venkat Anantharam; Andrej Bogdanov; Amit Chakrabarti; T. S. Jayram; Chandra Nair
source_title: A conjecture regarding optimality of the dictator function under Hellinger distance
text: For uniform X∈{−1,1}^n, let Y_i=X_i Z_i with independent signs of mean ρ∈[−1,1]. For every f:{−1,1}^n→{−1,1}, is sqrt(1−(E f(X))²)−E[sqrt(1−(E[f(X)|Y])²)]≤1−sqrt(1−ρ²)? The question conditions on the full noisy vector Y and allows unbalanced f.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Minimal square-root posterior uncertainty for balanced features
author: Lei Yu
source_title: Local Optimality of Dictator Functions with Applications to Courtade–Kumar and Li–Médard Conjectures
text: For uniform X∈{−1,1}^n, balanced f:{−1,1}^n→{0,1}, and 0≤ρ≤1, define Tρf(x)=E[f(Y)|X=x] under independent coordinate noise of correlation ρ. Must E[sqrt(Tρf(X))]≥[sqrt((1+ρ)/2)+sqrt((1−ρ)/2)]/2? This is the asymmetric one-half-stability conjecture; its symmetric square-root counterpart is grouped with it, not counted separately.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Subquadratic adaptive sampling for replicable multi-hypothesis testing
author: Max Hopkins; Russell Impagliazzo; Daniel Kane; Sihan Liu; Christopher Ye
source_title: Replicability in High Dimensional Statistics
text: For constants 0<p₀<q₀<1 and 0<δ<ρ<1/10, can an adaptive learner use o(N²) expected total coin flips uniformly over N biases p_i, returning O with {i:p_i≥q₀}⊆O⊆{i:p_i>p₀} with probability≥1−δ? Can it achieve O(N^(2−c)) for constant c>0? Replicability requires identical O on independent runs sharing randomness with probability≥1−ρ, including gap biases.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Efficient near-isoperimetric tilings for replicable estimation
author: Max Hopkins; Russell Impagliazzo; Daniel Kane; Sihan Liu; Christopher Ye
source_title: Replicability in High Dimensional Statistics
text: Does R^N admit, uniformly in N, a tiling with every cell inside a radius-one Euclidean ball and surface-area/volume ratio O(N), with a membership oracle returning the containing cell with probability≥2/3 in polynomial input-bit complexity? Is even O(N^(3/2−c)) achievable for universal c>0? Existence without efficient membership is known.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Sharp sample complexity of replicable independence testing
author: Ilias Diakonikolas; Jingyi Gao; Daniel Kane; Sihan Liu; Christopher Ye
source_title: Replicable Distribution Testing
text: For n1≥n2≥2 and ε,ρ∈(0,1/4), determine the minimax number of iid samples from p on [n1]×[n2] needed to distinguish p=p1⊗p2 from inf_{q product}TV(p,q)≥ε with success probability≥2/3, while Pr[A(S;r)=A(S′;r)]≥1−ρ for every p, for independent equal-size samples S,S′ and shared seed r. Is the proved upper bound Õ(n1^(2/3)n2^(1/3)/(ρ^(2/3)ε^(4/3))+√(n1n2)/(ρε²)+1/(ε²ρ²)) optimal up to logarithms?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: A half-probability lower tail for sampling without replacement
author: Guy Blanc
source_title: Subsampling Suffices for Adaptive Data Analysis
text: For every deterministic a∈[0,1]^N and 1≤n<N, let I be a uniform n-element subset of [N] and X=Σ_{i∈I}a_i. Must Pr[X>E X−1]≥1/2? Blanc proves the weaker universal constant (2√3−3)/13 and explicitly conjectures 1/2. The strict inequality and additive 1 are part of the target.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Complexity of a self-consistent three-level source ranking
author: Paolo Liberatore
source_title: Belief Integration and Source Reliability Assessment
text: For explicitly represented sources in the shared setup, what is the complexity of deciding whether any strongly stable tripartition exists?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Complexity of inference from strongly stable source integrations
author: Paolo Liberatore
source_title: Belief Integration and Source Reliability Assessment
text: Given those sources and φ, what is the complexity of deciding whether every maxcon of every strongly stable tripartition entails φ? Universal quantification is vacuously true if no such tripartition exists.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Minimax regret with very few delayed-evidence tracking slots
author: Alexander Ryabchenko; Idan Attias; Daniel M. Roy
source_title: Capacity-Constrained Online Learning with Delays: Scheduling Frameworks and Regret Trade-offs
text: In the clairvoyant capacity-C delayed bandit game, an oblivious adversary fixes loss vectors ℓ_t∈[0,1]^K and integer delays 0≤d_t≤T; d_t is revealed before choosing action A_t. At most C round indices can be tracked simultaneously, and ℓ_t(A_t) is received at t+d_t only if t remains tracked; At each round add the current index if space is available, receive expiring feedback, and then optionally preempt tracked indices, irrevocably losing their feedback. Determine the minimax expected regret EΣ_tℓ_t(A_t)−min_iΣ_tℓ_t(i) as a joint function of T,K,C and D=Σ_td_t in the small-capacity regime C=o(log T). The matched logarithmic-capacity and fixed-delay cases are excluded.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Total-delay rather than peak-backlog penalties in capacity-limited bandit optimization
author: Alexander Ryabchenko; Idan Attias; Daniel M. Roy
source_title: Capacity-Constrained Online Convex Optimization with Delayed Feedback
text: In capacity-constrained bandit convex optimization on K⊂R^k with rB_k⊂K⊂RB_k, diameter D_K, G-Lipschitz convex losses |f_t|≤M and oblivious delays d_t, can the √(Tσ_max) delay term in Theorem 5.2 be replaced by √(d_tot), while retaining its T^(3/4)(1+σ_max/C)^(1/4)√(νk) term, up to constants/logarithms, or is there a capacity-induced separation? Here C≥lnT+1, d_tot=Σd_t, σ_max is maximum pending-round backlog, ν=M/(Gr). Use the source’s clairvoyant or semi-clairvoyant preemptive tracking protocol; untracked feedback is lost.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: A greatest latent temporal-causal graph under E-separation
author: Georg Manten; Cecilia Casolo; Søren Wengel Mogensen; Niki Kilbertus
source_title: An Asymmetric Independence Model for Causal Discovery on Path Spaces
text: For every finite directed mixed graph G, possibly cyclic and with the source’s allowed self-loops, does its E-separation Markov-equivalence class contain a greatest graph under inclusion of both directed and bidirected edges? E-separation means A0 is σ-separated from B1 given C0∪(C1\B1) in the lifted graph with two copies V0,V1, each u→v lifted to u0→v0,u0→v1,u1→v1 and each u↔v lifted to all four cross-copy bidirected edges. Preserve σ-separation’s strongly-connected-component exception for conditioned noncolliders, not d-separation.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Pointwise rate of the unrestricted bivariate current-status MLE
author: Piet Groeneboom
source_title: The bivariate current status model
text: Observe iid (T_i,U_i,Δ_i1,Δ_i2), where Δ_i1=1{X_i≤T_i}, Δ_i2=1{Y_i≤U_i}, and (X_i,Y_i) is independent of (T_i,U_i). On [0,1]², assume the latent CDF F0 and observation CDF G are twice continuously differentiable near an interior(t,u), with positive observation density g(t,u). Does the unrestricted nonparametric likelihood maximizer F̂_n satisfy F̂_n(t,u)−F0(t,u)=O_P(n^(−1/3)), or what is its sharp local rate, including any logarithmic factor? This is not the already-analyzed plug-in or sieve estimator.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Local asymptotics of the nonseparated interval-censoring MLE
author: Piet Groeneboom
source_title: Nonparametric Least Squares Estimators for Interval Censoring
text: For iid independent latent event times X_i∼F0 and inspection pairs T_i<U_i, observe which of X_i≤T_i, T_i<X_i≤U_i, X_i>U_i occurs. At interior t0 assume F0 has continuous positive density f0(t0), and the inspection density h(t,u) extends continuously to the diagonal near(t0,t0) with h(t0,t0)>0 and 0<F0(t0)<1. Determine the correct pointwise normalization and nondegenerate limiting law of the unrestricted MLE F̂_n(t0)−F0(t0) when inspection intervals can be arbitrarily short. The familiar proposed (n log n)^(1/3) Chernoff law is not assumed.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Universality with arbitrary stationary-ergodic side information
author: Alankrita Bhatt; J. Jon Ryu; Young-Han Kim
source_title: On Universal Portfolios with Continuous Side Information
text: Fix m,S≥2 and a class G of state maps g:Z→[S] with finite Natarajan dimension. At time t observe Z_t before choosing b_t∈Δ_m and then see arbitrary nonzero nonnegative return vector x_t. With W_n(b)=∏_t〈b_t,x_t〉, can a causal strategy achieve E[sup_{g∈G,θ1:S∈Δ_m}log(W_n((θ_{g(Z_t)})_t)/W_n(b))]=o(n) for every stationary ergodic Z process, without the extra Eρ_{G×G}(Z^n)=o(n/log²n) condition? Here ρ_H= sup_{h∈H}|Σ_t(h(Z_t)−Eh(Z_t))| and H={1{g≠g′}:g,g′∈G}. Returns may depend on Z; they need not be stationary.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Chernoff local limit for monotone-kernel deconvolution MLEs
author: Piet Groeneboom
source_title: Nonparametric (smoothed) likelihood and integral equations
text: Observe iid Z=X+Y with independent X∼F0 supported on[0,S0] and known noise density g on[0,Sg]. Assume F0 continuous, F0(S0)=1, F0 continuously differentiable near t0∈(0,S0), f0(t0)>0; g is bounded, decreasing, continuous on[0,∞), and has a bounded Lipschitz derivative on(0,Sg). Write h0=g∗F0, assume h0(t0)>0, and let F̂_n maximize the convolution likelihood over CDFs. Does n^(1/3)[2g(0)²/(f0(t0)h0(t0))]^(1/3)(F̂_n(t0)−F0(t0)) converge to 2Z_C, where Z_C=argmax_s{W(s)−s²} for two-sided standard Brownian motion?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Constant-factor testable learning of general halfspaces
author: Ilias Diakonikolas; Daniel M. Kane; Sihan Liu; Nikos Zarifis
source_title: Testable Learning of General Halfspaces with Adversarial Label Noise
location: Definition 1, Theorem 2, Remark 14, pp. 2–3,13; Liu thesis §1.3 Remark 1.3.2 p. 23.
text: For C={x↦sign(w·x−t):w∈R^d,t∈R}, is there a tester-learner using time and samples polynomial in d,1/ε,log(1/δ), which accepts with probability≥1−δ whenever D_X=N(0,I_d), and for every joint distribution D on R^d×{−1,1} has probability≤δ of accepting and outputting h with err_D(h)>C_0 opt_D(C)+ε, for a universal constant C_0? Labels are arbitrary and the threshold t need not vanish. The known error is Õ(√opt)+ε.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: The degree–accuracy cost of testable polynomial classifiers
author: Lucas Slot; Stefan Tiegel; Manuel Wiedmer
source_title: Testably Learning Polynomial Threshold Functions
location: §1.2 Limitations p. 4; Theorem 19; official NeurIPS 2024 presentation slide 5.
text: Determine the sharp computational dependence on degree d and excess error ε for testably learning {sign(p):deg p≤d} on R^n with standard-Gaussian completeness and error opt+ε. Soundness must hold for arbitrary joint laws whenever the test accepts. Is the large exponent in the known n^{Õ_d(ε^{−4d·7^d})} upper bound necessary, or can it approach ordinary agnostic learning? Preserve computational-model qualifications: the cited n^{Ω(d²/ε²)} lower bound is an SQ lower bound, not an unconditional time lower bound.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Can membership queries speed up testable agnostic learning?
author: Jane Lange; Mingda Qiao
source_title: Limitations of Membership Queries in Testable Learning
location: §1.4.1 Conjecture 6 p. 91:5; §2.3 Definition 12; arXiv full version §1.4.1 Conjecture 1.
text: Can every t-time agnostic tester-learner with membership queries be replaced by a sample-only tester-learner running in poly(t) time, for the same Boolean class C, target distribution D and opt+ε error? Both must accept under D and otherwise either reject or return a near-optimal hypothesis. Sampled and queried labels come from the same fixed Boolean function. Use the source’s learning/output convention.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Sharp sample complexity of decision-relevant model diagnostics
author: Mark Bun; Rathin Desai; Renato Ferreira Pinto Jr.
source_title: Testing Distributions Against Bounded Distinguishers
text: Given a known reference law P₀ on X, a specified Boolean class F⊆{0,1}^X, iid sample access to unknown P, and ε>0, characterize the minimax samples required to distinguish P=P₀ from sup_{f∈F}|E_P f−E_{P₀}f|>ε with probability at least 2/3. Close the paper’s quadratic gap in its Rademacher-complexity characterization, jointly in F,P₀,ε; the tester has no computational restriction in this sample-complexity question.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Class-size dependence with abstention-only feedback
author: Aditya Gangrade; Anil Kag; Ashok Cutkosky; Venkatesh Saligrama
source_title: Online Selective Classification with Limited Feedback
text: Determine the sharp joint(T,N) Pareto frontier of(E[M],E[A−A*₀]). Can the optimal fixed-N exponents T^μ and T^{1−μ} retain only logarithmic dependence on N?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The noisy-comparator frontier for selective fallback
author: Aditya Gangrade; Anil Kag; Ashok Cutkosky; Venkatesh Saligrama
source_title: Online Selective Classification with Limited Feedback
location: §7 Discussion pp. 10–12, paragraph beginning “A practically relevant…”.
text: For supplied ε, determine the frontier of(E[M]−εT,E[A−A*_{ε}]); also determine what adaptation is possible when the comparator’s error allowance is unknown.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Does prequential credal randomness have a precise explanation?
author: Floris Persiau
source_title: Imprecise Probabilities in Algorithmic Randomness
location: Conclusion, Future work pp. 204–205; Definitions 16.1,17.6 pp. 149,153; compare Theorem 20.1 and Corollary 20.3 pp. 193–194.
text: For rational credal polytopes C_n, is game-randomness of(C₁,x₁,…) equivalent to game-randomness of some compatible precise path(p₁,x₁,…), with rational p_n∈C_n? Neither forecast sequence need be computable.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Can one precise model preserve every Church-random path?
author: Floris Persiau
source_title: Imprecise Probabilities in Algorithmic Randomness
location: Conclusion Future work p. 205; Theorem 20.1 p. 193; Definition 12.1 p. 102 and Definition 11.2 p. 89.
text: For R∈{CH,weak CH}, does every φ admit one compatible, possibly noncomputable p with Ω_R(p)=Ω_R(φ), where Ω_R is the set of R-random paths?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Do betting audits require a wider interval than frequency audits?
author: Floris Persiau; Gert de Cooman; Jasper De Bock
source_title: A comparative study of the smallest probability intervals for which a binary sequence is random
location: §7 paragraph before §8, p. 20, Figure 4; Definitions 2–6; Proposition 5–6.
text: Does there exist a binary path ω with I_CH(ω) strictly contained in I_C(ω)? Here I_R(ω) is the intersection of all closed probability intervals I⊆[0,1] for which ω is R-random; CH denotes Church randomness and C computable randomness. The CH intersection is attained, while C is interpreted through almost randomness: randomness for every strict enlargement [inf I−ε₁,sup I+ε₂]∩[0,1]. The known distinction between being C-random and merely almost C-random at the same interval is not a separation of the intervals.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Does fixed-level detection imply eventual correct model choice?
author: Daniil Ryabko
source_title: Asymptotic Nonparametric Statistical Analysis of Stationary Time Series
location: §5.7.1 Conjecture 5.2 p. 71, second implication; Definitions 5.2–5.3 pp. 54–55.
text: Does asymmetric consistency imply existence of a strongly asymptotically consistent test? No cross-α compatibility, mixing rate or computability is assumed.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Which dependent model classes are statistically distinguishable?
author: Daniil Ryabko
source_title: Asymptotic Nonparametric Statistical Analysis of Stationary Time Series
text: Characterize exactly which pairs(H₀,H₁) admit each of these three consistency notions, allowing H₁ to differ from the complement of H₀. The asymmetric complement case is already characterized.

subject: Bayesian Inference
title: Sharp Bayesian prediction overhead
author: Daniil Ryabko
source_title: On Asymptotic and Finite-Time Optimality of Bayesian Predictors
text: Is Θ(log n) the sharp universal overhead g(n) such that every C,ρ admit one discrete mixture ν over C with L_n(μ,ν)≤L_n(μ,ρ)+g(n) for all μ∈C,n? Known upper:8log₂n+O(loglog n); lower: merely divergent.

subject: Bayesian Inference
title: Bayesian regret under misspecification
author: Daniil Ryabko
source_title: On Asymptotic and Finite-Time Optimality of Bayesian Predictors
text: Characterize C for which a Bayesian predictor attains U_C, especially when U_C=0 is attainable without the mixture restriction.

subject: Bayesian Inference
title: Asymptotic predictive minimax equality
author: Daniil Ryabko
source_title: On Asymptotic and Finite-Time Optimality of Bayesian Predictors
text: Must inf_ρ sup_{W∈C*}E_W L̄(μ,ρ)=sup_{W∈C*}inf_ρ E_W L̄(μ,ρ) hold for every C? An upper-value minimizer exists.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Logarithmic prediction mistakes with sublinear label purchases
author: Steve Hanneke; Liu Yang
source_title: Toward a General Theory of Online Selective Sampling: Trading Off Mistakes and Queries
text: For every measurable binary class H of finite VC dimension, does one algorithm depending only on H attain expected cumulative mistakes O(log T) and expected label requests o(T), for every distribution P and target f*∈H? Covariates are i.i.d. P. Each prediction and query decision uses only current/past covariates, earlier requested labels and independent randomness. The current label is unavailable before prediction. Constants may depend on H,P,f*; these are distribution-dependent guarantees.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Efficient optimal exploration when several policies are good enough
author: Cyrille Kone; Kevin Jamieson
source_title: Optimal Posterior Sampling for Policy Identification in Tabular Markov Decision Processes
location: Appendix L, Theorem 47 and after (L.1), pp. 66–68.
text: In the finite tabular H-horizon episodic MDP model, transitions are unknown, rewards are N(μ(s,a,h),1) with μ∈(0,1), the initial state is fixed, and the optimal policy is unique. For ε>0, find an efficient sampling rule converging to the optimal exploration allocation without enumerating A^(SH) policies. The target is C_ε(M)=[max_{π∈Π*_ε(M)} max_{w∈Ω_M} inf_{M′:M≪M′,π∉Π*_ε(M′)} Σ_{s,a,h}w_h(s,a)KL(M,M′)_{s,a,h}]^(−1), where Π*_ε denotes ε-optimal Markov policies and Ω_M feasible episode occupancies. With a separately valid δ-calibrated stopping rule, require limsup_{δ↓0}E_Mτ_δ/log(1/δ)≤C_ε(M). Conditional posterior sampling is not assumed free.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Sharp item dependence for strongly monotone semi-bandit learning
author: Arpit Agarwal; Rohan Ghuge; Viswanath Nagarajan; Zhengjia Zhuo
source_title: Semi-Bandit Learning for Monotone Stochastic Optimization
text: With n independent item laws of support size ≤k, fresh product draws each round, 0≤f≤f_max and an exact offline oracle, determine sharp T-round semi-bandit regret for strongly up-monotone stochastic minimization. Policies adaptively probe and observe only probed outcomes. Strong up-monotonicity means E_E f(σ_D,X)≤OPT(D) whenever E stochastically dominates D and σ_D is D-optimal. Can the √n improvement for Pandora/prophet problems extend generally beyond Õ(n(√(kT)+k)f_max)? Keep k and f_max dependence explicit.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Efficient dependent-data prediction without observing update sites
author: Sasha Voitovych; Abhishek Shetty; Noah Golowich; Alexander Rakhlin
source_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
location: Appendix B, Theorem B.1 and following paragraph, pp. 22–23.
text: Let X_t∈{0,1}^n follow unknown Ising Glauber dynamics: choose I_t uniformly from[n], resample coordinate I_t as Bernoulli(σ(Σ_{j≠I_t}A_{I_tj}X_{t−1,j}+h_{I_t})), and leave all other coordinates fixed, where σ is logistic, A is symmetric with zero diagonal, and every free coefficient is in[−B,B], B≥1. X_0 is known. Can an algorithm observing X_t but not I_t, with an agnostic ERM oracle for any binary VC-d class F, run in poly(n,T,B) time and retain EReg_T(F)≲√(dT)(1+n²√log(BTn))? Labels are Y_t=f*(X_t) for an arbitrary fixed f*, possibly outside F, and are revealed after prediction.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Efficient adaptive rule verification
author: Lisa Hellerstein; Devorah Kletenik; Naifeng Liu; R. Teal Witter
source_title: Adaptivity Gaps for the Stochastic Boolean Function Evaluation Problem
text: For arbitrary-depth monotone read-once AND/OR formulas, is a constant-factor or O(log n)-approximation to OPT_A achievable in polynomial or pseudo-polynomial time?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Unbiased read-once adaptivity advantage
author: Lisa Hellerstein; Devorah Kletenik; Naifeng Liu; R. Teal Witter
source_title: Adaptivity Gaps for the Stochastic Boolean Function Evaluation Problem
text: When c_i=1 and p_i=1/2, does every η>0 admit arbitrarily large n and a monotone read-once formula with OPT_N/OPT_A=Ω_η(n^(1−η))?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Positive-rule adaptivity advantage
author: Lisa Hellerstein; Devorah Kletenik; Naifeng Liu; R. Teal Witter
source_title: Adaptivity Gaps for the Stochastic Boolean Function Evaluation Problem
text: When c_i=1 and p_i=1/2, can monotone DNF attain OPT_N/OPT_A=Ω(n/log n), matching unrestricted DNF?

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Exact complexity of fixed-order read-once verification
author: Felix Happach; Lisa Hellerstein; Thomas Lidbetter
source_title: A General Framework for Approximating Min Sum Ordering Problems
text: Given a monotone read-once AND/OR formula, independent rational Bernoulli probabilities and positive integer test costs, can a minimum-expected-cost fixed permutation of tests be found in polynomial time, or is it NP-hard? Testing stops when the Boolean value is determined. Resolve also the unit-cost case; the known 8-approximation is polynomial there and pseudo-polynomial for general costs.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Sharp norm-valued adaptivity gap
author: Jian Li; Yinchen Liu; Yiran Zhang
source_title: Adaptivity Gaps for Stochastic Probing with Subadditive Functions
text: For arbitrary monotone norms, determine the sharp worst-case A/N between Ω(log n/loglog n) and O(log r·log n/loglog n).

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Exact symmetric-norm batching cost
author: Jian Li; Yinchen Liu; Yiran Zhang
source_title: Adaptivity Gaps for Stochastic Probing with Subadditive Functions
text: For permutation-invariant monotone norms, determine the smallest universal C with A≤CN. The existing upper bound is 2050.

subject: Queueing, Scheduling & Simulation
title: Can expiring computation opportunities beat the LP barrier?
author: Yihua Xu; Rohan Ghuge; Sebastian Perez-Salazar
source_title: Sequential Selection with Expirations
text: All n options are initially available. Option j has known value v_j>0 and mutually independent integer processing/expiration times S_j,E_j with known laws. One processor selects an available option, runs it nonpreemptively, earns v_j and may repeat; a started option cannot expire. Can a polynomial-time adaptive policy beat ratio 1−1/e against the optimal nonanticipating policy, or is that a computational barrier? Use the explicitly bounded time-support input model, without claiming strong polynomiality in a binary-encoded horizon.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Improve adaptive unrelated-machine allocation
author: Franziska Eberle; Anupam Gupta; Nicole Megow; Benjamin Moseley; Rudy Zhou
source_title: Configuration balancing for stochastic requests
text: With all job distributions available offline on m unrelated machines, can polynomial-time adaptivity attain o(log m/loglog m) approximation? Dependence among one job’s machine-specific processing times is allowed.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Constant-competitive online processor allocation
author: Franziska Eberle; Anupam Gupta; Nicole Megow; Benjamin Moseley; Rudy Zhou
source_title: Configuration balancing for stochastic requests
text: For processing times X_j/s_i on known speeds s_i>0, can polynomial-time online adaptivity be O(1)-competitive when distributions arrive in fixed arbitrary order? Each distribution is revealed upon arrival; the current bound is O(loglog m).

subject: Queueing, Scheduling & Simulation
title: Variance-independent sublinear-machine approximation for general jobs
author: Anupam Gupta; Benjamin Moseley; Rudy Zhou
source_title: Minimizing Completion Times for Stochastic Jobs via Batched Free Times
text: For n independent nonnegative jobs on m identical machines with known finite-support processing laws, can a polynomial-time adaptive approximation to minimum E[Σ_j C_j] have sublinear m dependence independent of processing-time variances? Jobs are nonpreemptive, reveal duration through execution, and must all finish. Extend the Bernoulli Õ(√m) guarantee to general laws, displaying any polylog(n) factors explicitly; such factors must not be mistaken for a uniform o(m) ratio.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Constant approximation without extra reservations
author: David Alemán Espinosa; Naveen Garg; Sharat Ibrahimpur; Neil Olver; Chaitanya Swamy
source_title: Stochastic Load Balancing with Machine Reservations
text: For related machines with speeds s_i>0 and durations X_j/s_i, can polynomial time achieve O(OPT_k) while reserving ≤k machines per job, for arbitrary input k? The known constant guarantee reserves 2k.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Two reservations with eligibility restrictions
author: David Alemán Espinosa; Naveen Garg; Sharat Ibrahimpur; Neil Olver; Chaitanya Swamy
source_title: Stochastic Load Balancing with Machine Reservations
text: For restricted identical machines with arbitrary job-eligibility sets, is OPT_2=O(OPT_m)? If not, is OPT_2 within a universal constant of optimal adaptive makespan, where sizes appear only after irrevocable assignment?

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Exact simultaneous reachability guarantees against an adversary
author: Pranav Ashok; Krishnendu Chatterjee; Jan Křetínský; Maximilian Weininger; Tobias Winkler
source_title: Approximating Values of Generalized-Reachability Stochastic Games
text: Given a finite rational stochastic game, initial state s, target sets T₁,…,T_d and rational q∈[0,1]^d, is it decidable whether ∃σ ∀τ ∀i: Pr_s^{σ,τ}(◇T_i)≥q_i? Strategies may randomize and use unbounded history. The targets need not be absorbing and the game need not stop. Arbitrary-precision approximation of the attainable frontier is known; exact threshold feasibility remains the target.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Deciding mixed almost-sure and positive-probability contracts
author: Moritz Graf; Anthony Lin; Rupak Majumdar
source_title: Solving Qualitative Multi-Objective Stochastic Games
text: In a finite rational turn-based stochastic game, is it decidable whether ∃σ∀τ φ holds when φ is an arbitrary positive Boolean formula over AS(◇T), AS(□T), NZ(◇T), and NZ(□T)? AS means probability 1 and NZ means strictly positive probability under (σ,τ). The residual regime must include positive-probability safety atoms: without them the problem is NEXPTIME-complete. Determine whether a finite, in particular exponential-size, winning-memory bound suffices.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: The complexity of strict-priority reachability and safety
author: Krishnendu Chatterjee; Joost-Pieter Katoen; Stefanie Mohr; Maximilian Weininger; Tobias Winkler
source_title: Stochastic games with lexicographic objectives
text: For reachability/safety Ω_i, determine F’s exact complexity. Is PSPACE sufficient, closing the PSPACE-hard versus NEXPTIME∩coNEXPTIME gap? Constant d is already in NP∩coNP.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Strict-priority probabilities for recurring temporal objectives
author: Krishnendu Chatterjee; Joost-Pieter Katoen; Stefanie Mohr; Maximilian Weininger; Tobias Winkler
source_title: Stochastic games with lexicographic objectives
text: For parity Ω_i, is F decidable? Parity means the largest priority recurring infinitely often is even. The one-player ω-regular case is solved.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Deterministic policies for alternative almost-sure safety guarantees
author: Tobias Winkler; Maximilian Weininger
source_title: Stochastic Games with Disjunctions of Multiple Objectives
text: For deterministic strategies of both players, q_i=1, and Ω_i=□(S∖B_i) with every unsafe state absorbing, close the PSPACE-hard/EXPTIME complexity gap. Randomized strategies give polynomial-time decidability.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Exact complexity of quantitative alternative guarantees
author: Tobias Winkler; Maximilian Weininger
source_title: Stochastic Games with Disjunctions of Multiple Objectives
text: For randomized strategies, rational q_i∈[0,1], and reachability/safety Ω_i with unrestricted targets, close the PSPACE-hard/NEXPTIME gap. Absorbing-target queries are already NP-complete.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: One inviolable parity rule plus several probability guarantees
author: Raphaël Berthon; Joost-Pieter Katoen; Tobias Winkler
source_title: Markov Decision Processes with Sure Parity and Multiple Reachability Objectives
text: For a finite rational MDP with parity objectives Ω₀,Ω₁,…,Ω_d, d part of the input, and rational thresholds q_i∈(0,1), is it decidable whether a policy σ makes every possible consistent path satisfy Ω₀ while Pr_s^σ(Ω_i)≥q_i for all i≥1? Policies may randomize and use unbounded memory. The hard rule includes probability-zero paths. One probabilistic parity objective and multiple absorbing reachability targets are established special cases.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Hard parity safety with an arbitrary-probability parity promise
author: Laurent Doyen; Shibashis Guha
source_title: Algorithm and Strategy Construction for Sure-Almost-Sure Stochastic Parity Games
text: Given a finite rational turn-based stochastic game, two parity conditions Ω_hard and Ω_soft, initial state s and rational q∈(0,1), is it decidable whether some σ ensures Ω_hard on every path consistent with σ and any opponent, and ensures Pr_s^{σ,τ}(Ω_soft)≥q for every τ? Unbounded-memory strategies are allowed. The probability-one soft condition is solved; replacing it by an arbitrary threshold is the unresolved extension.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: The complexity of plural long-run downside-risk constraints
author: Jan Křetínský; Tobias Meggendorfer
source_title: Conditional Value-at-Risk for Reachability and Mean Payoff in Markov Decision Processes
text: In a finite rational MDP with rational vector rewards r∈Q^d, let X_j=liminf_n n⁻¹Σ_{t<n}r_j(S_t). Given p_j∈(0,1), c_j,e_j∈Q, decide whether a randomized history-dependent policy simultaneously satisfies lower-tail CVaR_{p_j}(X_j)≥c_j and E[X_j]≥e_j for every j. CVaR averages exactly the lowest p_j probability mass, fractionally splitting an atom at the quantile. Determine the exact complexity between NP-hardness and PSPACE; is NP sufficient?

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: The bit complexity of optimal tail completion time
author: Tobias Meggendorfer
source_title: Risk-Aware Stochastic Shortest Path
text: In a finite rational MDP with absorbing goals, unit cost at every non-goal step and a proper policy reaching a goal almost surely from every state, let T be the hitting time (∞ on failure). For rational α∈(0,1), determine the complexity of deciding inf_π CVaR^upper_α(T)≤b for rational b. Here CVaR^upper_α averages the largest α fraction of completion times, splitting boundary atoms. Is the known exponential-time algorithm optimal, as conjectured?

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Exact mean–variance tradeoffs with bounded integer rewards
author: Shie Mannor; John N. Tsitsiklis
source_title: Algorithmic aspects of mean–variance optimization in Markov decision processes
text: For an explicitly given T-step finite MDP with rational transitions/reward laws and integer rewards in [−K,K], let W=Σ_{t<T}R_t and v*(λ)=min_{π:EπW≥λ}Varπ(W), over all randomized history-dependent policies. Can v*(λ) be computed exactly in time polynomial in the explicit input length, T and K, with infeasibility reported? Fixed exact-mean feasibility and bicriteria approximations are known; neither answers this inequality-constrained exact problem.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Long-run performance versus within-run and between-run variability
author: Tomáš Brázdil; Krishnendu Chatterjee; Vojtěch Forejt; Antonín Kučera
source_title: Trading performance for stability in Markov decision processes
text: Let a finite rational MDP have rational costs r(a) and arbitrary randomized history-dependent policies. Define M=limsup_n n⁻¹Σ_{t<n}r(A_t), and L=limsup_n n⁻¹Σ_{t<n}(r(A_t)−M)². Determine the exact complexity of finding a policy with E[M]≤u and either Var(M)≤v (global variability) or E[L]≤v (local variability), for rational u,v. The known upper bounds are PSPACE and NP respectively; is either problem NP-hard, or polynomial-time solvable?

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Exact entropic-risk comparison without a real-algebraic oracle
author: Christel Baier; Krishnendu Chatterjee; Tobias Meggendorfer; Jakob Piribauer
source_title: Entropic risk for turn-based stochastic games
text: For a finite rational Markov chain, rational nonnegative state rewards r, rational base b>1, rational risk parameter γ>0 and rational threshold t, all binary encoded, let X=Σ_{n≥0}r(S_n). Determine the exact complexity of testing −γ⁻¹log_b E[b^(−γX)]≥t. Can the known reduction to the existential theory of the reals be replaced by a more efficient decision procedure for these unrestricted algebraic instances? Unary-restricted small algebraic instances already have a polynomial-time algorithm.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: The complexity gap for compounding trajectory utility
author: Christel Baier; Krishnendu Chatterjee; Tobias Meggendorfer; Jakob Piribauer
source_title: Multiplicative Rewards in Markovian Models
text: For a finite rational MDP with rational factors r(s)>0 and initial state s, put Z(ρ)=limsup_n∏_{k≤n}r(ρ_k). Determine the exact complexity of sup_π E_s^π[Z]≥θ, for rational θ. The June 2025 version gives a CSRI lower bound and an NP^CSRI upper bound, where CSRI compares binary-encoded products of integer powers. Can the policy-selection overhead be removed, or is it necessary? Do not replace E[limsup product] by limsup E[product].

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Deciding exact success-conditioned and success-contingent utility
author: Jakob Piribauer; Christel Baier
source_title: Positivity-hardness results on Markov decision processes
text: Put X=W on success, zero otherwise. For rational θ, decide whether sup_π Eπ[X]>θ or sup_{π:Prπ(success)>0}Eπ[W|success]>θ. Optimize over policies with finite relevant expectations; promise finite suprema.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Exact downside-tail utility with signed accumulated rewards
author: Jakob Piribauer; Christel Baier
source_title: Positivity-hardness results on Markov decision processes
text: Assume every policy reaches goal almost surely. For rational p∈(0,1),θ, is sup_π CVaR_p(W)>θ decidable? Lower-tail CVaR averages exactly the lowest p probability mass, fractionally splitting a quantile atom.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Does variance-penalized completion planning admit deterministic exponential time?
author: Jakob Piribauer; Ocan Sankur; Christel Baier
source_title: The Variance-Penalized Stochastic Shortest Path Problem
text: For a finite rational MDP with nonnegative integer action weights, a unique terminal goal reached almost surely under every policy, and rational λ>0, let W be total weight to the goal and V*=sup_π(EπW−λVarπW). Given rational θ, determine the exact complexity of V*≥θ. Is the EXPTIME lower bound matched by a deterministic exponential-time algorithm, improving the NEXPTIME upper bound? Variance penalization is distinct from a hard variance constraint.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Samples versus deployments for stable predictive feedback
author: Gabriele Farina; Juan Carlos Perdomo
source_title: Stabilizing Performative Feedback Loops with Minimal Model Deployments
location: Definition 1; §1.3, Joint Deployment and Sample Complexity, pp. 8–9; Theorems 3–4.
text: For an unknown memoryless map D, determine the minimax sample/deployment tradeoff for an ε-stable mixture μ: E_{θ∼μ,z∼D(θ)}ℓ(z;θ)−min_{θ′}E_{θ∼μ,z∼D(θ)}ℓ(z;θ′)≤ε, with confidence 1−δ. Each deployment supplies fresh i.i.d. sample gradients. Θ⊂R^d is well-bounded convex with known inner/outer radii and a separation oracle; differentiable losses are convex with bounded gradients. Include strongly convex losses. No continuity of D is assumed.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Does offline robust decision complexity characterize learnability?
author: Haolin Liu; Braham Snyder; Chen-Yu Wei
source_title: On the Complexity of Offline Reinforcement Learning with Q*-Approximation and Partial Coverage
location: §3 (observation law, coverage and realizability); §5.2 and Theorem 2; §6 D_av; §8.
text: Do matching minimax lower bounds characterize offline RL under Q*-realizability and partial coverage through Ordec? Preserve M_conf={M:Q*_M∈F_conf}, the shared discrepancy D^π, and Ordec_λ=inf_ρ sup_{M∈M_conf}{E_{π∼ρ}[J_M(π_M)−J_M(π)]−λ max_{f∈F_conf}D^{π_M}(f||M)}. A decision-estimation upper bound is established; necessity remains unresolved.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Sharp accuracy dependence for realizable offline evaluation
author: Zeyu Jia; Alexander Rakhlin; Ayush Sekhari; Chen-Yu Wei
source_title: Offline Reinforcement Learning: Role of State Aggregation and Trajectory Data
location: §2; Definition 3.1; Theorems 3.1 and 5.1; §6 accuracy-gap paragraph, pp. 12–13; Appendix F.2.
text: With Q^{π_e} in finite F⊂(X×A→[−1,1]), what is the sharp ε-dependence for |V̂−V^{π_e}(ρ)|≤ε with confidence 1−δ from i.i.d. offline H-stage transition tuples? Preserve C̄=max_{f,f′∈F}C̄_{ε²/H²}(M,Φ(f,f′),μ), the source’s discretization-induced aggregated coverage. The upper bound is O(C̄H⁶log(|F|/δ)/ε⁴); the lower bound has ε^{-1} dependence. Do not freeze the coverage truncation as ε varies.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Dimension-free directional bounds for nonlinear Bellman-residual minimization
author: Philip Amortila; Audrey Huang; Akshay Krishnamurthy; Nan Jiang
source_title: A Unifying View of Coverage in Linear Off-Policy Evaluation
location: §5.3, Connection to Bellman Residual Minimization, Eqs. (16)–(17), pp. 9–10.
text: For the nonlinear Bellman-residual estimator of Eq.(16), assume Q^π∈F and T^πF⊂F. Can its scalar-return error have leading bound O((V_max/(1−γ))√(C^πlog(1/δ)/n)), removing log|F| or analogous statistical dimension from Eq.(17)? Preserve that equation’s coverage coefficient; dimension may remain in burn-in or lower-order terms.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Dimension-free evaluation from adaptively logged trajectories
author: Xiang Li; Nan Jiang
source_title: Q-MMR: Off-Policy Evaluation via Recursive Reweighting and Moment Matching
location: Theorem 1; §6 Limitations and Future Work, pp. 11–12.
text: Can Q-MMR’s high-probability OPE bound survive adaptive logging without leading log|F|/covering-number dependence? Retain bounded finite-horizon Markov rewards/transitions, only Q^π-realizability, per-observation nonparametric weights, and error controlled by empirical matching loss and weight second moments. Logging policies may depend on earlier episodes; the existing theorem requires i.i.d. trajectories.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Joint cost of hidden decision rules and response memory
author: Han Shao; Shuo Xie; Kunhe Yang
source_title: Should Decision-Makers Reveal Classifiers in Online Strategic Classification?
location: Protocol 1; §2; Theorems 4.1 and 4.4; §6, p. 9 (conference) / p. 13 arXiv.
text: In γ-Weighted strategic classification, determine the sharp deterministic mistake bound jointly in d=Ldim(H), k_in,k_out,|H| and γ. The known graph includes self-loops; agents adversarially tie-break best responses to the normalized γ-discounted average of past classifiers. Only manipulated features and labels are observed. Assume some h* classifies every agent correctly under response to h*. Must the current bound’s k_in/(1−γ) penalties multiply?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Learning from reports with unknown manipulation radii
author: Han Shao; Avrim Blum; Omar Montasser
source_title: Strategic Classification under Unknown Personalized Manipulation
text: For finite binary H and a known metric, determine realizable PAC sample complexity when i.i.d. agents (x,r,y) can move within B(x,r), yet only final feature Δ and label are observed after deployment. Neither x nor r is revealed. Agents use a nearest positive-label manipulation, otherwise staying put. Allow randomized improper learners using all rounds: can they beat the conservative-learners’ Ω-tilde(|H|/ε) lower bound?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Computationally efficient uniform last-iterate control
author: Junyan Liu; Yunfan Li; Ruosong Wang; Lin F. Yang
source_title: Uniform Last-Iterate Guarantee for Bandits and Reinforcement Learning
text: For finite S,A, is F=t^{-1/2}poly(S,A,H,log(t/δ)) achievable with polynomial per-episode computation, avoiding enumeration of A^{SH} policies?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Sharp state and horizon dependence of uniform policy improvement
author: Junyan Liu; Yunfan Li; Ruosong Wang; Lin F. Yang
source_title: Uniform Last-Iterate Guarantee for Bandits and Reinforcement Learning
location: Theorem 5.1 and immediately following paragraph, p. 9.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning

author: Hao Qin; Kwang-Sung Jun; Chicheng Zhang

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Generic faithfulness with time-reused Bayesian parameters
author: Rajab Aghamov; Christel Baier; Joël Ouaknine; Jakob Piribauer; Mihir Vahanwala; Isa Vialard
source_title: Temporal Properties of Conditional Independence in Dynamic Bayesian Networks

text: For every binary dynamic Bayesian-network template with finitely many variables, let θ consist of the initial and one-step conditional-probability tables, with each one-step table reused at every time. Is the set of θ for which, at some t≥0, disjoint current-slice sets X^t,Y^t,Z^t satisfy X^t ⟂ Y^t | Z^t without d-separation in the time-t unrolling a Lebesgue-null subset of the finite-dimensional parameter cube?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Is the universal disagreement curve pointwise unavoidable?
author: Omer Angel; Yinon Spinka
source_title: Pairwise optimal coupling of multiple random variables

title: Is two the sharp scalar coupling ratio?
author: Cheuk Ting Li; Venkat Anantharam
