subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Least redundant finite-alphabet reports of one hidden bit
author: Michael Dikshtein; Or Ordentlich; Shlomo Shamai (Shitz)
source_title: The Double-Sided Information Bottleneck Function
text: Let X∼Bernoulli(1/2), U⊥V|X, with arbitrary finite output alphabets and I(X;U)=c, I(X;V)=d for c,d∈(0,1). Must I(U;V)≥I(Z_a;Z_b)? The comparison outputs are independent conditional on X, with P(Z_a=1|X=x)=ax and P(Z_b=1|X=x)=bx; a,b∈(0,1) satisfy h₂(a/2)−h₂(a)/2=c and h₂(b/2)−h₂(b)/2=d. Information is in bits. The binary-output case is proved.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: A finite weak-dependence regime for symmetric report compression
author: Michael Dikshtein; Or Ordentlich; Shlomo Shamai (Shitz)
source_title: The Double-Sided Information Bottleneck Function
text: Let X∼Bernoulli(1/2), Y=X⊕N with independent N∼Bernoulli(p). Define R(c,d,p)=sup I(U;V) over finite U−X−Y−V with I(X;U)≤c and I(Y;V)≤d. For every c,d∈(0,1), is there θ(c,d)<1/2 such that R(c,d,p)=1−h₂(α*p*β) whenever θ<p≤1/2? Here α=h₂^{-1}(1−c), β=h₂^{-1}(1−d), h₂^{-1} takes values in[0,1/2], and a*b=a(1−b)+(1−a)b. The formula represents independent binary-symmetric compression channels.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Complete orientation with temporal tiers and cross-tier confounding
author: Christine W. Bang; Vanessa Didelez
source_title: Constraint-based causal discovery with tiered background knowledge and latent variables in single or overlapping datasets
text: For an exact observational CI model faithful to an acyclic latent-variable causal model, and a correct ordered partition forbidding later-tier ancestry of earlier tiers, complete the tFCI graphical orientation rules: which additional rules, if any, ensure every endpoint mark shared by all compatible MAGs is oriented? Cross-tier latent confounding is allowed; selection variables are absent. Completeness of simple tFCI without restrictive cross-tier orientations is already proved.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Must classical inflation become exact at a finite level?
author: Miguel Navascués; Elie Wolfe
source_title: The Inflation Technique Completely Solves the Causal Compatibility Problem
text: For every finite classical correlation scenario G with fixed finite observed alphabets and unrestricted latent alphabets, does there exist a finite n=n(G,alphabets) such that an observed law passes the nth-order distribution-inflation test if and only if it is compatible with G? A correlation scenario has independent latent roots and observed children. The level must work for all laws on those alphabets, not depend on one incompatible input law.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Is the HLP reduction necessary for absence of latent inequalities?
author: Joe Henson; Raymond Lal; Matthew F. Pusey
source_title: Theory-independent limits on correlations from generalised Bayesian networks
text: Let C_G be the classical observed laws compatible with a latent-variable DAG G and I_G the laws satisfying its observed d-separation CIs, over arbitrary finite observed alphabets. If C_G=I_G, must G reduce to a latent-free DAG H with the same observed d-separations by a sequence of edge deletions and additions X→Y allowed when pa(X)⊆pa(Y) and pa(X) contains a latent node? Use the source’s exogenized canonical representation and discard isolated latent vertices.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Additional power of deletion separation
author: Shashaank Khanna; Marina Maciel Ansanelli; Matthew F. Pusey; Elie Wolfe
source_title: Classifying causal structures: Ascertaining when classical correlations are constrained by inequalities
text: Let G be a canonical latent-variable DAG in which every pair of observed nodes not joined by a directed edge or shared latent parent is d-separated by some other observed nodes. Suppose a latent-free DAG H has exactly G’s observed d-separation relations. Must H also have exactly G’s observed e-separation relations, where X⊥_eY|Z upon deletion of W means d-separation in G with the disjoint observed set W removed?

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Lifting support patterns to probabilities
author: Shashaank Khanna; Marina Maciel Ansanelli; Matthew F. Pusey; Elie Wolfe
source_title: Classifying causal structures: Ascertaining when classical correlations are constrained by inequalities
text: Fix a latent-variable DAG G and a finite support S of assignments to its observed variables. Suppose that for each observed d-separation X⊥Y|Z and each z, the projected support on X,Y at z is a Cartesian product. Must there exist a distribution with support exactly S that simultaneously satisfies every observed d-separation CI of G? It need not be a full latent-model realization in C_G.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Faithful hurdle-DAG identifiability beyond three variables
author: Shiqing Yu; Mathias Drton; Ali Shojaie
source_title: Directed Graphical Models and Causal Discovery for Zero-Inflated Data
text: For m>3, can a law faithful to two distinct Markov-equivalent DAGs factor over both with node conditionals (1−p)δ_0+pN(μ,σ²), positive constant σ², and logit(p),μ polynomials in parent values and nonzero indicators? For the reversible pair W→U/U→W with identical other-parent set P in Proposition 8, impose Theorem 10’s restriction in both factorizations: μ depends on W (respectively U) or its nonzero indicator, or logit(p) depends on that parent’s value. Is such a law impossible?

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: From Gaussian to nested inclusion
author: Thijs van Ommen
source_title: Efficiently Deciding Algebraic Equivalence of Bow-Free Acyclic Path Diagrams
text: For maximal arid acyclic directed mixed graphs G,G′ on the same vertices, does inclusion of their Gaussian linear-SEM models M(G)⊆M(G′) imply inclusion of their full nested Markov models N(G)⊆N(G′)? Equivalently in the source’s closed algebraic formulation, can Gaussian algebraic inclusion miss a non-Gaussian nested constraint? N(G) imposes ordinary and fixing-kernel conditional independences; maximal arid projection preserves N(G).

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Graphical algebraic equivalence
author: Thijs van Ommen
source_title: Efficiently Deciding Algebraic Equivalence of Bow-Free Acyclic Path Diagrams
text: Give a necessary-and-sufficient graphical criterion for equality of the algebraic covariance models of two bow-free acyclic path diagrams on the same observed vertices. A BAP permits directed and bidirected edges but no directed cycle and no pair carrying both types. Its covariance map is (I−Λ)^(-T)Ω(I−Λ)^(-1), with positive-definite Ω and graph-prescribed zeros. Equality means equal polynomial constraints/Zariski closures, not exact equality at exceptional covariance points.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Faithfulness under parameter sharing
author: Tobias Boege; Kaie Kubjas; Pratik Misra; Liam Solus
source_title: Colored Gaussian Directed Acyclic Graphical Models
text: Characterize the finite colored DAGs (G,c) for which at least one Gaussian law in M(G,c) is faithful to G. In X_j=Σ_(i→j)λ_ijX_i+ε_j, independent Gaussian errors have positive variances; equal vertex colors impose equal error variances and equal edge colors impose equal coefficients, with vertex and edge palettes disjoint. Both types of equality may be present simultaneously. Faithfulness means exactly the CIs from d-separation, with no additional CI.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Equivalence under shared coefficients
author: Tobias Boege; Kaie Kubjas; Pratik Misra; Liam Solus
source_title: Colored Gaussian Directed Acyclic Graphical Models
text: Characterize when two edge-colored Gaussian DAGs have equal covariance model sets. Equal edge colors constrain the corresponding structural coefficients to be equal; error variances are free positive and uncolored edges have free coefficients. The target is exact M(G,c)=M(H,d), not ordinary Markov equivalence of the underlying DAGs. Include colorings beyond the established blocked properly edge-colored identifiable class.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Is CDIS complete when selection precedes intervention?
author: Haoyue Dai; Ignavier Ng; Jianle Sun; Zeyu Tang; Gongxu Luo; Xinshuai Dong; Peter Spirtes; Kun Zhang
source_title: When Selection Meets Intervention: Additional Complexities in Causal Discovery
text: For the causally sufficient acyclic interventional-twin-graph model of Dai et al., selected units satisfy S*=1 before any intervention; data contain an observational regime and finitely many soft-intervention regimes with unknown target sets. Assume the within-regime CIs and cross-regime conditional invariances are exactly those implied by the twin graphs. Does oracle CDIS (Algorithm 1, with its iterative FCI+ refinements) identify every invariant edge mark of the observational MAG across all compatible (G,I) pairs?

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Generic coefficient identification with nonlinear confounding and feedback
author: Daniele Tramontano; Mathias Drton; Jalal Etesami
source_title: Parameter Identification in Linear Non-Gaussian Causal Models under General Confounding
location: §2 Definitions 2.1–2.2 and Assumption 1; §6 Definition 6.1; §8 conclusion p. 22.
text: For a directed mixed graph G, allowing directed cycles, characterize the entries of Λ generically identified from the full law X=(I−Λ)^(-T)ε, with graph-sparse Λ and det(I−Λ)≠0. The errors obey the connected-set Markov property of the bidirected graph: ε_C⊥ε_(V\Sib(C)) for each bidirected-connected C. Genericity excludes a fixed Lebesgue-null set of Λ and requires: aᵀε⊥bᵀε implies a_u b_v=0 whenever u=v or u↔v. Identification compares every admissible representation of the same observed law.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Can higher cumulants distinguish more soft-intervention latent graphs?
author: Paula Leyes Carreno; Chiara Meroni; Anna Seigal
source_title: Linear Causal Disentanglement via Higher-Order Cumulants
text: In linear causal disentanglement X^(k)=F(I−Λ^(k))^(-1)ε^(k), let F be generic and unchanged across contexts; generic latent DAG coefficients and independent non-Gaussian errors are observed under one unknown-target single-node soft intervention per latent node, plus a known observational context. Each intervention changes all incoming nonzero coefficients and the target’s sufficiently high nonzero cumulant. Are both inclusions soft(G)⊆soft_2(G)⊆{G′:closure(G′)=closure(G)} strict in general? The two classes reproduce respectively the recovered mixing matrices in all contexts and only their covariance matrices. Here closure means transitive closure.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Independences after unit-variance restriction
author: Carlos Améndola; Tobias Boege; Benjamin Hollering; Pratik Misra
source_title: Structural Identifiability of Graphical Continuous Lyapunov Models
text: For a DAG G with a free self-loop at every vertex, fix diagonal positive C and let M_(G,C)={Σ≻0: AΣ+ΣAᵀ+C=0 for a Hurwitz-stable G-sparse A}. Characterize all conditional independences that hold throughout the restricted model {Σ∈M_(G,C):diag(Σ)=1}, and their relation to d-separation in G. The operation is intersection with unit variances, not arbitrary post-hoc standardization while changing C.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Equivalence with directed cycles
author: Carlos Améndola; Tobias Boege; Benjamin Hollering; Pratik Misra
source_title: Structural Identifiability of Graphical Continuous Lyapunov Models
location: §5.3 Problem 5.6 p. 19; Theorems 3.3/3.7 for established acyclic case.
text: For finite simple directed graphs G,H with all self-loops and possible cycles of length≥3, characterize when M_(G,C)=M_(H,C), where M_(G,C)={Σ≻0:AΣ+ΣAᵀ+C=0, A Hurwitz-stable and G-sparse} and C is fixed positive diagonal. Simple means no opposite directed pair. Extend the known acyclic equivalence characterization; graph-preserving two-cycle ambiguity is not the target.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Are disconnected explanations the only exceptional equilibrium ambiguities?
author: Cecilie Olesen Recke; Niels Richard Hansen
source_title: Identifiability and Estimation in Continuous Lyapunov Models
location: §3.3 Theorem 1 and §3.5 after Corollary 2 p. 12; §6 first paragraph.
text: Let G be connected with all self-loops, r≥3, and Θ_G={G-sparse Hurwitz M}×(0,∞)^d×(R\{0})^d. The last factors are unknown diagonal innovation cumulants C_2,C_r. Let φ_(G,r)(M,C_2,C_r)=(Σ,K_r), the unique solutions of the continuous order 2 and orderr Lyapunov equations. Can its fiber exceed the positive scaling ray {cθ:c>0} when (Σ,K_r) belongs to no moment model of any disconnected spanning subgraph of G?

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Reward equivalence that survives every transition model
author: Joar Skalse; Alessandro Abate
source_title: Partial Identifiability and Misspecification in Inverse Reinforcement Learning
text: For fixed finite state and action spaces and discount 0<γ<1, characterize all pairs R₁,R₂:S×A×S→ℝ whose expected discounted returns induce identical weak orderings of stationary randomized policies for every transition kernel τ. Use full-support initial distribution μ₀, so every state is reachable. Equivalently, characterize ≡Ω:=⋂τ ≡ORD(τ,γ) by necessary and sufficient conditions on the reward functions. Potential shaping plus positive scaling characterizes a stronger trajectory-distribution equivalence, but is not necessary for ≡Ω.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Accuracy-optimal adaptive multinomial-logit learning
author: Flavio Chierichetti; Mirko Giacchini; Ravi Kumar; Silvio Lattanzi; Alessandro Panconesi; Erasmo Tani; Andrew Tomkins
source_title: Learning Multinomial Logits in O(n log n) Time
text: Determine adaptive query complexity in the shared model. Close Ω(n log n/ε²) versus O(n log n/ε³) for n≥1/ε. Queries may use arbitrary slates; known upper bounds use pairs.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Optimal nonadaptive multinomial-logit query complexity
author: Flavio Chierichetti; Mirko Giacchini; Ravi Kumar; Silvio Lattanzi; Alessandro Panconesi; Erasmo Tani; Andrew Tomkins
source_title: Learning Multinomial Logits in O(n log n) Time
text: Determine query complexity when every slate is chosen before any answers. Close Ω(n² log n/ε²) versus O(n² log n log(n/ε)/ε³), including the logarithmic n gap at fixed ε.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Joint horizon and tail-level complexity of recursive CVaR learning
author: Oliver Mortensen; Mohammad Sadegh Talebi
source_title: On the Sample Complexity of Discounted Reinforcement Learning with Optimized Certainty Equivalents
text: With a generative transition oracle for a finite discounted MDP, known rewards in [0,1], and recursive lower-tail CVaRτ value Vπ(s)=r(s,π(s))+γ CVaRτ(Vπ(S′)), what is the minimax sample complexity of returning π with ||V*−Vπ||∞≤ε with probability ≥1−δ, for δ∈(0,1/4) and sufficiently small ε>0? Determine the joint dependence on γ and τ in 0<τ<γ<1. Current lower bounds scale as the maximum of SA/[ε²(1−γ)²τ²] and (1−γτ)SA/[ε²(1−γ)⁴τ], while the cited general upper bound scales as SA/[ε²(1−γ)⁴τ²], up to logarithms.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Sharp state and horizon dependence for general recursive-risk regret
author: Wenhao Xu; Xuefeng Gao; Xuedong He
source_title: Regret Bounds for Markov Decision Processes with Recursive Optimized Certainty Equivalents
text: For each fixed finite-valued, nondecreasing, closed concave utility u:ℝ→ℝ with u(0)=0 and 1∈∂u(0), let ρu(X)=supλ{λ+E[u(X−λ)]}. In an unknown finite H-step, time-inhomogeneous MDP with S states, A actions and known rewards in [0,1], values recurse as Vhπ=rh+ρu(Vh+1π), with VH+1=0. Determine the minimax expected regret over K episodes, sharply in S,H and u. In particular, close the source’s extra √S and horizon-dependent gaps between upper and lower bounds, rather than only matching the already-correct √K and √A factors.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Efficient attainment of dimension-optimal inverse-optimization regret
author: Shinsaku Sakaue
source_title: Tight Regret Bound for Online Inverse Linear Optimization via Multiscale Matrix Weights
text: A fixed unknown u∈B₂ᵈ faces adaptively chosen nonempty compact menus Z_t⊆B₂ᵈ. After recommending X_t∈Z_t, the learner observes rational Y_t∈argmax_Zt u·z. Can it guarantee EΣ_t≤T u·(Y_t−X_t)=O(√d), uniformly in unknown T, with polynomial bit complexity and oracle calls? The rational oracle accepts (q,κ), κ>0, and returns rational x∈Z_t with q·x≥sup_Zt q·z−κ; polynomiality is in d,t and input/output encoding lengths.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Corruption-budget-free inverse optimization with bounded lifetime regret
author: Yang Cai; Anupam Gupta; Vineet Gupta; Guru Guruganesh; Yanchen Jiang; Christopher Liaw; Aranyak Mehta; Renato Paes Leme; Grigoris Velegkas; Di Wang
source_title: Efficient Online Inverse Optimization with O(d) Regret
text: A hidden w* lies in a known compact convex K₁⊆RB₂ᵈ. After each query pt∈ℝᵈ, an adaptive strong-separation oracle returns a unit vector vt. Write rt=〈w*−pt,vt〉. For every horizon T and every corruption budget C with Σt≤T(rt)₋≤C, can one algorithm, without being given C or an upper bound on it, guarantee Σt≤T(rt)₊=O(dR+C)? The source attains this rate when C is supplied; merely adjusting its existing step-size schedule cannot handle arbitrary unknown C.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Exact safety region for squared-error reward learning
author: Lukas Fluri; Leon Lang; Alessandro Abate; Patrick Forré; David Krueger; Joar Skalse
source_title: The Perils of Optimizing Learned Reward Functions: Low Training Error Does Not Guarantee Low Regret
text: Characterize D such that every R̂ with E_D[(R̂−R)²]/(range R)²≤ε and every π̂∈argmax J_R̂ satisfy Reg_R(π̂)<L. Seek necessary-and-sufficient geometric conditions analogous to the solved absolute-error characterization.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Exact safety region for regularized learned-reward optimization
author: Lukas Fluri; Leon Lang; Alessandro Abate; Patrick Forré; David Krueger; Joar Skalse
source_title: The Perils of Optimizing Learned Reward Functions: Low Training Error Does Not Guarantee Low Regret
text: For fixed λ>0 and continuous nonnegative policy penalty ω, characterize D such that every R̂ with E_D|R̂−R|/(range R)≤ε and every π̂∈argmaxπ[J_R̂(π)−λω(π)] satisfy Reg_R(π̂)<L. Seek structural necessary-and-sufficient conditions extending the unregularized theorem.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Unrestricted MaxMinLCB preference optimization
author: Barna Pásztor; Parnian Kassraie; Andreas Krause
source_title: Bandits with Preference Feedback: A Stackelberg Game Perspective
text: Does MaxMinLCB retain anytime regret O(β_Tᴰ(δ)√(Tγ_Tᴰ)) with probability 1−δ when both max–min domains are X rather than M_t? Keep its prescribed estimator/confidence coefficients. X is compact, ||f||_Hk≤B, k(x,x)≤1, and kernel eigenfunctions have zero mean. Pair feedback is Bernoulli σ(f(x)−f(y)), σ logistic; regret is Σ_t[σ(f*−f(x_t))+σ(f*−f(y_t))−1]/2. Here γ_Tᴰ is information gain for kᴰ((x,y),(x′,y′))=k(x,x′)+k(y,y′)−k(x,y′)−k(y,x′).

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Is the offline inverse-RL state-squared cost necessary?
author: Lei Zhao; Mengdi Wang; Yu Bai
source_title: Is Inverse Reinforcement Learning Harder than Standard Reinforcement Learning? A Theoretical Perspective
text: For offline tabular IRL with H steps, S states, 2≤A<S actions and deterministic expert πᴱ, can the lower bound Ω(H²SC*min{S,A}/ε²) be strengthened to Ω(H²S²C*/ε²), or is the state-quadratic upper bound improvable? Data consist of K behavior-policy trajectories plus expert actions at their visited states. Require recovery of the source’s bounded feasible-reward mapping R*(V,A)_h(s,a)=−A_h(s,a)1[a≠π_hᴱ(s)]+V_h(s)−P_hV_{h+1}, with |V_h|≤H−h+1 and 0≤A_h≤H−h+1. Error is sup_(V,A) max_h E_{s_h∼πeval}|V_h^πeval(s_h;R*)−V_h^πeval(s_h;R̂)|≤ε with probability ≥2/3. C* bounds (HS)⁻¹Σ_hsa d_h^πeval(s,a)/d_h^πb(s,a), with 0/0=0.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Correct posterior-sampling stopping under bounded linear structure
author: Cyrille Kone; Marc Jourdan; Émilie Kaufmann
source_title: Pareto Set Identification With Posterior Sampling
text: Finite spanning sampling arms a∈ℝʰ yield N(θᵀa,Σ), Σ≻0 known; finite answer arms z have means θᵀz. For θ inside a known full-dimensional ball Θ⊂ℝ^{h×d}, with locally constant Pareto set, can PSIPS calibrate c,M for δ-correct stopping while preserving its asymptotic characteristic-time optimum? It stops when M(t−1,δ) draws from N(vec θ̂_t,c(t−1,δ)[Σ⊗(V_t+ξI)⁻¹]) all avoid Θ∩Alt(Ŝ_t), where V_t=Σ_s≤t a_sa_sᵀ and Alt means different coordinatewise Pareto set. Keep the prescribed ridge estimator/sampling policy and require limsup_δ↓0 c(t,δ)log M(t,δ)/log(1/δ)≤1.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Output-polynomial exact utility–cost tradeoff enumeration
author: Henri Nikoleit; Ankit Anand; Anurag Murty Naredla; Heiko Röglin
source_title: The Art of Being Difficult: Combining Human and AI Strengths to Find Adversarial Instances for Heuristics
text: Given n binary-encoded positive rational profits p_i and weights w_i, can all nondominated subsets I⊆[n] be enumerated in time polynomial in input length and final output size? Domination means weakly greater profit and weakly smaller weight, with one strict inequality. There is no capacity bound; distinct subsets with identical objective pairs remain distinct outputs. Seek any algorithm, not the already-refuted Nemhauser–Ullmann candidate.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Does quantile homogenization enlarge every possible aggregate law?
author: Yuyu Chen; Peng Liu; Yang Liu; Ruodu Wang
source_title: Ordering and Inequalities for Mixtures on Risk Aggregation
text: For every n≥2, every tuple F=(F_1,…,F_n) whose members have decreasing densities on their supports, and every doubly stochastic n×n matrix Λ, is D_n(F)⊆D_n(Λ⊗F)? Here D_n(F) is the set of laws of Σ_iX_i over all joint distributions with X_i∼F_i, and the i-th marginal of Λ⊗F has quantile function Σ_jΛ_ij F_j^{-1}.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Which laws are sums of two uniform reports?
author: Tiantian Mao; Bin Wang; Ruodu Wang
source_title: Sums of Standard Uniform Random Variables
text: Characterize the set D_2={Law(U+V):U,V∼Unif[0,1]}, with arbitrary dependence: for a given probability law G on [0,2], determine whether a joint uniform coupling has sum law G. The target is the complete intrinsic description left open beyond the source’s unimodal, two-atom, three-atom, and uniform-component subclasses; convex-order domination by Unif[0,2] alone is insufficient.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Can uniform convex beliefs always be balanced jointly?
author: Ruodu Wang
source_title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability
text: For every convex body C⊂R^d with 0<vol_d(C)<∞ and every integer n≥d+1, do there exist jointly distributed X_1,…,X_n, each uniform on C, with Σ_iX_i=nE[X_1] almost surely? This is n-complete mixability of the uniform distribution; d=1 is established.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Can negative association survive exchangeable joint representation?
author: Takaaki Koike; Liyuan Lin; Ruodu Wang
source_title: Joint mixability and notions of negative dependence
text: If F supports an NA n-joint mix, must it support an exchangeable NA n-joint mix?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Is a balanced coupling optimal under uncertain observation subsets?
author: Takaaki Koike; Liyuan Lin; Ruodu Wang
source_title: Joint mixability and notions of negative dependence
text: For n-completely mixable F with finite variance, convex f and permutation-invariant nonempty M⊆Prob(2^[n]), must some exchangeable joint mix minimize sup_{μ∈M}Σ_Kμ(K)E[f(Σ_{i∈K}X_i)] over couplings X_i∼F, when costs are defined?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Does finite-menu representation commute with combination?
author: Justyna Dąbrowska; Arthur Van Camp; Erik Quaeghebeur
source_title: Sets of Desirable Gamble Sets and their Representations as Information Algebras
text: For finite menus and arbitrary nonempty representing families 𝒟_1,𝒟_2, does γ(𝒟_1⊗𝒟_2)=cl_K(γ(𝒟_1)∪γ(𝒟_2))? The target is only this combination-commutation equality.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Does individual irrelevance already give joint irrelevance?
author: Arthur Van Camp; Kevin Blackwell; Jason Konek
source_title: Independent Natural Extension for Choice Functions
text: For all disjoint nonempty I,O and ∅≠E⊆Ω_I, must Marg_O(K*|E)=Marg_O K*? This asks whether many-to-one and many-to-many extensions coincide.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Does independent extension permit option-specific conditioning events?
author: Arthur Van Camp; Kevin Blackwell; Jason Konek
source_title: Independent Natural Extension for Choice Functions
text: For each j, finite menu A on Ω_j, and assignment ∅≠E_f⊆Ω_{[n]\{j}} to f∈A, must A∈K* iff {I_{E_f}f:f∈A}∈K*?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Do 3k moments uniquely identify a univariate Gaussian mixture?
author: Carlos Améndola; Jean-Charles Faugère; Bernd Sturmfels
source_title: Moment Varieties of Gaussian Mixtures
text: For arbitrary k, is the complexified moment map of k-component univariate Gaussian mixtures, with unknown means, variances and weights summing to 1, generically one-to-one modulo component permutation from moments m_1,…,m_{3k}? Equivalently, is the model rationally identifiable at order 3k? Algebraic finite-fiber identification at 3k−1 and rational identification at 3k+2 are established; these are not the target.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Is parameter counting exact for every bivariate Gaussian mixture?
author: Carlos Améndola; Kristian Ranestad; Bernd Sturmfels
source_title: Algebraic Identifiability of Gaussian Mixtures
text: For every d≥2,k≥1, is dim Sec_k(G_{2,d})=min{binom(d+2,2)−1,6k−1}?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: How much latent ambiguity survives fourth-order Gaussian summaries?
author: Carlos Améndola; Kristian Ranestad; Bernd Sturmfels
source_title: Algebraic Identifiability of Gaussian Mixtures
text: For n≥8,r≥3,k=n+r and P=k n(n+3)/2+k−1≤binom(n+4,4)−1, is dim Sec_k(G_{n,4})=P−binom(r−1,2)?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Are high-order Gaussian moment tangent maps nondegenerate?
author: Alexander Taveira Blomenhofer; Alex Casarotti
source_title: Nondefectivity of invariant secant varieties
text: For all d≥5 and n≥2, does V=GM_d(C^n)=closure{[exp(ℓ+q/2)]_d:ℓ∈S¹(C^n),q∈S²(C^n)} have a nondegenerate tangent map? Precisely, must T:P(V_reg)→Gr(dimV,S^d(C^n)), [v]↦T_vV, have finite fibers? The unresolved extension is beyond the proved degrees 5,…,9; [·]_d means the homogeneous degree-d part.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Do 3k moments identify positive-support mixture sensors?
author: Oskar Henriksson; Kristian Ranestad; Lisa Seccia; Teresa Yu
source_title: Moment varieties of the inverse Gaussian and gamma distributions are nondefective
text: For each k≥2, are k-mixtures of gamma distributions and k-mixtures of inverse Gaussian distributions rationally identifiable from their first 3k moments, modulo component permutations? Component parameters and mixture weights are unknown. Rational identifiability refers to generic one-to-one fibers of the complexified moment parameterization; the two positive-support families are one source-conjectured target, not two counts.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Can reduced information-bottleneck roots be singular away from bifurcations?
author: Shlomi Agmon
source_title: The Information Bottleneck’s Ordinary Differential Equation: First-Order Root Tracking for the Information Bottleneck
text: For a finite information-bottleneck problem p(X,Y), write q_t(y)=p(y|t), w_t=p(t), and let BA_β denote the source’s Blahut–Arimoto map in their logarithmic coordinates. At every reduced fixed point for which log coordinates and the Jacobian are defined, is I−D_log(q),log(w)BA_β nonsingular except at bifurcation points? Reduced means all w_t>0 and pairwise distinct q_t. BA_β first sets r(t|x)∝w_t exp(−β KL(p(Y|x)||q_t)), then w′_t=Σ_xp(x)r(t|x), q′_t(y)=Σ_xp(x,y)r(t|x)/w′_t, and returns (log q′,log w′).

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Uniqueness of canonical information-optimal representations
author: Hippolyte Charvin; Nicola Catenacci Volpi; Daniel Polani
source_title: Exact and Soft Successive Refinement of the Information Bottleneck
text: For a finite joint law p(X,Y), put F(λ)=max_{T−X−Y:I(X;T)≤λ}I(Y;T), restricting |T|≤|X|+1, and assume F is strictly concave on [0,H(X)]. At each fixed λ, must every optimal canonical T have the same pair (q(T),q(X|T)), up to output permutation, and must q(X|T) be injective as a map from output probability distributions to distributions on X? Canonical means positive-mass output symbols have distinct posterior vectors q(X|t).

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Can two mixture components always yield the optimal two-stream e-value?
author: Yunda Hao; Peter Grünwald; Tyron Lardy; Long Long; Reuben Adams
source_title: E-values for k-Sample Tests with Exponential Families
location: §5.2, displayed unnumbered Conjecture before §6; Lardy thesis §4.5.2 pp. 59–60.
text: For any regular one-parameter exponential family {P_μ:μ∈I} and μ₁,μ₂∈I, is the reverse information projection of P_μ₁⊗P_μ₂ onto conv{P_μ⊗P_μ:μ∈I} always attained by a mixture of at most two null elements? The alternative coordinates are independent; the mixture is over common-parameter product laws.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Does nonamenability break invariant worst-case e-value optimality?
author: Muriel Felipe Pérez-Ortiz; Tyron Lardy; Rianne de Heide; Peter Grünwald
source_title: E-statistics, group invariance and anytime-valid testing
location: §5.1 p. 1424; Assumption 1 and Theorem 2; Lardy thesis §8.5.1 p. 161.
text: With all other premises of Theorem 2 retained, can a nonamenable group make the maximal-invariant likelihood ratio T_M fail to maximize inf_g E_Qg logT over nonnegative T satisfying sup_g E_PgT≤1?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Can repeated multiaccuracy-oracle calls recover weak agnostic learning?
author: Sílvia Casacuberta; Parikshit Gopalan; Varun Kanade; Omer Reingold
source_title: How Global Calibration Strengthens Multiaccuracy
location: §7 p. 39; §§3–4 definitions and scalar-postprocessing lower bounds.
text: Does efficient oracle access to arbitrarily accurate C-multiaccuracy imply standard weak agnostic learning, allowing repeated calls rather than scalar postprocessing of one predictor?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The best multiaccuracy tolerance obtainable from a restricted weak learner
author: Sílvia Casacuberta; Parikshit Gopalan; Varun Kanade; Omer Reingold
source_title: How Global Calibration Strengthens Multiaccuracy
text: For 0<β≤α<1, what is the optimal efficiently attainable multiaccuracy tolerance from this restricted weak oracle? Known: min{α+ε,1/2} with O(β⁻²) calls; under the source’s pseudorandom-function assumption, tolerance below α/2−ε is impossible in general.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Can calibrated multiaccuracy support selective omniprediction?
author: Sílvia Casacuberta; Varun Kanade
source_title: Selective Omniprediction and Fair Abstention
text: Can calibrated C-multiaccuracy suffice for this selective-omniprediction guarantee, replacing full multicalibration, or can ordinary omniprediction supply a direct reduction?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Is the squared-accuracy cost of fully reliable learning necessary?
author: Sílvia Casacuberta; Varun Kanade
source_title: Selective Omniprediction and Fair Abstention
location: §5 “The complexity of reliable agnostic learning”; Definition 2.5, Theorem 3.3.
text: Is ε² base-learner precision necessary for fully reliable learning: prediction loss≤ε and abstention loss≤inf_{c?∈SC(C)}loss_abst(c?)+ε? Theorem 3.3 obtains both using agnostic-learning time T(ε²/6,δ); can this precision dependence improve?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Sharp noise-margin dependence for certifying halfspace learners
author: Surbhi Goel; Adam Klivans; Konstantinos Stavropoulos; Arsen Vasilyan
source_title: Testing Noise Assumptions of Learning Algorithms
location: Definition 3; Theorem 10 and following paragraph p. 12 (proceedings pp. 2815–2816).
text: For origin-centered halfspaces in R^d, improve or match the(d/ε)^{poly(1/c)} complexity of a tester-learner that accepts Gaussian-Massart data with η(x)≤1/2−c, yet for every joint law D has probability≤δ of accepting a classifier worse than opt_D+ε. What dependence on c>0 is necessary?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: E-values unlocked by iid replication
author: Martin Larsson; Aaditya Ramdas; Johannes Ruf
source_title: Testing hypotheses generated by constraints
text: Describe E({μ^{⊗n}:μ∈P}), n≥2, beyond limits of mixtures of products of one-observation e-variables. Nontrivial rank-based examples exist even when all one-observation e-variables are≤1.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Admissible e-processes for an iid model
author: Martin Larsson; Aaditya Ramdas; Johannes Ruf
source_title: Testing hypotheses generated by constraints
text: For finite Φ, characterize admissible natural-filtration e-processes for {μ^{⊗∞}:μ∈P}, valid at every finite stopping time. How do they differ from processes valid when each conditional law may vary within P?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: E-value duality with one-sided integrability
author: Martin Larsson; Aaditya Ramdas; Johannes Ruf
source_title: Testing hypotheses generated by constraints
text: For infinite Φ, give a dual representation of E(P̃), where P̃ allows E f∈[−∞,0] but requires E f⁺<∞. Finite Φ gives E(P̃)=E(P); an infinite-Φ counterexample rules out that identity generally.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Complete admissibility theory for randomized post-hoc tests
author: Ben Chugg; Tyron Lardy; Aaditya Ramdas; Peter Grünwald
source_title: On admissibility in post-hoc hypothesis testing
text: Characterize randomized C-admissible post-hoc test families δ(x,b)∈[0,1]: E_P[sup_b L_b(0,1)δ(X,b)]≤1, with no other safe family having at least their Q-power for every constant b and more for some b. Are canonical e-value form, likelihood-ratio monotonicity and compatibility sufficient for continuous P,Q? Compatible mixtures of likelihood-ratio tests are an explicit subcase.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: A monotone deterministic improvement of Gaffke’s merger in dimension at least three
author: Jiahao Ming; Aaditya Ramdas; Yi Shen; Ruodu Wang; Ian Waudby-Smith
source_title: Gaffke's confidence interval for the mean of bounded data is inadmissible but asymptotically efficient
text: For every n≥3, is there a measurable, deterministic, coordinatewise nonincreasing F_n≤K_n, strict somewhere, that is a valid p-value for every independent vector E_i≥0 with E E_i≤1? Here K_n(x)=Pr_D(Σ_i x_iD_i≤1), D∼Dirichlet(1,…,1) with coordinates 0,…,n.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The remaining Sobolev two-sample privacy regimes
author: Ilmun Kim; Antonin Schrab
source_title: Differentially Private Permutation Tests
location: v3(29July2026), §5.2 equation(17), Theorem 10 and following paragraph pp. 23–24; §7.
text: For independent n- and m-samples with n≤m≤τn, densities p,q≤M and p−q∈S_d^s(R), determine ρ* when n^{−1/2}≲ξ≲a, or ξ≲n^{−1/2} and s<d/2. Are the respective upper rates(n^{3/2}ξ)^{−s/(2s+d)} and(nξ)^{−2s/(2s+d)} sharp?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Sharp private independence-testing power for smooth departures
author: Ilmun Kim; Antonin Schrab
source_title: Differentially Private Permutation Tests
location: v3 AppendixC.6, Theorem 16, equation(21), final bullet pp. 53–54.
text: For n iid pairs with p_XY,p_Xp_Y≤M and p_XY−p_Xp_Y∈S_d^s(R), d=d_X+d_Y, determine ρ* for independence testing when ξ≲a. Do equation(21)’s intermediate/high-privacy rates match lower bounds?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Minimax smooth two-sample testing under adversarial record corruption
author: Antonin Schrab; Ilmun Kim
source_title: Robust Kernel Hypothesis Testing under Data Corruption
location: §2.1 corruption model and §7 limitations; Schrab thesis §3.7 item 4, with §3.4.3 Sobolev setup.
text: Two n-sample groups have densities p,q≤M on R^d, with p−q∈S_d^s(R). An adversary sees the clean pooled data and replaces at most r records. Determine the minimax L² separation for testing p=q, uniformly over replacements, and the cost of adapting to unknown s. Fixed-kernel MMD rates are already established.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Does arbitrary mixing preserve maximum description gain?
author: Tyron Lardy; Peter Grünwald; Peter Harremoës
source_title: Reverse Information Projections and Optimal E-statistics
location: AppendixC final conjecture; Lardy thesis AppendixA.3 p. 216.
text: For σ-convex subprobabilities C and their Choquet-convex hull C′, does G(P,Q;C)=G(P,Q;C′) for every commonly σ-finitely dominated subprobability P,Q? Here G(P,Q;A)=sup_{R∈A}{∫log(r/q)dP−R(Ω)+Q(Ω)}, with undefined terms counted as−∞. C is closed under countable mixtures; C′ allows arbitrary measurable barycentric mixtures.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Constant-factor decision trees for equally likely hypotheses
author: Ray Li; Percy Liang; Stephen Mussmann
source_title: A Tight Analysis of Greedy Yields Subexponential Time Approximation for Uniform Decision Tree
text: Given an explicit separating table of m binary tests on n equally likely hypotheses, all tests costing 1, does a polynomial-time algorithm output an exact-identification decision tree with expected depth at most a universal constant times optimal? Known constant-factor algorithms are subexponential-time.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Hardness with query prerequisites
author: Michał Szyfelbein; Dariusz Dereniowski
source_title: Precedence-Constrained Decision Trees and Coverings
text: For uniform-prior prerequisite-constrained decision trees, can an m^c inapproximability factor, c>0, be proved under P≠NP for worst-case or average depth, replacing the Planted Dense Subgraph assumption?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Nonuniform-prior query guarantees
author: Michał Szyfelbein; Dariusz Dereniowski
source_title: Precedence-Constrained Decision Trees and Coverings
text: For arbitrary positive rational priors, can polynomial-bit-time algorithms retain O(log n), O(log²n), and O(√m log^(3/2)n) average-depth approximations for inforest, outforest, and arbitrary precedences respectively? Edges run prerequisite→successor; inforests have at most one child and outforests at most one parent.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Bounded prerequisite query bundles
author: Michał Szyfelbein; Dariusz Dereniowski
source_title: Precedence-Constrained Decision Trees and Coverings
text: Given m explicit subsets with a precedence poset and budget b≤m, can a polynomial-time o(m)-approximation maximize |∪C|/|C| over nonempty predecessor-closed subfamilies C with |C|≤b? The budget must hold exactly.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Sharp computational approximation for repeated median testing
author: Martin Hoefer; Kevin Schewior; Daniel Schmand
source_title: Stochastic Probing with Increasing Precision
text: What is the optimal polynomial-time approximation ratio for the adaptive median-testing optimum? Does a PTAS exist, or is there nontrivial approximation hardness? A constant approximation is already proved.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Exact utility loss from partial rather than complete probes
author: Martin Hoefer; Kevin Schewior; Daniel Schmand
source_title: Stochastic Probing with Increasing Precision
text: What is the sharp supremum OPT_full(k)/OPT_median(k), over positive-value instances, when full probes reveal one entire value? Both models may finally choose an unqueried item. This compares unrestricted optimal policies at equal budgets.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Constant approximation for search under a latent mixture
author: Sahil Singla
source_title: Combinatorial Optimization Under Uncertainty: Probing and Stopping-Time Algorithms
text: A known finite latent state S makes nonnegative box values conditionally independent. Opening unused box i costs c_i and reveals its value; S stays hidden. Is a universal constant approximation to E[opening costs+minimum opened value] computable in polynomial time, including online decisions, for explicit rational finite-support mixtures without a separation promise? At least one box must be opened.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Sharp particle accuracy
author: Noah Golowich; Fan Chen; Dhruv Rohatgi; Raghav Singhal; Carles Domingo-Enrich; Dylan J. Foster; Akshay Krishnamurthy
source_title: Reject, Resample, Repeat: Understanding Parallel Reasoning in Language Model Inference
text: For Algorithm 1, Output Option 1, with multinomial resampling and N particles, what is sharp worst-case terminal TV error in horizon H and N under bounded C and χ²(π*_h||πhat_h)≤D at every h, including Vhat=V*?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Minimum particle memory
author: Noah Golowich; Fan Chen; Dhruv Rohatgi; Raghav Singhal; Carles Domingo-Enrich; Dylan J. Foster; Akshay Krishnamurthy
source_title: Reject, Resample, Repeat: Understanding Parallel Reasoning in Language Model Inference
text: For binary actions, C=2,K=e³, find minimal worst-case particle cap N(H) giving TV≤1/3. Particles descend from retained predecessors; stage-h laws use only information through h. Within-stage computation is unrestricted. Output must be a retained terminal particle.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Quadratic query barrier
author: Noah Golowich; Fan Chen; Dhruv Rohatgi; Raghav Singhal; Carles Domingo-Enrich; Dylan J. Foster; Akshay Krishnamurthy
source_title: Reject, Resample, Repeat: Understanding Parallel Reasoning in Language Model Inference
text: For uniform binary proposal, C≤2,K=e³, is it impossible for any o(H²)-prefix-query algorithm, including lookahead/backtracking, to uniformly produce an output law ν ensuring ν(E)≥H^(−1/5) whenever π*(E)≥1/2?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Verifier-robust coverage without enumerating the action alphabet
author: Dhruv Rohatgi; Abhishek Shetty; Donya Saless; Yuchen Li; Ankur Moitra; Andrej Risteski; Dylan J. Foster
source_title: Taming Imperfect Process Verifiers: A Sampling Perspective on Backtracking
text: Can VGB’s average-error coverage theorem extend to a large action alphabet using only proposal sampling, proposal probability evaluation, and Vhat-prefix queries, without an additional uniform bound on Vhat? For δ∈(0,1) and each depth h assume E_{π*}[Vhat/V*]≤1+ε_V and E_{π*}[V*/Vhat]≤1+ε_V. Seek its coverage guarantee Pr_{Y~π*}{π*(Y)/ν(Y)>48H(1+ε_V)²/δ}≤δ with oracle work polynomial in H,1+ε_V,δ^(−1) and the true action-coverage C_act, rather than linear in |A|. Unknown terminal rewards are allowed as in Theorem 4.2.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Optimal first-order query complexity of log-concave inference
author: Sinho Chewi; Jaume de Dios Pont; Jerry Li; Chen Lu; Shyam Narayanan
source_title: Query lower bounds for log-concave sampling
text: For π∝exp(−V) on R^d with V∈C², I≼∇²V≼κI and ∇V(0)=0, determine the minimax number of adaptive exact queries (V(x),∇V(x)) required to output one sample with TV error≤ε. Randomization and arbitrary computation between queries are allowed. Resolve the joint d,κ,ε dependence, including whether a polynomial dimension factor is necessary at fixed κ. This counts oracle queries, not bit operations or function-evaluation cost hidden inside an oracle.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Joint dimension and noise cost of stochastic posterior queries
author: Fan Chen; Sinho Chewi; Constantinos Daskalakis; Alexander Rakhlin
source_title: High-accuracy log-concave sampling with stochastic queries
text: For unbiased gradient samples with E exp(||g−∇f||/σ)≤2, determine sharp query lower bounds jointly in d,κ,σ²/α,δ,Δ. The question concerns parameter interactions beyond the solved light-tail polylog(1/δ) and bounded-variance Θ(1/δ) precision rates.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Optimal finite-sum posterior-sampling budget
author: Fan Chen; Sinho Chewi; Constantinos Daskalakis; Alexander Rakhlin
source_title: High-accuracy log-concave sampling with stochastic queries
text: For f=m^(−1)Σ_i f_i with β-Lipschitz component gradients, determine optimal incremental-gradient complexity jointly in m,d,κ,δ, with Δ=O(d). Each ∇f_i query costs 1; a full gradient costs m. Is Õ(m+κ√(md)) optimal?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Sharp one-dimensional cost of local posterior mixing
author: Sinho Chewi; Patrik Gerber; Holden Lee; Chen Lu
source_title: Fisher information lower bounds for sampling
text: Let π∝exp(−V) on R with V∈C² and |V′(x)−V′(y)|≤|x−y|, without log-concavity. Given free samples from any initialization μ₀ with KL(μ₀||π)≤1 and exact local queries (V(x),V′(x)), determine the minimax query complexity C(1,1,ε;1) of producing ν with FI(ν||π)=∫|(log(dν/dπ))′|²dν≤ε² as ε→0. The remaining gap is between the one-dimensional Ω̃(ε^(−2/3)) lower bound and the O(ε^(−2)) proximal-sampling upper bound.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: A PTAS for unequal-cost fixed-order threshold verification
author: Mads Anker Nielsen; Lars Rohwedder; Kevin Schewior
source_title: Non-Adaptive Evaluation of k-of-n Functions: Tight Gap and a Unit-Cost PTAS
text: For independent Bernoulli bits with explicitly given rational biases p_i and nonnegative rational testing costs c_i, is there a PTAS for the minimum expected cost of a fixed permutation that stops once k ones or n−k+1 zeros have been observed? The ratio is relative to the best nonadaptive permutation, with polynomial input-bit runtime for each fixed approximation ε>0. The unit-cost PTAS and arbitrary-cost adaptivity gap 2 are already proved.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Unknown sensitivity, cumulative regret
author: Meena Jagadeesan; Tijana Zrnic; Celestine Mendler-Dünner
source_title: Regret Minimization with Performative Feedback
text: Without knowing ε, can one retain R_T=O(P_T), up to logarithms, where P_T=T^((d+1)/(d+2))((εL_z)^dB²/m₀)^(1/(d+2))+√T B/√m₀?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Adapting between feedback guarantees
author: Meena Jagadeesan; Tijana Zrnic; Celestine Mendler-Dünner
source_title: Regret Minimization with Performative Feedback
text: If ℓ is also L_Θ-Lipschitz in θ, can one algorithm attain O(min{P_T,Z_T}) cumulative regret, where Z_T=T^((d′+1)/(d′+2))(log T/m₀)^(1/(d′+2))(L_Θ+εL_z)^(d′/(d′+2)) and d′ is the (L_Θ+εL_z)-zooming dimension (Definition 2.3), using the same samples?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Sharp precision versus expansiveness for predictive stability
author: Ioannis Anagnostides; Rohan Chauhan; Ioannis Panageas; Tuomas Sandholm; Jingming Yan
source_title: On the Computational Complexity of Performative Prediction
text: For the source’s well-bounded Euclidean parameter domain and oracle model, determine the largest expansiveness ρ−1, as a function of target accuracy η and the domain/loss parameters, permitting poly(d,log(1/η)) computation of an η-performatively stable point. Close the gap between Theorem 3.5’s O(η⁴) tolerance and the linear-in-η tolerance of the slower fixed-point method, while respecting Theorem 3.4’s hardness constants. Stability means ⟨y−x,E_{D(x)}∇_xℓ(x;z)⟩≥−η for all y in the domain.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The leader-action cost of mutually tolerant learning
author: Kate Donahue; Nicole Immorlica; Meena Jagadeesan; Brendan Lucier; Aleksandrs Slivkins
source_title: Impact of Decentralized Learning on Player Utilities in Stackelberg Games
text: For fixed γ∈(0,1], determine the minimax max{R₁,R₂} jointly in T, |A| and |B| in the shared decentralized model. In particular, close the |A|-dependence between Õ(|A|^(1/3)|B|^(1/3)T^(2/3)) and Ω(|B|^(1/3)T^(2/3)), for γ≫(|A||B|/T)^(1/3), with the displayed logarithmic factors and trivial T cap retained. Both agents may be designed; the stronger upper theorem also permits any follower satisfying its stated high-probability instantaneous-regret guarantee.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Optimal utility-learning round complexity
author: Brian Hu Zhang; Tao Lin; Yiling Chen; Tuomas Sandholm
source_title: Learning a Game by Paying the Agents
text: Determine the minimax rounds for ε-learning, closing the gap between poly(M,C)/ε² and max{Ω̃(nM)log(1/ε),C²/(4ε²)}.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Learning utilities without signals
author: Brian Hu Zhang; Tao Lin; Yiling Chen; Tuomas Sandholm
source_title: Learning a Game by Paying the Agents
text: Without signals, can payments alone ε-learn every n≥2 game in polynomially many rounds? Replace per-signal regret by ordinary anytime regret; payments still depend only on their recipient’s action.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Steering without full identification
author: Brian Hu Zhang; Tao Lin; Yiling Chen; Tuomas Sandholm
source_title: Learning a Game by Paying the Agents
text: Can direct steering avoid the Ω̃(nM)log(1/ε) full-identification bottleneck? Allow correlated private signals and bounded joint-signal/action payments; target the optimal correlated-equilibrium-with-payments value of known mean principal utility minus payments.

subject: Games of Incomplete Information & Bayesian Games
title: Polynomial statistical dependence with hidden follower types
author: Gerson Personnat; Tao Lin; Safwan Hossain; David C. Parkes
source_title: Learning to Play Multi-Follower Bayesian Stackelberg Games
text: In repeated Bayesian Stackelberg games with L leader actions, n followers, K types per follower and A follower actions, can action-only feedback achieve expected regret poly(n,K,L,A)√T (up to logarithms) against the optimal fixed leader mixture? Types are drawn i.i.d. each round from an unknown possibly correlated joint distribution; payoffs are known, each follower myopically best responds without inter-follower externalities, and ties favor the leader. Computational time may be exponential in L; the question concerns regret dependence.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Fully polynomial normal-form correlation with hidden information
author: Ioannis Anagnostides; Constantinos Daskalakis; Gabriele Farina; Noah Golowich; Tuomas Sandholm; Brian Hu Zhang
source_title: Normal-Form Correlation in Markov Games
text: Is there an FPTAS for finding an ε-normal-form correlated equilibrium in a finite two-player perfect-recall extensive-form game with imperfect information and rational payoffs in [0,1]? Recommendations disclose each player’s entire contingent plan before play, and deviations may depend on that recommendation. Use the primary sources’ efficiently representable finite-support distributions over mixed strategy profiles, rather than expanding the exponentially large pure normal form. Time should be polynomial in game-tree encoding and 1/ε.

subject: Games of Incomplete Information & Bayesian Games
title: Optimal conventions robust to choosing whose advice to inspect
author: Brian Hu Zhang; Ioannis Anagnostides; Emanuel Tewolde; Ratip Emin Berker; Gabriele Farina; Vincent Conitzer; Tuomas Sandholm
source_title: Expected Variational Inequalities
text: For a rational finite normal-form game with a fixed number n of players, what is the complexity of maximizing expected social welfare over anonymous linear correlated equilibria? Such an equilibrium is a distribution μ over mixed profiles x, satisfying E_μ[u_i(φ_i(x),x_{−i})−u_i(x)]≤0 for every player i and every linear map φ_i:∏_jΔ(A_j)→Δ(A_i). Exact or additive-ε optimum should have an explicit bit/precision complexity. Restricting μ to pure profiles changes the problem.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Learning an optimal convention from trajectory-only steering
author: Brian Hu Zhang; Gabriele Farina; Ioannis Anagnostides; Federico Cacciamani; Stephen Marcus McAleer; Andreas Alexander Haupt; Andrea Celli; Nicola Gatti; Vincent Conitzer; Tuomas Sandholm
source_title: Steering No-Regret Learners to a Desired Equilibrium
text: Can extensive-form online steering compute a mediator-optimal Bayes-correlated equilibrium while inducing it, when the mediator observes only reached terminal trajectories? Use the known finite perfect-recall game, private recommendations and nonnegative terminal-node payments of §§5–6. Players are arbitrary no-regret learners for payment-augmented utilities, with known normalized regret bound R(T). Seek vanishing average realized payments, obedience/directness error and mediator optimality gap, preferably T^(−c) for c>0 when R(T)=O(√T); per-round offers may grow with T. Do not assume a target equilibrium precomputed.

subject: Games of Incomplete Information & Bayesian Games
title: Can extra signal labels reduce binary persuasion learning regret?
author: Ce Li; Tao Lin
source_title: Information Design with Unknown Prior
text: In repeated persuasion with two receiver actions, known bounded sender/receiver payoffs and an unknown full-support prior μ, what is the optimal regret order if the designer may use more than two signals per round? The receiver knows μ, updates by Bayes’ rule and best responds; the designer sees only the signal and chosen action. States are i.i.d.; retain the known positive prior lower bound and non-dominated-action assumption. Regret is T·OPT(μ) minus cumulative expected sender utility. The Ω(log log T) lower bound currently assumes two signals, even with two states.

subject: Games of Incomplete Information & Bayesian Games
title: Finite patience and information value
author: Dimitry Shaiderman
source_title: On the Monotonicity and Rate of Convergence of the Markovian Persuasion Value
text: An informed sender commits to signals about a finite irreducible Markov chain M. A myopic Bayesian receiver, with finite actions or [0,1], breaks ties for the sender. Let v_δ(q)=sup_σE[(1−δ)Σ_nδ^(n−1)u(p_n)], where p_n is its posterior and u≥0 is upper-semicontinuous. For invariant π and point-masses e_k, set Φ(δ)=v_δ(π), Ψ(δ)=Σ_kπ_kv_δ(e_k). Can Φ>Ψ below some δ₀∈(0,1), with Φ(δ₀)=Ψ(δ₀)?

subject: Games of Incomplete Information & Bayesian Games
title: Sharp ergodic discount convergence
author: Dimitry Shaiderman
source_title: On the Monotonicity and Rate of Convergence of the Markovian Persuasion Value
text: For finite zero-sum Markov-chain games with an exogenous irreducible aperiodic transition matrix M, determine the sharp worst-case order, as δ↑1, of sup_q|V_δ(q)−V_∞|. Player 1 observes the current state and hence the payoff matrix; Player 2 does not. Actions are simultaneous and then public; only Player 1 observes the realized payoff. The known uniform bound is O((1−δ)log²(1/(1−δ))), with game-dependent constants. Is the logarithmic loss necessary, and how does the sharp bound depend on mixing?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: One off-policy learner adapting to every comparator’s coverage
author: Germano Gabbianelli; Gergely Neu; Matteo Papini
source_title: Online Learning with Off-Policy Feedback
text: In K-action online learning, an adaptive adversary selects r_t∈[0,1]^K before current random actions. The learner samples from π_t but sees only (A_t^B,r_t(A_t^B)) for an independent fixed behavior policy π_B. With C(π;π_B)=Σ_aπ(a)/π_B(a) and R_T(π)=Σ_t⟨π−π_t,r_t⟩, can one algorithm achieve E R_T(π)=Õ(√(T C(π;π_B))) simultaneously for every supported comparator π, without tuning to its coverage? The fixed known-behavior case is the base target; current tuning-independent bounds are linear in C.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: High-probability square-root coverage for off-policy control
author: Francesco Bacchiocchi; Francesco Emanuele Stradi; Matteo Papini; Alberto Maria Metelli; Nicola Gatti
source_title: Online Learning with Off-Policy Feedback in Adversarial MDPs
text: In the source’s finite L-stage loop-free MDP with known transitions and known fixed logging policy π_C, can off-policy regret against a fixed supported comparator π* have a high-probability bound with square-root rather than linear dependence on D=Σ_{x,a}q^{π*}(x,a)/q^{π_C}(x,a)? Rewards r_t(x,a)∈[0,1] form an arbitrary fixed sequence; each episode reveals only the logger’s trajectory and rewards. Seek the expected-bound scale Õ(√(LTD)), with explicit δ and lower-order terms, or establish the necessary larger dependence.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Can hybrid feedback avoid the price of choosing a learning method?
author: Duo Cheng; Xingyu Zhou; Bo Ji
source_title: Hybrid Reinforcement Learning in Adversarial Markov Decision Processes
text: For K actions and an oblivious loss sequence ℓ_t∈[0,1]^K, each round reveals both the loss of the learner’s sampled action and one fresh action–loss pair from a known fixed logger π_B. Can one algorithm guarantee EΣ_t⟨π_t−π,ℓ_t⟩=Õ(√(T·min{K,C(π)})) simultaneously for every comparator π, where C(π)=Σ_aπ(a)/π_B(a)? The known universal bound is Õ(√T·min{K,√C(π)}). Preserve the one-plus-one observation budget. Use 0/0=0 and positive/0=∞.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: When does conservative revision learn infinite hypothesis spaces?
author: Edoardo Baccini; Zoé Christoff; Nina Gierasimczuk; Rineke Verbrugge
source_title: Who is Afraid of Minimal Revision?
text: Characterise the priors under which minimal revision learns arbitrary such spaces from every sound, complete stream, and hence identify spaces admitting such a prior.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Conservative revision after finitely many corrected errors
author: Edoardo Baccini; Zoé Christoff; Nina Gierasimczuk; Rineke Verbrugge
source_title: Who is Afraid of Minimal Revision?
text: Characterise successful priors for negation-closed spaces with fair streams: every true observable appears, finitely many observations are false, and each false observation is later followed by its complement. The finite-space case remains included.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Deciding probabilistic action specifications with unrestricted branching
author: Daniil Kozhemiachenko; Igor Sedlár
source_title: Reasoning About Probabilities, Actions, and Knowledge in Fuzzy Modal Logic
text: Is satisfiability for the full EA^Pr language decidable over arbitrary frames, and what is its exact computational complexity?

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: A complete calculus for probability, knowledge and actions
author: Daniil Kozhemiachenko; Igor Sedlár
source_title: Reasoning About Probabilities, Actions, and Knowledge in Fuzzy Modal Logic
text: Give a sound and complete axiomatization of EA^Pr, with its stated probabilistic-frame semantics.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: The uniform-reliability dichotomy beyond graph queries
author: Antoine Amarilli
source_title: Uniform Reliability for Unbounded Homomorphism-Closed Graph Queries
text: For every fixed homomorphism-closed Boolean query Q over a finite relational signature of arbitrary arity, is counting the subsets J⊆I satisfying Q polynomial-time exactly when Q is equivalent to a safe union of conjunctive queries, and #P-hard otherwise? Here safe means polynomial-time evaluation on tuple-independent probabilistic databases.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Which value-bearing relation permits tractable evidence attribution?
author: Christoph Standke; Benny Kimelfeld
source_title: Tractability Frontiers of the Shapley Value for Aggregate Conjunctive Queries
text: Classify exact Shapley-value computation for A=α∘τ∘Q when Q is a fixed self-join-free conjunctive query, α is average, a fixed rational q-quantile (0<q<1), or has-duplicates, and τ is a polynomial-time value function localized on a specified atom of Q. Seek the tractability frontier for each pair (Q,localization atom), uniformly over its allowed τ. Database facts are partitioned into endogenous players and fixed exogenous facts; Shapley averages a fact’s marginal change in A over all player orders. Localized means that τ depends only on answer coordinates occurring in the designated atom. Set α(∅)=0 and use the source’s quantile convention.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Exact complexity of plausibly most likely explanations
author: Tommaso Flaminio; Katsumi Inoue; Daniil Kozhemiachenko
source_title: Probabilistic Abduction in a Fuzzy Logic Framework
text: Given finite propositional theory φ, observation χ, hypothesis literals H, rational probability assignments p on a finite event set E, and a conjunction τ of H (all variables occur in φ or χ), determine the exact complexity of preferred-solution recognition. A solution σ satisfies φ∧σ⊨χ and has μ(φ∧σ)>0 for some μ matching p. A solution τ is preferred iff for every solution σ there exists a μ matching p with μ(τ)≥μ(σ). Retain ∀σ∃μ; one common maximizing distribution is not required. The known upper bound is Π₂^P.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Can edge interventions distinguish identical latent projections?
author: Marina Maciel Ansanelli; Elie Wolfe; Robert W. Spekkens
source_title: Everything that can be learned about a causal structure with latent variables by observational and interventional probing schemes
text: For two finite classical partitioned DAGs with identical visible alphabets inducing the same mDAG, can a visible-node probing scheme allowing edge interventions distinguish their realizable statistics? Such interventions send different values to different children. Latent cardinalities are unrestricted. The authors conjecture no.

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Completeness of graphical computation for causal kernels
author: Martin Rabel; Jakob Runge
source_title: Symmetries and Causality: Causal Effect Identification Beyond IID Data
text: If μ(G, L) is standard-regularly computable from supplied structured kernels K, must simplification, c-component decomposition, gluing and revealing suffice?

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Can every causal fusion proof postpone all gluing?
author: Martin Rabel; Jakob Runge
source_title: Symmetries and Causality: Causal Effect Identification Beyond IID Data
text: Can every graphical derivation between such kernels be reordered so all gluing occurs last, preserving its inputs and target?

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Parameterized hardness of ancestry-constrained network learning
author: Juha Harviainen; Pekka Parviainen
source_title: On Tractability of Learning Bayesian Networks with Ancestral Constraints
text: Is optimization W[1]-hard parameterized by pc(P), or by (pc(A), pc(A*)) in the positive-ancestry regime?

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Learning with both precedence and positive ancestry restrictions
author: Juha Harviainen; Pekka Parviainen
source_title: On Tractability of Learning Bayesian Networks with Ancestral Constraints
text: With both P and A imposed, does bounding either path-cover number suffice for polynomial time, or is optimization hard even when both are bounded?

title: Optimal efficient reconstruction of doubly permuted reliability matrices
author: Emmanuel Pilliat; Alexandra Carpentier; Nicolas Verzelen
source_title: Optimal rates for ranking a permuted isotonic matrix in polynomial time
text: Can polynomial-time reconstruction attain worst-case expected squared Frobenius error O~(n/λ), or is there a computational-statistical gap?

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Subexponential tree aggregation without irreducibility assumptions
author: Yashodhan Kanoria; Andrea Montanari
source_title: Subexponential convergence for information aggregation on regular trees
text: Must P_e(t)=exp[-o(k^t)] without any of §IV.B’s irreducibility assumptions? No internal node receives an extra private signal.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Do signed latent models realize every nested-Markov law?
author: Paul Becsi; Matty J. Hoban
source_title: Bounding Classical and Quantum Correlations in Bayesian Networks with Quasiprobabilities
text: Is W(G)=N(G) for every G and finite observed alphabet assignment?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Exact complexity of DAG-constrained linear probability feasibility
author: Markus Bläser; Julian Dörfler; Maciej Liśkiewicz; Benito van der Zander
source_title: Probabilistic and Causal Satisfiability: Constraining the Model
text: Determine satisfiability by a Markovian SCM whose functional-dependence graph is contained in G, without small-support restrictions. Is SAT^{lin⟨Σ⟩}_{DAG, L1} ∃R^Σ-complete (existential real feasibility with succinct summation)?

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Is the nearest undirected dependence model one edge away?
author: Juha Harviainen; Pekka Parviainen; Vidya Sagar Sharma
source_title: Learning Bayesian and Markov Networks with an Unreliable Oracle
text: For every undirected G with |V|≥2, does some minimizer of d(G, H), H≠G, differ by exactly one added or deleted edge?

subject: Experimental Design & Causal Inference
title: Is the nearest causal equivalence class one arc edit away?
author: Juha Harviainen; Pekka Parviainen; Vidya Sagar Sharma
source_title: Learning Bayesian and Markov Networks with an Unreliable Oracle
text: For every DAG D with |V|≥2, does a minimum-positive-distance alternative arise by one arc addition, deletion or reversal, while remaining acyclic?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Does square-summable updating preserve a predictive density?
author: Samuele Garelli; Fabrizio Leisen; Luca Pratelli; Pietro Rigo
source_title: Asymptotics of predictive distributions driven by sample means and variances
text: Fix positive density f_0 on R, positive bivariate copula density c, and deterministic r_n∈(0, 1] with ∑r_n=∞, ∑r_n²<∞. Draw X_{n+1}∼f_n and update f_{n+1}(x)=f_n(x)[1−r_n+r_n c(F_n(x), F_n(X_{n+1}))], where F_n is the CDF. Must f_n(x)dx converge almost surely in total variation to its weak limit? No boundedness of c is assumed.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Sharp decision-distinguishability distortion from averaging sensors
author: Aryeh Kontorovich
source_title: A homogenization principle for total variation
text: For probability measures P_i, Q_i on one measurable space, let P̄=n^{-1}∑P_i, Q̄=n^{-1}∑Q_i. What is the largest universal c such that TV(⊗P_i,⊗Q_i)≥c TV(P̄^{⊗n}, Q̄^{⊗n}) for all n? Is c=8/9?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Which fully parameterized latent tensors are uniquely decomposable?
author: Jonathan D. Hauenstein; Luke Oeding; Giorgio Ottaviani; Andrew J. Sommese
source_title: Homotopy techniques for tensor decomposition and perfect identifiability
text: For d≥3, n_i≥2 and integer R=∏n_i/[1+∑(n_i−1)], are the only complex tensor formats with a generically unique minimal rank-one decomposition (2, k, k), (3, 4, 5), and (2, 2, 2, 3), up to permuting modes? Uniqueness ignores component permutation and rescaling.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Does optimal nonnegative compression retain unique latent components?
author: Yang Qi
source_title: A Very Brief Introduction to Nonnegative Tensors from the Geometric Viewpoint
text: Assume the real tensor space V=⊗_{i=1}^d R^{n_i}, d≥3, is generically r-identifiable. For general T≥0 with nonnegative rank>r, does its unique Frobenius-nearest tensor of nonnegative rank≤r also have a unique nonnegative rank-r decomposition, modulo permutation and rescaling? Boundary minimizers remain included.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Realizability of the remaining five-variable entropy rays
author: Laszlo Csirmaz
source_title: Exploring the entropic region
text: Which of Γ_5’s117, 983 extremal rays contain a nonzero entropic vector, and which lie in the almost-entropic cone?

author: Laszlo Csirmaz
source_title: Exploring the entropic region

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Rational certificates for alternative entropy guarantees
author: Mahmoud Abo Khamis; Phokion G. Kolaitis; Hung Q. Ngo; Dan Suciu
source_title: Bag Query Containment and Information Theory
text: For rational homogeneous linear entropy forms E_1,…, E_m, suppose max_j E_j(h)≥0 for every finite-variable entropy vector h. Must there be rational λ_j≥0 summing to 1 with ∑λ_jE_j(h)≥0 for all such h? Real witnesses are known to exist.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Almost-linear stability for a six-variable dependence certificate
author: Laszlo Csirmaz
source_title: Revisiting the Stability of the Ingleton Inequality: A Tropicalization-Free Approach
text: For finite-valued jointly distributed x, y, a, b, c, d, define ing(x, y, a, b)=−I(x; y)+I(x; y|a)+I(x; y|b)+I(a; b), A=I(x; a|y)+I(y; a|x), B=I(x; b|y)+I(y; b|x), S=ing(x, y, a, b)+ing(x, y, c, d)+A−B. Is (2^k−1)S+I(x; y|a)+(k2^k−k)A+k2^kB≥0 for every integer k≥1?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Can a stochastic interpretation forget its exact randomization weights?
author: Thomas A. Henzinger; Keya Prakash; K. S. Thejaswini
source_title: Resolving Nondeterminism with Randomness
text: Does changing only a finite-memory SR resolver’s positive transition probabilities, preserving their supports, initial memory and memory updates, preserve almost-sure correctness?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Decide whether temporal ambiguity has a finite-memory random resolver
author: Thomas A. Henzinger; Keya Prakash; K. S. Thejaswini
source_title: Resolving Nondeterminism with Randomness
text: Is SR membership decidable for Büchi and coBüchi automata?
