author: Thomas A. Henzinger; Keya Prakash; K. S. Thejaswini
source_title: Resolving Nondeterminism with Randomness
text: Does every n-state HD parity automaton have a language-equivalent MA parity automaton with at most n states?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Exact equivalence of one-symbol credal sequence sensors
author: Gerco van Heerdt; Justin Hsu; Joël Ouaknine; Alexandra Silva
source_title: Convex language semantics for nondeterministic probabilistic automata
text: For two finite unary automata, let each state s have rational terminal weight γ(s)∈[0, 1] and finite nonempty set D_s of rational transition distributions. Set v_0=γ and v_{t+1}(s)=max_{d∈D_s}∑_q d(q)v_t(q). Is equality of their initial-state values for every t≥0 decidable? Min semantics reduces to max by complementing terminal weights.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Exact probability that one uncertain report occurs inside another
author: Antoine Amarilli; Mikaël Monet; Paul Raphaël; Sylvain Salvati
source_title: On the Complexity of Language Membership for Probabilistic Words
text: Given independent probabilistic words p, p′, what is the exact complexity of Pr[U is a contiguous factor of U′], U∼p, U′∼p′: polynomial time or #P-hard?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Must tractable language inference admit a compact executable representation?
author: Antoine Amarilli; Mikaël Monet; Paul Raphaël; Sylvain Salvati
source_title: On the Complexity of Language Membership for Probabilistic Words
text: Does some CFL L have #pM(L)∈FP but no polynomial-time constructor for circuits representing L∩Σ^n using decomposable Cartesian products, smooth disjoint unions and complements?

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Exact complexity of exhaustive unambiguous semantic coverage
author: Lorenzo Clemente
source_title: On the Complexity of the Universality and Inclusion Problems for Unambiguous Context-Free Grammars
text: Given a grammar G promised unambiguous, what is the exact complexity of testing L(G)=Σ*? Is polynomial time possible? This also asks whether the coin-flip language measure equals 1.

subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
title: Recognize exact finite-state replacements for unambiguous grammars
author: Lorenzo Clemente
source_title: On the Complexity of the Universality and Inclusion Problems for Unambiguous Context-Free Grammars
text: Given a grammar promised unambiguous, is regularity of its generated language decidable?

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Sharp value of adapting a risky computation schedule
author: Zohar Barak; Inbal Talgam-Cohen
source_title: Stochastic Knapsack: Semi-Adaptivity Gaps and Improved Approximation
text: Determine sup_I A_*(I)/A_0(I), over all finite Risky-SK instances with A_0(I)>0. Close the current lower bound 2 and upper bound 2φ³≈8.47, where φ=(1+√5)/2.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: A tighter LP certificate for risky computation value
author: Zohar Barak; Inbal Talgam-Cohen
source_title: Stochastic Knapsack: Semi-Adaptivity Gaps and Improved Approximation
text: Set μ_i=E[min{S_i, 1}], w_i=v_i Pr(S_i≤1), and Φ(1)=max{Σ_i w_i x_i:Σ_i μ_i x_i≤1, 0≤x_i≤1}. Is A_*≤(3/2)Φ(1) for every Risky-SK instance?

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Are near-constant noisy query designs globally optimal?
author: Junren Chen; Jonathan Scarlett
source_title: Exact Thresholds for Noisy Non-Adaptive Group Testing
text: Fix 0<θ<1 and 0<ρ<1/2, let k=⌊n^θ⌋, and draw S uniformly among k-subsets. Each nonadaptive OR test is independently flipped with probability ρ. Is the supremum achievable exact-recovery rate liminf log₂(binomial(n, k))/T over all designs equal to that over near-constant-column designs, optimized over ν>0? In the latter, each item independently chooses L=⌊νT/k⌋ tests uniformly with replacement. Achievable means Pr(Ŝ≠S)→0; decoding time is unrestricted.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Exact information rate of noisy adaptive diagnosis
author: Matthew Aldridge; Oliver Johnson; Jonathan Scarlett
source_title: Group Testing: An Information Theory Perspective, Second Edition
location: Open Problem 12; §5.2.2; Scarlett 2019 model and bounds.
text: For S uniform among k=⌊n^θ⌋ subsets of [n], 0<θ<1, an adaptive OR query is independently flipped with known probability 0<ρ<1/2. Determine the supremum liminf log₂(binomial(n, k))/T_n over strategies using at most T_n tests on every history and satisfying Pr(Ŝ≠S)→0. Queries may depend on all earlier results; the number of adaptive stages and decoding computation are unrestricted.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Order-optimal noisy observations and decoding together
author: Xiaxin Li; Arya Mazumdar
source_title: Noisy Nonadaptive Group Testing with Binary Splitting: New Test Design and Improvement on Price-Scarlett-Tan’s Scheme
text: For every fixed θ∈(0, 1), ρ∈(0, 1/2), and k=Θ(n^θ), does a nonadaptive noisy OR-testing scheme achieve exact recovery with error o(1), using both T=O(k log n) tests and O(k log n) word-RAM decoding operations? Outcomes are independently flipped with probability ρ. Use the small-error uniform-support model, randomized design, and random access to tests/results; matrix construction time is separate.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Best acquisition constant with near-linear sparse decoding
author: Hsin-Po Wang; Ryan Gabrys; Venkatesan Guruswami
source_title: Quickly-Decodable Group Testing with Fewer Tests: Price-Scarlett and Cheraghchi-Nakos’s Nonadaptive Splitting with Explicit Scalars
text: For each fixed θ∈(0, 1), k=⌊n^θ⌋, noiseless nonadaptive OR tests and a uniform k-subset, what is the infimum achievable leading constant a(θ) in T=(a(θ)+o(1))k ln n when exact-recovery error tends to zero and decoding uses O(k log n) word operations? In particular, can a(θ)<(ln 2)^(−2) be achieved? Random-access design/outcome lookup is allowed; construction time is not decoder time.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Efficient certainty-preserving partial diagnosis at rate one
author: Daniel McMorrow; Jonathan Scarlett
source_title: Optimal Non-Adaptive Group Testing with One-Sided Error Guarantees
text: Let S be a uniform k=⌊n^θ⌋ subset, ln(2)/(1+ln(2))<θ<1. Under noiseless nonadaptive OR queries, can a polynomial-time design/decoder attain rate 1 and, with probability 1−o(1), output Ŝ⊂S with |Ŝ|≥(1−η)k whenever η=o(1) and η=Ω(k^(−λ(1/θ−1))) for fixed 0<λ<1/2? Rate is liminf log₂(binomial(n, k))/T. Preserve zero false positives on the successful event.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: A universal lower bound for selectable-threshold sensors
author: Trung-Khang Tran; Daniel McMorrow; Jonathan Scarlett
source_title: Group Testing with Selectable Thresholds
location: Theorems 5–6, Lemma 1 and §IV “Converse for arbitrary designs”.
text: Fix r≥2, θ∈(0, 1), k=⌊n^θ⌋, and uniform S. Nonadaptive test t selects Q_t⊂[n] and γ_t∈{1,…, r}, returning 1{|Q_t∩S|≥γ_t}. Does every design with exact-recovery success bounded away from zero require T≥(1−o(1))k ln k/B_r, where B_r=max_{u>0} −u ln(1−u^(r−1)e^(−u)/(r−1)!)? Remove the paper’s degree-regularity and small-pairwise-overlap assumptions; tests have no repeated item.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Sharp query cost with bounded pool sizes
author: Nelvin Tan; Way Tan; Jonathan Scarlett
source_title: Performance Bounds for Group Testing With Doubly-Regular Designs
text: For fixed θ,β∈(0, 1), k=⌊n^θ⌋ and ρ=⌊(n/k)^β⌋, determine the sharp asymptotic number of tests needed for Pr(Ŝ≠S)→0 when every pool has at most ρ items. Close the remaining leading-constant gap at scale n/ρ; the constant-pool case β=0 is excluded.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: One-sided approximate recovery in the dense regime
author: Nelvin Tan; Way Tan; Jonathan Scarlett
source_title: Performance Bounds for Group Testing With Doubly-Regular Designs
text: For fixed p∈(0, 1), δ∈(0, 1) and k=⌊pn⌋, determine the optimal leading test density T/n for Pr(Ŝ⊂S and |S∖Ŝ|≤δk)→1. In particular, obtain matching achievable and converse bounds for this false-negatives-only criterion; sparse k=o(n) results do not settle it.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Fast decoding with tightly limited evidence reuse
author: Eric Price; Jonathan Scarlett; Nelvin Tan
source_title: Fast Splitting Algorithms for Sparsity-Constrained and Noisy Group Testing
text: Fix θ,δ∈(0, 1), k=⌊n^θ⌋ and γ=⌊(ln n)^(1−δ)⌋. With noiseless nonadaptive OR tests and each item in at most γ pools, can exact recovery with error o(1) attain T=O(γk max{k, n/k}^(1/γ)) with o(n) word-RAM decoding operations? Require randomized for-each recovery and random-access outcomes/design lookup; design construction time is separate.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Optimal information threshold with limited item participation
author: Oliver Gebhard; Max Hahn-Klimroth; Olaf Parczyk; Manuel Penschuck; Maurice Rolvien; Jonathan Scarlett; Nelvin Tan
source_title: Near-Optimal Sparsity-Constrained Group Testing: Improved Bounds and Algorithms
location: §III equations (6), Theorems 3.1–3.4 and following open-problem paragraph.
text: Fix 0<θ<1/2 and 0<δ<1; let k=⌊n^θ⌋ and Δ=⌊(ln n)^(1−δ)⌋. For a uniform k-subset and noiseless nonadaptive OR tests with each item in at most Δ pools, determine the exact recovery threshold at scale M=Δk(n/k)^(1/Δ). Is the best possible test count asymptotic to M/e, M, or an intermediate constant times M? Decoding is unrestricted; error must tend to zero.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Order-optimal inference for every monotone pooled sensor
author: Xiwei Cheng; Sidharth Jaggi; Qiaoqiao Zhou
source_title: Generalized Group Testing
location: Conjecture 1; equations (4)–(14), Definition 9 and equation (23), September 2022 v4.
text: Let d=⌊n^θ⌋, 0<θ<1, and known nonconstant nondecreasing f:{0,…, d}→[0, 1]. A pool containing j defectives returns Bernoulli(f(j)), conditionally independently. Put B~Bin(d−1, q), a(q)=E f(B+1), b(q)=E f(B), Δ(q)=(1−q)(a(q)−b(q)), and G(q)=min{a(q), 1−b(q)}(1−q)/(qΔ(q)²). For Z_χ~Hypergeom(n, d,χ), set h(f)=min_{1≤χ<n, Var(f(Z_χ))>0} E[f(Z_χ)](1−E[f(Z_χ)])/Var(f(Z_χ)). Is inf_{0<q<1}G(q)=Θ(d h(f)) uniformly over such sensor families? This is Conjecture 1 with the fixed-error logarithm and numerical constant in Γ removed.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: When do pooled tests stop saving worst-case queries?
author: M. C. Hu; F. K. Hwang; Ju Kwei Wang
source_title: A Boundary Problem for Group Testing
text: For integers 0<d<n with d≥n/3, must every adaptive noiseless OR-testing strategy that identifies every d-subset of [n] require at least n−1 tests in the worst case? Equivalently, is M(d, n)=n−1 throughout that range, where M is the minimum worst-case test count and d is known?

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Do pairwise queries achieve the best nested Bayesian policy?
author: Yaakov Malinovsky
source_title: Conjectures on Optimal Nested Generalized Group Testing Algorithm
location: Conjecture 2; 2025 follow-up Definition 2, Conjecture 2 and Comment 1(a).
text: Let independent X_i~Bern(p_i), with p_i∈[1−1/√2,(3−√5)/2]. Does some ordering make GPTA minimize expected noiseless OR-test count among all nested strategies identifying every X_i? GPTA tests the first remaining pair; after a positive result it tests the member with smaller p_i, infers the partner if negative, otherwise returns that partner to its original position among unclassified items; a lone item is tested. A nested strategy, while a group is known to contain an unresolved defective, next tests a proper subset of that group.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Exact eleven-query capacity for two hidden failures
author: Fedor Karpelevitch
source_title: Certified exact bounds for adaptive quantitative group testing with two defectives
text: What is the largest n for which M(K_n)≤11? An eleven-test strategy is known for n=328; maximality remains unproved, including whether n=329 or 330 can be resolved.

subject: Information Theory & Coding
title: Does imbalance reduce two-failure query complexity?
author: Fedor Karpelevitch
source_title: Certified exact bounds for adaptive quantitative group testing with two defectives
text: For all n≥m>1 and integers k≥0, does M(K_{n, m})≤k imply M(K_{n+1, m−1})≤k? The prior information is exactly one defective in each of two disjoint sets; this is the source’s antidiagonal-transfer conjecture.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Admissibility of exchangeability-aware calibration mergers
author: Matteo Gasparin; Ruodu Wang; Aaditya Ramdas
source_title: Combining exchangeable P-values
text: For the calibrator construction F_f(p)=inf{α∈(0, 1): max_{k≤K}k⁻¹Σ_{i≤k}f(p_i/α)≥1}, inf∅=1, characterize admissibility among deterministic increasing Borel ex-p-mergers: G≤F_f implies G=F_f. Here K≥2; f is nonnegative and nonincreasing, vanishes above 1 and ∫₀¹f≤1; validity means Pr(G(P)≤α)≤α for every exchangeable uniform-marginal vector P. The arithmetic K=2 case is already inadmissible.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Domain-independent computation beyond proper model selection
author: Anders Aamand; Maryam Aliakbarpour; Justin Y. Chen; Sandeep Silwal
source_title: How fast can you find a good hypothesis?
text: Can an improper algorithm achieve an absolute constant C<3 with O(log(N/δ)/ε²) P-samples and finite runtime independent of domain size? The solved mixture ratio 3−2/N is insufficient.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: High-confidence model selection in near-linear time
author: Anders Aamand; Maryam Aliakbarpour; Justin Y. Chen; Sandeep Silwal
source_title: How fast can you find a good hypothesis?
text: Can a proper C=3 selector use O(log(N/δ)/ε²) P-samples and Õ(N log(1/δ)/ε²) time, without known OPT or class preprocessing?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The full confidence cost of distribution clustering
author: Gunjan Kumar; Yash Pote; Jonathan Scarlett
source_title: A Distribution Testing Approach to Clustering Distributions
text: For d=2, determine minimax total samples jointly in n, k, r,ε,δ for success 1−δ, in both known/unknown-law variants.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Clustering an increasing number of distinct sensor laws
author: Gunjan Kumar; Yash Pote; Jonathan Scarlett
source_title: A Distribution Testing Approach to Clustering Distributions
text: For unknown group laws and d→∞, determine minimax samples jointly in n, k, d,ε and group sizes, with success 2/3.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Is adaptive sampling necessary to cluster distributions?
author: Gunjan Kumar; Yash Pote; Jonathan Scarlett
source_title: A Distribution Testing Approach to Clustering Distributions
text: For d=2 and success 2/3, is there a strict gap between adaptive sampling and fixed-in-advance allocations, with matched cluster-size information?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The remaining accuracy cost of support-size diagnosis
author: Renato Ferreira Pinto Jr.; Nathaniel Harms
source_title: Testing Support Size More Efficiently Than Learning Histograms
text: Close the minimax gap Ω(n/(ε log n)) versus O((n/(ε log n))min{log(1/ε), log n}) for distinguishing d_n(p)=0 from d_n(p)>ε.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Tolerant support diagnosis without a support-size promise
author: Renato Ferreira Pinto Jr.; Nathaniel Harms
source_title: Testing Support Size More Efficiently Than Learning Histograms
text: For 0≤ε′<ε<1, can d_n(p)≤ε′ versus d_n(p)>ε be tested with (n/log n)·Õ((ε−ε′)⁻²) samples, without a bound on the true support?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Removing the log cost of dependent missing-mass estimation
author: Ashwin Pananjady; Vidya Muthukumar; Andrew Thangaraj
source_title: Just Wing It: Near-Optimal Estimation of Missing Mass in a Markovian Sequence
text: Is minimax MSE for M₀ O(T/n) when n≳T log n, removing the known log(n/T) factor?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Linear mixing-time variance of unseen stationary mass
author: Ashwin Pananjady; Vidya Muthukumar; Andrew Thangaraj
source_title: Just Wing It: Near-Optimal Estimation of Missing Mass in a Markovian Sequence
text: Does Var(M₀)≤C min{T log(1+n/T)/n, 1} hold universally, replacing T² in Theorem 2?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The rare-count mass estimation frontier
author: Ashwin Pananjady; Vidya Muthukumar; Andrew Thangaraj
source_title: Just Wing It: Near-Optimal Estimation of Missing Mass in a Markovian Sequence
text: For 1≤ζ=o(n), determine minimax MSE for M_ζ jointly in n,ζ, T. Are O(min{(ζ+1)T log(1+n/T)/n, 1}) and iid O(min{(ζ+1)/n, 1}) sharp?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The exact minimax constant for unseen probability mass
author: Jayadev Acharya; Yelun Bao; Yuheng Kang; Ziteng Sun
source_title: Improved Bounds for Minimax Risk of Estimating Missing Mass
text: For iid X₁: n∼p on an unrestricted countable alphabet, let M₀=Σ_xp_x1{N_x=0} and R_n*=inf_Mhat sup_p E_p[(Mhat−M₀)²]. Does lim_n nR_n* exist, and is it c_u=max_{x∈(0, 1]} x e^(−x)(1−e^(−x))²/[1−e^(−x)−x e^(−x)]≈0.570077, the uniform-family constant?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Accurate gradients throughout adaptive model fitting
author: Roi Livni
source_title: Making Progress Based on False Discoveries
text: What dimension-independent dataset size permits ε-accurate population gradients throughout T=Θ(ε⁻²) projected-GD steps, η=Θ(ε), with probability≥0.99? Start w₁=0, use w_{t+1}=Π_B₂(w_t−ηg_t), and require ||g_t−E_D∇f(w_t, X)||₂≤ε simultaneously. Sample losses are convex1-Lipschitz; use the source’s fixed subgradient convention. The oracle may access the full losses on its iid dataset; neither post-hoc generalization nor first-order-access restrictions are imposed. Can O(ε⁻²) samples suffice?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Gaussian uncertainty for distinct entities observed in pairs
author: Svante Janson
source_title: On Edge Exchangeable Random Graphs
text: For iid unordered pairs E_i of distinct natural numbers with arbitrary fixed law μ, set V_n=∪_{i≤n}E_i. Does Var(|V_n|)→∞ imply (|V_n|−E|V_n|)/sqrt(Var(|V_n|))⇒N(0, 1), without eventual connectedness? This is the loopless countable-support model, without dust.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Linear rarity cost for next-event exposure estimation
author: Milind Nakul; Vidya Muthukumar; Ashwin Pananjady
source_title: Next-token functional estimation
text: For a stationary finite-state ergodic Markov trajectory X₁: n+1, let S_ζ=Pr{N_{X_{n+1}}(X₁: n)≤ζ}, an unconditional probability. Determine minimax MSE’s optimal ζ-dependence from X₁: n. Can the leading O((ζ+1)²T/n) bound become O((ζ+1)T/n), where T is a worst-start TV mixing-time bound? Retain Corollary 2’s finite-n bias terms, or state a valid growing-parameter regime. The ζ=0 case is settled.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Ranking preferences without knowing the transitivity strength
author: Tao Jin; Yue Wu; Quanquan Gu; Farzad Farnoud
source_title: Ranking with Multiple Oracles: From Weak to Strong Stochastic Transitivity
text: N items and M Bernoulli comparison oracles share one strict order σ. Define Δᵘᵢⱼ=|pᵘᵢⱼ−1/2|, Hᵢⱼ=M/Σᵤ(Δᵘᵢⱼ)² and Hᵢ=maxⱼ≠ᵢHᵢⱼ. Can one δ-correct exact-ranking algorithm, ignorant of the transitivity strength, simultaneously attain the weak-transitivity bound ~O(NΣᵢ₌₂ᴺH_{σ⁻¹(i),σ⁻¹(i−1)}) and, whenever all oracles satisfy strong stochastic transitivity, ~O(ΣᵢHᵢ[log log Hᵢ+log(N/δ)])? Strong transitivity requires pᵘᵢₖ≥max(pᵘᵢⱼ, pᵘⱼₖ) for i≻j≻k. Comparisons are independent; retain the source’s logarithmic overheads.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Sharp quantile-decision complexity under one-bit feedback
author: Ivan Lau; Jonathan Scarlett
source_title: Quantile Multi-Armed Bandits with 1-bit Feedback
text: With K i.i.d. arms, a pull returns only 1{Xₖ≤θ}; the reporting sensor has no reward memory. Let Qₖ(p)=inf{x: Fₖ(x)≥p}, Qₖ⁺(p)=sup{x: Fₖ(x)≤p}, q∈(0, 1), Qₖ(q)∈[0,λ], 0<ε≤λ, and Aε={k: Qₖ(q)≥maxₐQₐ(q)−ε}. Fix c≥1 and ε̃=λ/ceil((c+1)λ/ε). For k∉Aε set Δₖ=sup{z∈[0, min(q, 1−q)]: Qₖ(q+z)≤maxₐQₐ⁺(q−z)−ε̃}; for k∈Aε set Δₖ=max_{Aε⊆S⊆[K]}sup{z∈[0, minₐ∉SΔₐ]: Qₖ⁺(q−z)≥maxₐ∈S\{k}Qₐ(q+z)−cε̃}, with empty minimum/maximum +∞/−∞. Put dₖ=max(Δₖ, maxₐ∈AεΔₐ)>0. Can the log(1/dₖ) factor in O(Σₖdₖ⁻²[log(1/δ)+log(1/dₖ)+log(cλK/ε)]) become log log(1/dₖ), and what is the sharp joint gap/range dependence? Require ε-optimal output and the pull bound with probability≥1−δ; δ∈(0, 1/2).

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Oracle-efficient preference learning without realizability
author: Aadirupa Saha; Akshay Krishnamurthy
source_title: Efficient and Optimal Algorithms for Contextual Dueling Bandits under Realizability
text: In stochastic contextual dueling bandits, (xₜ, Pₜ) are i.i.d., Pₜ is an antisymmetric K×K matrix in [−1, 1], and comparing aₜ, bₜ reveals a ±1 variable with conditional mean Pₜ(aₜ, bₜ). Given a finite policy class Π⊆[K]^X and a cost-sensitive policy-optimization oracle over Π, can an oracle-efficient learner achieve expected ~O(√(KT log|Π|)) policy regret max_{π∈Π}Σₜ[f*(xₜ)(π(xₜ), aₜ)+f*(xₜ)(π(xₜ), bₜ)]/2, where f*(x)=E[P|x], without a realizable preference-function class? Oracle-efficient means polynomial time/oracle calls in T, K, log|Π| rather than enumeration of Π. The benchmark is policy regret, not the stronger unrealizable best-response regret.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Optimal strict-priority learning without known tradeoffs
author: Bo Xue; Ji Cheng; Fei Liu; Yimu Wang; Lijun Zhang; Qingfu Zhang
source_title: Lexicographic Lipschitz Bandits: New Algorithms and a Lower Bound
text: Actions form a metric space of diameter≤1; m reward means μⁱ are 1-Lipschitz with conditionally 1-sub-Gaussian noise. For lexicographic optimum x*, let unknown finite λ* be least λ satisfying μⁱ(x)−μⁱ(x*)≤λ maxⱼ<i(μʲ(x*)−μʲ(x)) for all x, i≥2. Set Λⁱ(λ)=Σⱼ₌₀ⁱ⁻¹λʲ and Rⁱ(T)=Σₜ(μⁱ(x*)−μⁱ(xₜ)). Define dᵢ by covering {x:Λⁱ(λ*)r/2<μⁱ(x*)−μⁱ(x)≤Λⁱ(λ*)r} with at most Zᵢr^(−dᵢ) radius-r/96 balls for some finite Zᵢ, all r>0. Without a known upper bound on λ*, can E[Rⁱ(T)]=~O(Λⁱ(λ*)T^((dᵢ+1)/(dᵢ+2))) hold for every i and finite m?

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Sharp horizon dependence for strict-priority linear control
author: Bo Xue; Dake Bu; Ji Cheng; Yuanyu Wan; Qingfu Zhang
source_title: Multi-objective Linear Reinforcement Learning with Lexicographic Rewards
text: Consider the source’s episodic d-dimensional linear MDP with m lexicographic rewards in [0, 1], horizon H, K episodes, known features ‖φ‖≤1 and unknown reward/transition coefficients bounded by √d. Under Assumption 1, can Rⁱ(K)=~O(Λⁱ(λ)[√(d²H³K)+d⁷H⁸]) hold simultaneously for all i, where Λⁱ(λ)=Σⱼ₌₀ⁱ⁻¹λʲ and Rⁱ sums the value gaps to π* over episodes? Assumption 1 requires π*(x, h) to remain lexicographically optimal for the algorithm’s continuation vectors Q̃ⁱ_h=rⁱ_h+P_hṼⁱ_{h+1}, with Q̃ⁱ_h(x, a)−Q̃ⁱ_h(x,π*)≤λ maxⱼ<i[Q̃ʲ_h(x,π*)−Q̃ʲ_h(x, a)]. The known leading horizon factor is H²√K.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Is the statistical conservatism of minimax-regret control unavoidable?
author: Tesshu Fujinami; Bruce D. Lee; Nikolai Matni; George J. Pappas
source_title: Domain Randomization is Sample Efficient for Linear Quadratic Control
text: For fully unknown stabilizable Xₜ₊₁=AXₜ+BUₜ+Wₜ, Wₜ∼N(0, I), Q⪰I, R=I, collect N independent length-T trajectories with Gaussian excitation Σᵤ≻0. Let θ̂ be least squares, F̂I empirical Fisher information, and G_N={θ:(θ−θ̂)ᵀNF̂I(θ−θ̂)≤16[dθ+log(2/δ)]}. Set K_RC∈argmin_K sup_{θ∈G_N}[C(K,θ)−C(K(θ),θ)], with C average quadratic cost. Under Theorem 3’s same confidence and burn-in convention, can its leading excess-cost term N⁻¹dθ‖HFI⁻¹‖ uniformly be replaced by N⁻¹tr(HFI⁻¹), or is the dimension/anisotropy gap unavoidable? Here FI is per-trajectory Fisher information and H=∇²_θC(K(θ),θ*)|θ=θ*. Retain Theorem 3’s robust-stabilizability and burn-in conditions.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Must survival-optimal learning know its deadline?
author: Charles Riou; Junya Honda; Masashi Sugiyama
source_title: The Survival Bandit Problem
text: For laws supported on {−1, 0, 1}, is every anytime policy non-Pareto-optimal? Anytime means one history-to-action rule for all horizons.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Does survival-optimal exploration extend beyond integer rewards?
author: Charles Riou; Junya Honda; Masashi Sugiyama
source_title: The Survival Bandit Problem
text: For laws on [−1, 1], is Algorithm 2 EXPLOIT-UCB-DOUBLE, with Definition 28’s generalized EXPLOIT rule and n=⌈log T⌉, Pareto-optimal? Its budget-reset rule is fixed.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: A four-thirds guarantee for compact preference consensus
author: Abu Mohammad Hammad Ali; Boting Yang; Sandra Zilles
source_title: Approximation Algorithms for Preference Aggregation Using CP-Nets
text: For binary attributes V₁,…, Vₙ and explicit complete conditional-preference tables N₁,…, Nₜ for Vₙ, define f_T(N)=ΣₛΔ_swap(N, Nₛ), counting disagreements on outcome pairs differing only at Vₙ. Algorithm 1 considers each input parent set P, computes an optimal table restricted to P, and returns the best candidate. Is f_T(Algorithm 1(T))≤(4/3)min_N f_T(N) for every input tuple T, or is there a counterexample? The optimum may use any parent set; the algorithm’s output remains polynomial-size. The 4/3 theorem for maximum-indegree-one inputs is already known.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Optimal decisions with asymmetric nonsmooth identified bounds
author: José Luis Montiel Olea; Chen Qiu; Jörg Stoye
source_title: Local Asymptotics for Treatment Choice with Partial Identification
text: Observe Z∼N(h, I₀⁻¹) and choose measurable d(Z)∈[0, 1]. Let I∞(h)=[C₋+ℓ′(μ₀; G₀h), C₊+u′(μ₀; G₀h)] and H={h: I∞(h)≠∅}, where C₋<0<C₊ and C₋/C₊=ℓ(μ₀)/u(μ₀). The identified interval bounds ℓ, u are attained and Hadamard directionally differentiable at the global least-favorable interior μ₀; G₀ differentiates the regular reduced form. Determine inf_d sup_{h∈H, v∈I∞(h)}v[1{v≥0}−E_hd(Z)] and an attaining rule under Assumptions 1–4 and convexity, without centrosymmetry or full differentiability.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Global first-order guarantees for state-rectangular ambiguity
author: Toshinori Kitamura; Arnob Ghosh; Alex Ayoub; Thang D. Chu; Csaba Szepesvári
source_title: Revisiting Subgradient Dominance in Robust MDPs: Counterexamples, Hardness, and Sufficient Conditions
text: Let Π=∏ₛΔ(A) be stationary randomized policies in a finite discounted MDP, with fixed costs c∈[0, 1], 0≤γ<1, full-support initial law μ, and compact s-rectangular transition uncertainty P=∏ₛPₛ, Pₛ⊆Δ(S)^A. Put J(π)=max_{P∈P}E_{μ,π, P}Σₜγᵗc(sₜ, aₜ). Does every such instance satisfy subgradient dominance: ∃D<∞, ∀π∈Π, J(π)−min_{π′∈Π}J(π′)≤D min_{g∈∂J(π)}max_{π′∈Π}⟨π−π′, g⟩? Here ∂ is the source’s Fréchet subdifferential. Preserve the minimum over subgradients. The known counterexamples use nonrectangular uncertainty and do not decide this conjecture.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Exact robust thresholds with independent action uncertainty
author: Marnix Suilen; Guillermo A. Pérez
source_title: On the Complexity of Robust Markov Decision Processes and Bisimulation Metrics
text: For (s, a)-rectangular U=∏ₛ,ₐUₛₐ, determine the exact bit complexity of this threshold problem when γ is part of the input. It lies in NP and is parity-game-hard; a fixed-discount polynomial algorithm is already known.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Certified robust value iteration without enumerating transition supports
author: Tobias Meggendorfer; Maximilian Weininger; Patrick Wienhöft
source_title: Solving Robust Markov Decision Processes: Generic, Reliable, Efficient
text: For finite (s, a)-rectangular robust MDPs with nonnegative rational rewards and compact rational H-polytope uncertainty sets whose transition supports may vary, is there an implicit anytime algorithm for long-run-average reward or minimizing total reward under the source’s conventional total-reward semantics? It must maintain valid lower/upper value bounds and terminate for any prescribed positive error on finite-valued states, without enumerating the exponentially many extreme transitions/supports or constructing the induced stochastic game. The unresolved ingredient is implicit maximal-end-component search after fixing the agent’s policy; no polynomial bound on the total number of value iterations is asserted.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Comparing risk aversion on a finite outcome menu
author: Jean Baccelli; Georg Schollmeyer; Christoph Jansen
source_title: Risk aversion over finite domains
text: Fix numerical outcomes X={x₁>⋯>xₙ}, n≥3, and continuous strictly increasing weights w₁, w₂:[0, 1]→[0, 1] with endpoints 0, 1. For p∈Δₙ define V_w(p)=xₙ+Σᵢ₌₁ⁿ⁻¹w(Σⱼ≤ᵢpⱼ)(xᵢ−xᵢ₊₁). Characterize necessary and sufficient conditions on (w₁, w₂, X) for weak comparative risk aversion: for every p and every sure xⱼ, V_{w₁}(p)≥xⱼ implies V_{w₂}(p)≥xⱼ. This is finite-domain dual expected utility; pointwise w₁≤w₂ is sufficient but not necessary. The strong-risk-aversion characterization and expected-utility characterization are already known.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Nonmonotone optimal no-regret dynamics: must last iterates fail?
author: Vidya Muthukumar; Soham Phade; Anant Sahai
source_title: On the Impossibility of Convergence of Mixed Strategies with No Regret Learning
text: For a 2×2 game with a unique completely mixed Nash equilibrium, both players observe only realized opponent actions and set P_t=f_t(empirical opponent frequency), with independent conditional action draws. Assume uniform external regret O(√T) against every opponent-action sequence, for each player. Must (P_t, Q_t) fail to converge almost surely without monotonicity of f_t? This is Conjecture 3.12; the monotone case is proved.

author: Côme Fiegel; Pierre Ménard; Tadashi Kozuno; Michal Valko; Vianney Perchet

author: Côme Fiegel; Pierre Ménard; Tadashi Kozuno; Michal Valko; Vianney Perchet

title: One learner with polylogarithmic Nash and square-root external regret
author: Arnab Maiti; Kevin Jamieson; Lillian J. Ratliff
source_title: On the Limitations and Possibilities of Nash Regret Minimization in Zero-Sum Matrix Games under Noisy Feedback

author: Shinji Ito; Haipeng Luo; Arnab Maiti; Taira Tsuchiya; Yue Wu
source_title: Adversarial Learning in Games with Bandit Feedback: Logarithmic Pure-Strategy Maximin Regret
text: Can one normal-form learner attain min{(log T/Δ_min^c)Σ_{i≠i*}1/Δ_i^r, Σ_{Δ_ij>0}(1/Δ_ij+Δ_ij log T)} at strict pure equilibria and keep O(√(|X|T)) worst-case regret? Here Δ_i^r=u(i*, j*)−u(i, j*), Δ_min^c=min_{j≠j*}[u(i*, j)−u(i*, j*)], Δ_ij=v*−u(i, j).

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Instance-optimal informed learning for bilinear games
author: Shinji Ito; Haipeng Luo; Arnab Maiti; Taira Tsuchiya; Yue Wu
source_title: Adversarial Learning in Games with Bandit Feedback: Logarithmic Pure-Strategy Maximin Regret

title: Remove degree-amplified misspecification in strategic PAC learning

source_title: Learnability Gaps of Strategic Classification
text: Agents (x, y)∼D respond through unknown G*, with out-degree≤k. Agents stay if already positive; otherwise they choose uniformly among reachable positives. Training reveals x before classification and (v, y) afterward, not its neighborhood. For VC-class H and finite candidate graphs 𝒢, define Δ_H=inf_h L_str(G*, D)(h), Δ_G=min_G Pr[N_G(x)≠N_G*(x)]. Can the guarantee Δ_H+6kΔ_G+ε become Δ_H+O(Δ_G)+ε with polynomial(k, d, log|𝒢|, 1/ε, log(1/δ)) samples, or is degree amplification necessary?

title: Instance-optimal randomized strategic mistake complexity
author: Saba Ahmadi; Kunhe Yang; Hanrui Zhang
source_title: Strategic Littlestone Dimension: Improved Bounds on Online Strategic Classification
text: For known directed G and binary H, characterize the minimum worst-case expected realizable mistakes of randomized improper learners, jointly in (H, G). The labeled original agent is fixed before the current classifier draw; the realized classifier is public, agents select any positive reachable node with adversarial ties (staying only if all are negative), and only manipulated features and labels are observed. Seek the randomized analogue of Strategic Littlestone Dimension, beyond worst-case Ldim/degree bounds.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Statistical and computational efficiency in contractual RL
author: Jibang Wu; Siyu Chen; Mengdi Wang; Huazheng Wang; Haifeng Xu
source_title: Contractual Reinforcement Learning: Pulling Arms with Invisible Hands
text: In the finite-H principal-agent MDP, costs are known, transitions/rewards unknown, contracts x_h(s, s′)∈[0,η], and each farsighted agent best responds; states/actions/rewards are observed. Retain Appendix D’s volume/cost-separation assumptions and P_h≥κ. Under weak inducibility (for each deterministic π, some binary events e_h satisfy Σ_h(ρ_h^π−ρ_h^{π′})·e_h≥λ_w for all π′≠π), can Algorithm 6’s Õ(√T) regret be retained with a polynomial-time contract solver, without Algorithm 7’s stronger stagewise inducibility? source_title: Learning in Structured Stackelberg Games
text: In a known contextual Stackelberg game with finite actions/types, context precedes commitment and the follower’s type is revealed afterward; ties use a known fixed order. Given H⊂[K]^Z without realizability, characterize sublinear learnability and sharp minimax regret against the best induced policy π_h in hindsight, evaluated against actual follower best responses. Account for the game structure, not merely |H| or multiclass prediction complexity.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Efficient certification of strong quadratic information substitutes
author: Yiling Chen
source_title: Operational Characterizations of Informational Substitutes and Complements

text: For rational finite P(E, A, B) and G(p)=||p||², is strong substitutability decidable in polynomial bit complexity? With V(X)=E G(P(E|X)), require V(B, A′)−V(A′)≥V(A, B)−V(A) for every garbling A′ of A retaining common deterministic information A∧B, and symmetrically. Otherwise establish the complexity obstruction. Testing only whole signals is insufficient.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Decide strict probability raising for an observed history
author: Christel Baier; Jakob Piribauer; Robin Ziemek
source_title: Foundations of probability-raising causality in Markov decision processes

text: Given a finite rational MDP M, a nonempty ω-regular effect E represented by a deterministic Rabin automaton, and a nonempty co-safety cause candidate C represented by a DFA accepting its minimal good prefixes, is it decidable whether, for every such prefix σ and every history-dependent randomized scheduler π with Pr_M^π(σ)>0, Pr_M^π(E|σ)>Pr_M^π(E)? Both automata read full MDP states, not hidden observation labels. This is the co-safety SPR check, not the solved state-set or global co-safety GPR check.

Fixed directed G is accessed by edge queries; N[x] is the closed out-neighborhood. α1 is the largest C-shattered independent set; α2 the largest independent set whose vertices have oppositely labeled out-neighbors, maximized over c∈C. Retain the source’s measurability assumptions.

Each fixed time-state-action ambiguity set is closed convex over rewards [0, 1] and next states; nature selects adaptively and secretly. author: Frits Verhagen; Marco Tomamichel; Erkka Haapasalo
source_title: Matrix Majorization in Large Samples with Varying Support Restrictions
text: For normalized U, is power universality equivalent to Φ(U)≠1 for every nondegenerate monotone homomorphism into ordinary or max-times nonnegative reals, with either order? Nondegenerate means nonconstant on comparable pairs.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Sharp prefix-query cost with a known model class
author: Noah Golowich; Ankur Moitra; Dhruv Rohatgi
source_title: The Power of Test-Time Training for Approximate Sampling
text: For unknown μ* in a known finite F⊂Δ({0, 1}^n), an oracle μ̂ approximates every prefix probability within fixed factor R>1 and is exact on leaves. Member-law prefix evaluation is free. What is the minimax number of adaptive μ̂ queries, jointly in n,|F|, to attain fixed TV error δ<1/10, with unrestricted intermediate computation?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Deterministic counting with twice-used evidence atoms
author: Chengyu Lin; Jingcheng Liu; Pinyan Lu
source_title: A Simple FPTAS for Counting Edge Covers
text: Does counting satisfying assignments of an arbitrary read-twice CNF admit an FPTAS? Each Boolean variable occurs in at most two clauses, with arbitrary signs and clause widths. Given explicit formula Φ and ε∈(0, 1), output Ẑ with (1−ε)Z≤Ẑ≤(1+ε)Z in deterministic time polynomial in |Φ| and 1/ε, where Z is the number of satisfying assignments (so Z=0 requires output 0).

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Derandomizing the probability of global connectivity
author: Konrad Anand; Graham Freifeld; Heng Guo; Chunyang Wang; Jiaheng Wang
source_title: Sink-Free Orientations: A Local Sampler with Applications
text: Given an undirected graph G=(V, E) and rational independent edge-survival probabilities p_e∈[0, 1], does an FPTAS compute R=Pr[(V,{e: B_e=1}) is connected], where B_e are independent Bernoulli(p_e)? Require (1−ε)R≤R̂≤(1+ε)R and deterministic time polynomial in the full input bit length and 1/ε. The target is connectivity probability R, not its complement.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Local Ising sampling throughout uniqueness
author: Hongyang Liu; Chunyang Wang; Yitong Yin
source_title: Local Gibbs sampling beyond local uniformity
text: For fixed Δ≥3 and β∈((Δ−2)/Δ,Δ/(Δ−2)), can exact Ising marginals on Λ be sampled in expected C(Δ,β)|Λ| time for every maximum-degree-Δ graph and arbitrary nonnegative vertex weights with nonzero partition function? Here β weights agreeing edge spins.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Local coloring sampling at the CFTP threshold
author: Hongyang Liu; Chunyang Wang; Yitong Yin
source_title: Local Gibbs sampling beyond local uniformity
text: For each fixed η>0 and large Δ, can uniform proper q-coloring marginals be sampled locally in expected poly(q,Δ, 1/η)|Λ| time when q≥(8/3+η)Δ?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Sharp critical Glauber inference time
author: Xiaoyu Chen; Zongchen Chen; Yitong Yin; Xinyuan Zhang
source_title: Rapid Mixing at the Uniqueness Threshold
text: What are the sharp worst-case TV(1/4) mixing times of single-site heat-bath dynamics, jointly in n,Δ, over all starts and graphs in these models?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Deterministic normalizers at criticality
author: Xiaoyu Chen; Zongchen Chen; Yitong Yin; Xinyuan Zhang
source_title: Rapid Mixing at the Uniqueness Threshold
text: For fixed Δ, do their partition functions admit deterministic (1±ε) approximation in poly(n, 1/ε) time on every graph in the setup?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Sparse Bayesian sampling with near-minimal observations
author: Syamantak Kumar; Purnamrita Sarkar; Kevin Tian; Yusong Zhu
source_title: High-Magnetization Sampling at Low Temperatures: Ising Models and Bayesian Sparse Linear Regression
text: For iid X_ij∼N(0, 1/n), independent θ*_j∼(1−k/d)δ_0+(k/d)N(0, 1), and y=Xθ*+ξ, with ξ∼N(0,σ²I) independent of X,θ*, can π(·|X, y) be sampled in polynomial arithmetic time at n=Ω(k log d), for every known σ>0? For fixed δ∈(0, 1/2), require TV≤δ with probability≥1−δ over the model. Retain the source’s numerical-parameter runtime dependence.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Comparing Ising posteriors without bounded-away-from-zero marginals
author: Weiming Feng; Hongyang Liu; Minji Yang
source_title: Approximating the total variation distance between spin systems
text: Remove the constant positive conditional-marginal lower bound from Corollary 7’s relative-TV FPRAS. Each explicit Ising input must satisfy one of: spectral width≤1−η (fixed η>0); ferromagnetic couplings with nonnegative fields; or uniform antiferromagnetic coupling β with exp(2β)≥(Δ−2)/Δ. Require polynomial-time (1±ε) estimation of full-law TV with success≥2/3, despite arbitrarily small positive conditional marginals. Use the source’s exact local-factor evaluation convention.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Deterministic normalization of assignment hypotheses
author: Sergei Kudria; Jason Luo; Mahbod Majid
source_title: Subexponential Approximation of the Permanent in Deterministic Polynomial Time
text: Does the permanent of every nonnegative rational n×n matrix admit a deterministic FPTAS? Given A and ε∈(0, 1), output P̂ satisfying (1−ε)per(A)≤P̂≤(1+ε)per(A) in time polynomial in the full input bit length and 1/ε, where per(A)=Σ_{π∈S_n}∏_i A_{i,π(i)}. No density, expansion, or bounded-entry-ratio promise is available.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Parallel sampling of uniformly plausible matchings
author: Xiaoyu Chen; Hongyang Liu; Yitong Yin; Xinyuan Zhang
source_title: Efficient Parallel Ising Samplers via Localization Schemes
text: Does uniform perfect-matching sampling on every bipartite graph having a perfect matching admit this RNC guarantee?

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Parallel inference with unrestricted ferromagnetic fields
author: Xiaoyu Chen; Hongyang Liu; Yitong Yin; Xinyuan Zhang
source_title: Efficient Parallel Ising Samplers via Localization Schemes
text: For ferromagnetic Ising weights β_e>1, 0<λ_v≤1, can sampling achieve the same RNC guarantee without a constant field gap, in the source’s arithmetic PRAM model? The law weights agreeing edges by β_e and positive vertices by λ_v; λ_v=1 is allowed.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Deterministic likelihoods for arbitrary disjunctive evidence
author: Rocco A. Servedio; Li-Yang Tan
source_title: Pseudorandomness for read-k DNF formulas
text: Does arbitrary DNF model counting admit a deterministic FPTAS? Given an explicit DNF Φ on n Boolean variables and ε∈(0, 1), approximate Z=#{x∈{0, 1}^n:Φ(x)=1} within multiplicative factor 1±ε in time polynomial in |Φ| and 1/ε. There is no bound on variable occurrences or term width. Zero counts must be returned exactly.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Optimal parallel rounds for coherent conditional queries
author: Nima Anari; Ruiquan Gao; Aviad Rubinstein
source_title: Parallel Sampling via Counting
text: For arbitrary μ on {0, 1}^n, an oracle returns exact pinning probabilities Pr_μ[X_S=x_S] (equivalently, conditionals under feasible pinnings). With polynomially many queries per round and polynomial expected total queries, what is the minimum worst-case expected round count for exact sampling? The current general bounds are Õ(n^(1/3)) below and Õ(√n) above.

subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms
title: Subquadratic normalizers throughout the uniqueness phase
author: Xiaoyu Chen; Zongchen Chen; Kuikui Liu; Xinyuan Zhang
source_title: Subquadratic Counting via Perfect Marginal Sampling
text: For every fixed Δ≥3 and 0<λ<λ_c(Δ)=(Δ−1)^{Δ−1}/(Δ−2)^Δ, is there an FPRAS for Z_G(λ)=Σ_{I independent in G}λ^{|I|} on all n-vertex graphs of maximum degree Δ that has expected o(n²) runtime for every fixed ε∈(0, 1), while retaining polynomial dependence on 1/ε? Require relative error 1±ε with probability≥3/4. Graph access is the paper’s adjacency-list oracle/unit-cost arithmetic model. The endpoint λ=λ_c is not silently included.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Can minimally adaptive BH be uniformly improved?
author: Ziyu Xu; Aldo Solari; Lasse Fischer; Rianne de Heide; Aaditya Ramdas; Jelle Goeman
source_title: Bringing Closure to False Discovery Rate Control: A General Principle for Multiple Testing
text: Under PRDS on the true nulls, let r_B=max({r: p_(r)≤αr/m}∪{0}) and r_M=max({r: p_(r)≤αr/(m−1)}∪{0}), m≥2. MABH rejects nothing if r_B=0, otherwise the r_M smallest p-values. Does any α-FDR-controlling p-value procedure always contain these rejections and strictly enlarge them with positive probability for an allowed law? True-null p-values are superuniform.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Exact misspecification slack for robust Hellinger testing
author: Eeshan Modak; Sivaraman Balakrishnan; Ananda Theertha Suresh
source_title: On Robust Hypothesis Testing with respect to the Hellinger Distance
text: For known distinct laws p₀, p₁ and H²(p, q)=1−∫√(pq), determine the infimum γ>1 such that every pair admits a test distinguishing γH²(p, p₀)≤H²(p, p₁) from H²(p, p₀)≥γH²(p, p₁), using finitely many iid p-samples uniformly over the promised p, with both errors≤δ. Sample size may depend on the pair,γ,δ; randomized tests and continuous domains are allowed. Current gap: 2+√2≤γ*≤3+2√2.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: A sharp repeated-coverage bound without reversibility
author: Siu On Chan; Qinghua Ding; Sing Hei Li
source_title: Learning and Testing Irreducible Markov Chains via the k-Cover Time
text: For every finite irreducible Markov chain and k≥1, let t_cov^(k) be the worst-start expected time to visit every state k times, t_cov=t_cov^(1), and π*=min_iπ_i. Does t_cov^(k)≤C(t_cov+k/π*) hold with a universal C? Reversible chains are settled; the general bound loses log n. Periodic chains are included.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Fast learning at every generation under recycled labels
author: Kareem Amin; Alex Bie; Weiwei Kong; Umar Syed; Sergei Vassilvitskii
source_title: Learning from Synthetic Data: Limitations of ERM
text: A binary VC-d class contains f*. Initially n iid D examples receive true labels. Each later round adds n fresh D covariates, labeled independently by f* with known probability 1−α>0 and by the previously released classifier otherwise; origins are hidden. Using all batches and past classifiers, can one learner guarantee expected true error O_{d,α}(1/(nt)) at every t≥1, rather than only a chosen final round? Computation is unrestricted.

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: Harmonic-mean subuniformity under positive Gaussian dependence
author: Yuyu Chen; Ruodu Wang; Yuming Wang; Wenhao Zhu
source_title: Subuniformity of harmonic mean p-values
text: For n≥2 and ρ∈(0, 1), let Z∼N_n(0,Σ), Σ_ii=1, Σ_ij=ρ for i≠j, and U_i=Φ(Z_i). Must Pr{(n⁻¹Σ_iU_i⁻¹)⁻¹≤u}≥u for every u∈(0, 1)? This is the equal-weight equicorrelated case; ρ denotes correlation, not the source’s common-factor loading. Preserve finite-u ordering.

subject: Bayesian Inference
title: Can one convex PAC-Bayes bound attain the pointwise ideal in expectation?
author: Andrew Y. K. Foong; Wessel P. Bruinsma; David R. Burt; Richard E. Turner
source_title: How Tight Can PAC-Bayes be in the Small Data Regime?
text: Let S∼D^N, ℓ∈[0, 1], fixed prior P and posterior Q(S); put q=E_Q R_S, K=KL(Q||P). For proper convex l.s.c. Δ:[0, 1]²→R∪{∞}, set I_Δ=sup_{r∈[0, 1]} E_{B∼Bin(N, r)}e^{NΔ(B/N, r)} and b_Δ=sup{p∈[0, 1]: NΔ(q, p)≤K+log(I_Δ/δ)}, sup∅=1. For each setup and N≥1, δ∈(0, 1), does some Δ fixed before S attain E b_Δ=E sup{p∈[0, 1]: Nkl(q, p)≤K+log(1/δ)}? If not, how close can it get?

subject: Mathematical Statistics
title: A beta-function inequality for earlier certified plurality stopping
author: Shubham Anand Jain; Rohan Shah; Sanit Gupta; Denil Mehta; Inderjeet Nair; Jian Vora; Sushil Khyalia; Sourav Das; Vinay J. Ribeiro; Shivaram Kalyanakrishnan
source_title: PAC Mode Estimation using PPR Martingale Confidence Sequences
text: For integers K≥3, a>b≥1, f≥0, put t=a+b+f, r=[a!(t−a)!/(b!(t−b)!)]^(1/(a−b)), θ=r/(1+r). Must θ^a(1−θ)^(t−a)/B(a+1, t−a+1)≥(K−1)/(K2^(a+b)B(a+1, b+1))? Here B is the beta function. This is the stated sufficient inequality for pathwise PPR-1v1 stopping dominance over PPR-1vr.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Constant-factor agnostic halfspace learning on the uniform hypercube
author: Arsen Vasilyan
source_title: Testing Assumptions of Learning Algorithms
text: Given iid (X, f(X)), with X uniform on {−1, 1}^d and arbitrary unknown Boolean f, define opt=inf_(w, b)Pr[sign(w·X−b)≠f(X)]. Can a randomized poly(d, 1/ε)-time learner output an evaluable, possibly improper h with error≤C·opt+ε, probability≥2/3, for universal C? Only sample access is allowed; the marginal is assumed, not tested.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The margin cost of resistance to targeted clean-label poisoning
author: Avrim Blum; Steve Hanneke; Jian Qian; Han Shao
source_title: Robust learning under clean-label attack
text: In the unit disk of R², clean iid data are labeled by h*(x)=1{w·x+b≥0} with signed margin≥γ||w||₂/2, γ∈(0, 2]. An attacker sees h*, clean sample S and test x, then adds any finite correctly labeled multiset, without a margin restriction. Determine the sharp γ-dependence of the least |S| such that some randomized, possibly improper learner has attackable rate≤ε with probability≥1−δ. Attackable rate is sup_Adv E_{(X, Y), A}[1{A(S∪Adv(h*, S, X), X)≠Y}]. Fix ε,δ∈(0, 1/10). The known 2D upper bound is O(log(1/γ)loglog(1/γ)) as γ→0.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Sharp reward-free complexity for static CVaR
author: Xinyi Ni; Guanlin Liu; Lifeng Lai
source_title: Risk-Sensitive Reward-Free Reinforcement Learning with CVaR
text: What is the minimax episode complexity for simultaneous (ε,δ)-PAC validity? Close Õ(S²AH⁴/(ε²τ²)) versus Ω(S²AH²/(ε²τ)). Retain A≥2, S≥C log₂A+2, H≥C log₂S+1 and ε≤min{1/(4τ), H/(48τ)} at fixed δ<1/2.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Efficient return-distribution matching under an unknown reward
author: Filippo Lazzati; Alberto Maria Metelli
source_title: Imitation Learning as Return Distribution Matching
text: Can min_π max_r W₁(η_r^π,η̂_{r^θ}) be approximated within ε in poly(S, A, H, N, 1/ε, input-bits) time, outputting a succinct executable history policy?

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Sharp discounted recursive entropic policy-learning complexity
author: Oliver Mortensen; Mohammad Sadegh Talebi
source_title: Recursive Entropic Risk Optimization in Discounted MDPs: Sample Complexity Bounds with a Generative Model
text: What is the minimax sample complexity to output stationary π with Pr{||V*−V^π||∞≤ε}≥1−δ? Close Theorems 2/4’s joint β,γ gap. The lower bound uses δ<1/4 and ε<γ(1−e^{−|β|/(1−γ)})/(50|β|); its exponential term is positive when |β|>(1−γ)log3.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Almost-sure convergence of average-risk UBSR Q-learning
author: Weikai Wang; Erick Delage
source_title: Planning and Learning in Average Risk-aware MDPs
text: Does Q_{n+1}(x, a)=Q_n(x, a)+γ_nℓ(c(x, a)+min_bQ_n(S′, b)−f(Q_n)−Q_n(x, a)) converge almost surely to an optimal average-nested-risk Bellman solution? Shortfall risk ρ solves Eℓ(Z−ρ(Z))=0.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Exact threshold complexity for Euclidean-robust Markov chains
author: Ali Asadi; Krishnendu Chatterjee; Alipasha Montaseri; Ali Shafiee
source_title: On the Complexity of Discounted Robust MDPs with L_p Uncertainty Sets
text: Determine the exact Turing complexity of v_{s₀}≥q for rational q: square-root-sum hard and in ∃R, but no tight classification.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Joint statistical and computational efficiency for robust mixture dynamics
author: Zhishuai Liu; Pan Xu
source_title: Linear Mixture Distributionally Robust Markov Decision Processes
text: Can polynomial-time learning attain (ε,ζ)-PAC robust optimality with K=Õ(d²H⁴(C^{π*})²/ε²), matching the planning-oracle guarantee under these same coverage assumptions?

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Sharp query complexity for convex optimization with flat preferences
author: Aadirupa Saha; Tomer Koren; Yishay Mansour
source_title: Dueling Convex Optimization with General Preferences
text: What is the sharp comparison complexity for outputting an ε-optimal point with probability 1−δ? Improve the merely-convex ε^{-4p}-type dependence or prove matching lower bounds; good-iterate visitation alone is insufficient.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Optimal randomized metric distortion from ordinal preferences
author: Ziyi Cai; Moses Charikar; Jabari Hastings; Prasanna Ramakrishnan; Kangning Wang; Qilin Ye
source_title: Stable Voting Rules on the Edge of Optimal Metric Distortion
text: Determine inf_F sup_{finite profiles, consistent metrics} E_F SC(c)/min_aSC(a), using the usual zero-optimum convention. Close 2.11264≤D*≤2.13713.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: High-dimensional minimax optimality of Firth utility estimation
author: Yicheng Li; Huifu Xu
source_title: Error Bounds for Statistical Estimators in BTL Model with Parametric Multivariate Utility Functions
text: Does unrestricted θ̂_F=argmin[ℓ_N(θ)−logdet∇²ℓ_N(θ)/(2N)] attain minimax Euclidean risk σ²tr(W⁻¹)/N once N≳d^{3/2}, up to B,μ_Q and logarithmic factors? Hereℓ_N is average negative log-likelihood.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Polynomial-time corruption-robust threshold search
author: Renato Paes Leme; Chara Podimata; Jon Schneider
source_title: Density-Based Algorithms for Corruption-Robust Contextual Search and Convex Optimization
text: For ε∈(0, 1), can learning polynomial in d, T and numerical input/accuracy encoding attain Σ1{|y_t−v_t|≥ε}=O(C₀+d log(1/ε)), without knowing C₀?

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Horizon-free absolute loss with corrupted comparisons
author: Renato Paes Leme; Chara Podimata; Jon Schneider
source_title: Density-Based Algorithms for Corruption-Robust Contextual Search and Convex Optimization
text: Can corruption-agnostic learning attain Σ|y_t−v_t|=O(C₁+d), removing log T from the current absolute-loss bound?

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Learning when response memory spans the whole horizon
author: Khashayar Khosravi; Renato Paes Leme; Chara Podimata; Apostolis Tsorvantzis
source_title: Preferences Evolve And So Should Your Bandits: Bandits with Evolving States for Online Platforms
text: For known λ=c/T, fixed c>0, K, can worst-case expected regret against the parameter-informed best length-T sequence be o(T), without discounting benchmark reward?

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Sharp statistical price of a narrow safe starting margin
author: Aldo Pacchiano; Mohammad Ghavamzadeh; Peter Bartlett
source_title: Contextual Bandits with Stage-wise Constraints
text: What is the sharp Δ=τ−c₀ dependence of minimax regret? The upper rate is Õ((1+(1−r₀)/Δ)d√T); the lower is B=max{d√T/(8e²),(1−r₀)/(21Δ²)}, for T≥max{d−1, 168eB/(1−r₀)}. Retain the T cap.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Certified feasibility search with uninflated coupled perturbations
author: Aditya Gangrade; Aldo Pacchiano; Clayton Scott; Venkatesh Saligrama
source_title: Feasible Action Search for Bandit Linear Programs via Thompson Sampling
text: Can FAST use coupled H_t=1_m ζ_tᵀ, ζ_t∼Unif(cS^{d−1}), with fixed positive dimension-independent c,π in its unchanged stopping boundary, and remain (ε,δ)-reliable with finite stopping for |M*|>0? Otherwise, exhibit failure.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Remove safety slack from the ordinary learning term
author: Gianmarco Genalti; Francesco Emanuele Stradi; Matteo Castiglioni; Alberto Marchesi; Nicola Gatti
source_title: Data-Dependent Regret Bounds for Constrained MABs
text: Put L*=Σ_tℓ_tᵀx*. Can the bound Õ((K/ρ)√Σ[ℓ_tᵀ(x⋄−x*)]²+(1/ρ)√(KL*)) lose 1/ρ only in its second term, preserving joint per-round feasibility? Allow the source’s L*-informed tuning and ρ≥12K/T.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Does locally cheap universal Nash learning collapse PPAD?
author: Oliver Biggar; Christos Papadimitriou; Georgios Piliouras
source_title: On the Complexity of Learning Nash Equilibria
text: Suppose a single polynomial-time algorithm evaluates continuous updates f_G(x) from rational finite bimatrix input G and mixed profile x, and lim_t f_G^t(x) exists in NE(G) for every G, x. Must P=PPAD? Use Definition 2.1(A); no convergence-time bound, uncoupledness, or computable Lyapunov function is assumed.

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Efficiently certify a predicted long-run response region
author: Oliver Biggar; Christos Papadimitriou
source_title: Sink equilibria and the attractors of learning in games
text: Given a rational finite normal-form game and a sink preference-graph component H, can one decide in polynomial time whether content(H) is a replicator attractor?

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Find a stable periodic strategic response
author: Oliver Biggar; Christos Papadimitriou
source_title: Computing stable limit cycles of learning in games
text: Can a rational finite normal-form game be tested in polynomial time for a nonconstant stable periodic play sequence, and one found, or is search intractable?

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Must two-player stable play alternate the changing player?
author: Oliver Biggar; Christos Papadimitriou
source_title: Computing stable limit cycles of learning in games
text: In every two-player game, must every stable periodic sequence alternate which player changes strategy, including the last-to-first switch?

subject: Algorithmic Game Theory, Learning & Network Games
title: Compute mixed safeguards against private attacker types
author: Vincent Conitzer
source_title: Computing Nash Equilibria in Bayesian Security Games
location: Research Goal; Problem Description; earlier author note §1.
text: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm for a Bayes-Nash equilibrium from the explicit rational input, using defender coverage marginals (with a compact implementing mixture) and type-conditional attacker mixtures?

subject: Games of Incomplete Information & Bayesian Games
title: Finite versus asymptotic value of longer dialogues
author: Renato Paes Leme; Jon Schneider; Heyang Shang; Shuran Zheng
source_title: Bayesian Conversations
text: With binary types and arbitrary finite actions, characterize finite attainment of sup_T W_T, stopping-round bounds, and otherwise the convergence rate. Is the finite/asymptotic case efficiently decidable?

subject: Games of Incomplete Information & Bayesian Games
title: Exact joint optimization of framing and Bayesian signals
author: Paul Dütting; Safwan Hossain; Tao Lin; Renato Paes Leme; Sai Srivatsa Ravindranath; Haifeng Xu; Song Zuo
source_title: Information Design With Large Language Models
text: For rational μ₀, u, v, determine the exact complexity of max_(μ∈ΔΩ,π)Σμ₀(ω)π(a|ω)u(a,ω), subject to stochasticπ and Σμ(ω)π(a|ω)[v(a,ω)−v(a′,ω)]≥0 for all a, a′. General state-dependent u is essential; all receiver actions are strictly inducible.

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Linear dimension cost for corrupted binary-response pricing
author: Matteo Castiglioni; Francesco Emanuele Stradi
source_title: Decoupling Corruption and Horizon in Robust Contextual Pricing
text: With C known, can O(C+d log T) regret replace O(Cd+d²log T), or is a larger dimension penalty necessary?

subject: Optimization & Operations Research
title: Adapt to unknown corruption without multiplying the horizon cost
author: Matteo Castiglioni; Francesco Emanuele Stradi
source_title: Decoupling Corruption and Horizon in Robust Contextual Pricing
text: Without knowing C, can one learner guarantee poly(d)(C+log T) regret for every C≤T, retaining the trivial T cap?

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Sharp memory and stability cost of autoregressive decisions
author: Francesco Bacchiocchi; Gianmarco Genalti; Davide Maran; Marco Mussi; Marcello Restelli; Nicola Gatti; Alberto Maria Metelli
source_title: Autoregressive Bandits
text: For n actions, X_t=γ₀(a_t)+Σ_{j=1}^kγ_j(a_t)X_{t−j}+ξ_t, with unknown nonnegative coefficients, Γ=max_aΣ_{j≥1}γ_j(a)<1, bounded intercepts, fixed initial history and conditionally centered sub-Gaussian noise, determine optimal k and 1−Γ dependence of expected policy regret. Can the current Õ((k+1)^(3/2)√(nT)/(1−Γ)²) improve? Deterministic policies know k and an intercept bound, not Γ; comparison uses the optimal policy’s own trajectory.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The exact price of tracking concavely improving options
author: Cristiano Migali; Marco Mussi; Gianmarco Genalti; Alberto Maria Metelli
source_title: Tightening Regret Lower and Upper Bounds in Restless Rising Bandits
text: For fixed K≥2 and σ≥1, what is the minimax order over deterministic history-based policies in T of expected dynamic regret Σ_{t≤T}(max_i μ_i(t)−μ_{I_t}(t)) when independent σ-sub-Gaussian rewards have means μ_i(t)∈[0, 1] that are nondecreasing and discretely concave in t? Only the selected arm is observed and every arm evolves each round. Close the Ω(T^(3/5)) versus Õ(T^(7/11)) gap; the source conjectures the lower exponent is attainable.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: Intermediate error growth under selectively revealed labels
author: Zachary Chase; Idan Mehalel
source_title: Deterministic Apple Tasting
text: Does a fixed binary class H have optimal worst-case mistake bound Θ_H(√(T log log T))? The source more broadly asks which rates between √T and √(T log T) are realizable.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: The narrow expert-count transition in deterministic feedback learning
author: Zachary Chase; Idan Mehalel
source_title: Deterministic Apple Tasting
text: For n experts with one always correct and predictions visible before acting, determine the minimax mistakes when n=T^(1/2+ε(T)) and ε(T)↓0. Known endpoints: Θ(n) below √T and Θ(√(T log n)) above T^(1/2+c), fixed c>0.

subject: Classical Statistical Machine Learning
title: State-linear burn-in with a known long-run bias span
